rows.title: Atmospheric disturbances - tropical cyclones, temperate cyclones, anticyclones, thunderstorms, tornadoes
sub: Group-II S2-12: Cyclones - tropical and temperate; other atmospheric disturbances

secs.t: Tropical cyclones — meaning, formation conditions, limits of occurrence

x: Tropical cyclones require a large warm ocean surface, generally with sea-surface temperature above about 26.5–27°C. Moisture and low wind shear are also favourable conditions.
Tropical cyclones do not normally form in the
South Atlantic and south-east Pacific
, where cool waters and strong vertical wind shear are unfavourable.
Tropical cyclones form only over
warm oceans
(SST above about 26.5 °C over a large area) and draw their energy from them (APPSC-GS 2025).

secs.t: Cyclone and anticyclone structure — parts → feature; rotation and steering

x: The strongest winds and heaviest rain are in the eyewall, the ring of towering cumulonimbus around the calm eye.
Because of Coriolis deflection, tropical cyclones rotate anticlockwise in the Northern Hemisphere and clockwise in the Southern Hemisphere.
Sinking and diverging air in a high-pressure system generally produces clear, dry, calm and settled weather.

secs.t: Cyclone intensity — IMD category → wind; scales → what they measure

x: The (Enhanced) Fujita scale rates tornadoes EF0–EF5 by the damage caused; Saffir-Simpson rates hurricanes by sustained wind.
Depression corresponds to 31–49 km/h, Deep Depression to 50–61 km/h, Very Severe Cyclonic Storm to 118–166 km/h and Extremely Severe Cyclonic Storm to 167–221 km/h.
Both statements are correct: the Saffir-Simpson scale rates hurricanes (categories 1-5 by sustained wind; PYQ 2025), and storm surge is the biggest killer.

secs.t: Regional names → region; tornadoes and waterspouts

x: Tornadoes are small, funnel-shaped and usually short-lived, while hurricanes may be hundreds of kilometres wide, last for days and form over warm oceans.
Baguio is a regional name used in the Philippines; the North Indian Ocean and South Pacific use the term cyclone.
Tornadoes are small, violent funnels generally associated with land, while hurricanes, typhoons and cyclones form over oceans.

secs.t: Temperate (extra-tropical) vs tropical cyclones — features

x: Temperate or extra-tropical cyclones develop
along the polar front in the middle and higher latitudes
Temperate cyclones possess a clear frontal system, including warm and cold fronts; an occluded front may also develop.
Western disturbances
bring winter rainfall of about 10–15 cm to north-western India, which is beneficial for rabi cultivation.

secs.t: Thunderstorms and local storms → season and region; lightning alerts

x: Kaal Baisakhi or Nor'westers occur in
Bihar, Odisha, West Bengal and Assam
and approach from the north-west.
A cloudburst refers to roughly 100 mm of rainfall in an hour over 20–30 square kilometres, commonly affecting the Himalaya during June–August.
Damini App gives
lightning
alerts in 15 languages, backed by a network of 104 lightning detection locations.

secs.t: Cyclone naming bodies and IMD warning colour codes

x: The Indian cyclone warning colour codes are green—no warning, yellow—be aware, orange—be prepared and red—
take action

Cyclones are named worldwide by 6 Regional Specialised Meteorological Centres (RSMCs) and 5 Tropical Cyclone Warning Centres (TCWCs); IMD functions as RSMC New Delhi. '5 and 6' reverses the numbers, 13 is the number of WMO/ESCAP panel members, and '4 and 3' is wrong.

secs.t: North Indian Ocean cyclones — Bay of Bengal vs Arabian Sea, season, India's exposure data

x: Arabian Sea cyclones are fewer, but they are becoming more intense (Tauktae, Biparjoy).
The cited significance figures are approximately 8,000 km of coastline and nearly 5,900 km directly exposed to cyclones.
INCOIS (Hyderabad) found only 15 post-monsoon Bay of Bengal cyclones in 9 El Nino years against 33 in 11 La Nina years, so
El Nino may reduce them

secs.t: Recent cyclones → year, basin and coast hit

x: Michaung (2023, Bay of Bengal) caused Chennai floods and hit the AP coast; Gujarat's offshore infrastructure was hit by Tauktae (2021, Arabian Sea).
Idai affected Mozambique in 2019; Shakti was an Arabian Sea cyclone named by Sri Lanka in 2025; and Ditwah was linked with Operation Sagar Bandhu in November 2025.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The low over the Andaman Sea around 19–21 September 2026 was expected to become the first cyclone of that South-West monsoon season and head towards the Odisha coast.
Hudhud, Titli, Michaung and Montha
are the cyclones cited in relation to Andhra Pradesh's mainly October–December impacts.
RTGS
AWARE 2.0
auto-triggered evacuations using 423 drones and sent alerts to 3.60 crore people, keeping deaths to only 15.

rows.title: Elements and factors of climate; world climatic classification (Koeppen)
sub: Group-II S2-13: World climatic types and elements and factors of climate

secs.t: Climate — elements, definitions and terms

x: A climograph combines monthly temperature, shown by a line, and rainfall, shown by bars, and is used to interpret the climate type of a station.
The tree line is the altitude or latitude beyond which
trees cannot grow
; alpine tundra lies above it.
Anthropogenic biomes are ecological units shaped by sustained human use and include croplands, villages and cities.

secs.t: Controls of climate → how each operates, Indian examples

x: Exam angle: "Distance from river" is
not
a control of climate.
The sea moderates temperatures near the coast, whereas inland areas tend to experience greater temperature extremes and a continental climate.
Relief causes windward rainfall and leeward rain-shadow conditions, while the Himalayas moderate winter temperatures in northern India.
Cold currents cool and dry adjacent coasts, particularly on the western margins of tropical continents.
Monsoons, westerlies, western disturbances and cyclones
are atmospheric circulation features associated with winds and pressure systems.

secs.t: Classifications → scholars, basis and codes (Koeppen, Thornthwaite) — Scholar → basis

x: Wladimir Koeppen
proposed an empirical climatic classification based on mean temperature and precipitation, with climate types linked to natural vegetation.
H denotes a highland climate in which low temperatures are controlled mainly by altitude.
A warmest-month temperature below 10°C is a defining descriptive feature of the
tundra climate
Thornthwaite’s scheme is based on precipitation effectiveness and thermal efficiency, including potential evapotranspiration.

secs.t: Classifications → scholars, basis and codes (Koeppen, Thornthwaite) — Koeppen codes → regions of India

x: Exam angle: match-the-following of code, name and area (APPSC-G1 2024: Amw-west coast, As-Coromandel, Cwg-Ganga plain, BShw-NW India).
Amw occurs on the west coast south of Goa, As on the Coromandel coast, BWhw in extreme western Rajasthan and Dfc in Arunachal Pradesh.
As in APPSC-G1 2024: Amw is the west coast south of Goa, As the Coromandel coast (dry summer, winter rain), Cwg the Ganga plain (monsoon with dry winter) and BShw north-west India.

secs.t: World climatic regions → location, climate and vegetation — Climatic regions

x: The
equatorial
region, including the Amazon, Congo and Indonesia, has dense evergreen hardwood forests and almost daily rainfall.
Tropical monsoon forests in India and South-East Asia include
teak and sal
; the trees shed their leaves during the dry season.
Taiga or boreal forests of northern North America and Eurasia are dominated by
evergreen conifers such as spruce, fir and pine
Tropical rainforests occur in the equatorial belt, receive about 50–260 inches of rain, and have dense canopies, epiphytes and lianas.
Tundra occurs mainly along Arctic coasts and above the tree line in high mountains, not in central tropical Brazil or the Congo Basin.

secs.t: World climatic regions → location, climate and vegetation — Hot deserts

x: Taiga is the largest land biome, has a wide seasonal temperature range and moderate precipitation, but it has the lowest productivity of all forests.
Subtropical high pressure suppresses rainfall, offshore trade winds reduce moisture supply, and cold currents further stabilise and dry the air.
In winter, the seasonal shift of pressure belts allows westerly depressions to bring cyclonic rainfall to Mediterranean regions.

secs.t: World climatic regions → location, climate and vegetation — Mediterranean regions → towns

x: Hot deserts
western margins;
Mediterranean
western margins;
China type
= east margin.

secs.t: Grasslands → continent / country

x: Exam angle: "Prairies are found in" - USA
and
Canada (not USA alone, not Mexico).
Llanos
is a tropical grassland of the Orinoco basin, whereas Pampas, Steppes and Veld are temperate grasslands.
Temperate grasslands have hot summers, chilly winters, annual rainfall of about 25–50 cm, and grasses with few trees.
Savanna vegetation includes tall grasses such as elephant and guinea grass, along with baobab and acacia; it is naturally prone to fire.

secs.t: Climatic extremes — highest, lowest, wettest, driest (world and India)

x: Vostok in Antarctica recorded the lowest known temperature, about −89.2°C. Oymyakon and Verkhoyansk are associated with the cold pole among inhabited places.
Mawsynram and Cherrapunji receive more than 1,100 cm of annual rainfall because moist air is funnelled and forced to rise over the terrain.
Death Valley in California holds the record of 56.7 °C (1913); the WMO rejected Al Aziziya, Libya.

secs.t: Matching → description and peoples → climate type

x: Hot wet summers and long dry winters are characteristic of savanna or monsoon climatic conditions.
Extreme heat, a large diurnal temperature range and rainfall below 25 cm indicate a
hot desert
climate.
The Masai are herders of the Kenya-Tanzania savanna, the Pygmies hunter-gatherers of the Congo equatorial forest, the Bushmen (San) live in the Kalahari desert, and the Inuit in the Arctic tundra.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Magnetic minerals in Bakhira Lake sediments provide an approximately 25,000-year record of Indian monsoon variability.
The projection concerns about 40 coastal districts warming by more than 1°C by 2040, while Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu are expected to receive excess southwest-monsoon rain.
Andhra Pradesh extends from 12°41′ N to 19°07′ N and is classified as Aw, representing a tropical wet and dry climate.

rows.title: Climate change - evidence, natural and anthropogenic causes, global warming, IPCC assessments, impacts

secs.t: Evidence of warming — data: warmest years, glaciers, sea level, sea ice

x: 2024 was the hottest year on record, and the period 2015–2025 contains the eleven warmest years in the record.
2024 was about 1.55°C above the pre-industrial level, 2025 about 1.43°C, and 2025 was the warmest La Niña year recorded.
Gangotri Glacier has retreated approximately
etres since 1935, with global warming identified as the cause of its melting.

secs.t: Natural causes → terms and effects (orbital, solar, volcanic)

x: Precession refers to the wobble of Earth’s axis.
The Little Ice Age is placed approximately in the period 1500–1850.
The evidence indicates no net increase, not a continuous decline, in solar output since 1978.
Volcanic activity, continental drift and ocean currents are natural climate influences.
Sulphur dioxide and ash generate cooling aerosols that reflect incoming sunlight.

secs.t: IPCC and other reports → findings — IPCC basics

x: The IPCC has 195 members and assesses available scientific literature.
Working Group I deals with the physical science basis, Working Group II with impacts, adaptation and vulnerability, and Working Group III with mitigation.

secs.t: IPCC and other reports → findings — Report → year → finding

x: The IPCC shared the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize with
Al Gore
Net zero is achieved when human-caused emissions are balanced by removals through natural sinks or technological capture, resulting in zero net addition.
The UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2025 estimates approximately
of warming under current policies.
Syukuro Manabe and Klaus Hasselmann
shared the 2021 Physics Nobel (with Giorgio Parisi) for physical modelling of Earth's climate.

secs.t: Impacts of climate change → effects

x: The uninhabited South Pacific islets
Tebua Tarawa and Abanuea
were reported to have been submerged in 1999.
The approximately 1.2°C threshold for large-scale warm-water reef collapse has already been crossed, and coral reefs require more than 15 years to recover.
Warmer and wetter conditions can expand the range of vectors and thereby increase the spread of diseases such as malaria and dengue.

secs.t: Geoengineering proposals → terms and risks

x: In this proposal, sulphur dioxide forms sulphuric-acid aerosols that reflect sunlight, imitating the cooling effect of volcanic eruptions.
Termination shock denotes rapid warming that could occur if the cooling intervention were stopped suddenly.
Cirrus cloud thinning seeks to reduce the insulating effect of high cirrus clouds and allow more outgoing heat to escape.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: COP31 is scheduled to meet in
Türkiye in November 2026
The CMIP7 scenarios drop the worst-case SSP5-8.5 pathway and place projected warming near 2.8°C by 2100.
Palnadu, Kurnool and Anantapur are identified in connection with heatwaves.
APSES 2024–25 tracks climate action under
SDG 13

rows.title: Oceans - relief of the ocean floor, continental shelf, ridges, trenches
sub: Group-II S2-14: Ocean water - temperature and salinity; relief of the ocean floor

secs.t: Oceans — size ranking, largest and smallest, data

x: Oceans cover about 70–71 per cent of Earth's surface, contain about 97 per cent of its water, and form the largest component of the hydrosphere.
About 2 per cent of Earth's water is represented as ice and about 1 per cent as usable fresh water in the stated broad division.
Groundwater far exceeds the amount of fresh water stored in lakes and rivers.

secs.t: Terms → meaning (depth mapping, zones, minor relief) — Depth mapping

x: Echo sounding measures the time taken by a sound pulse to travel to the sea floor and return; depth equals speed multiplied by half the round-trip time.
Isobaths join points of equal
depth
, especially on maps of submerged relief.
Bathymetry
is the measuring of ocean depth and the study and mapping of the sea floor (APPSC GS 2018).

secs.t: Terms → meaning (depth mapping, zones, minor relief) — Minor relief

x: An atoll is a ring- or horseshoe-shaped coral reef surrounding a central lagoon.
A submarine canyon is a deep, steep-sided valley that cuts across the continental shelf and slope, often near river mouths.
A seamount is an undersea volcanic mountain or peak that does not reach the surface; seamounts carry cobalt-rich crusts.

secs.t: Ocean bottom relief → depth and features

x: The deep sea below 200 metres is described as the
oldest and largest biome
, occupying about 90–95 per cent of Earth's habitable space.

The continental shelf is rich in fisheries and hydrocarbons; the slope has canyons and trenches; the deep-sea plain is the flattest surface; and oceanic deeps are associated with volcanoes and earthquakes.

secs.t: Continental shelf of India — places, resources and law

x: Mumbai High lies on
the wide western continental shelf
, particularly in the Gujarat-Mumbai sector.
The Constitution (Fortieth Amendment) Act, 1976 vests minerals of the continental shelf and the EEZ in the
Union
In 2025, India added about 10,000 square kilometres in the central Arabian Sea to its extended-shelf claim before the UN CLCS.

secs.t: Trenches and ridges → ocean, deepest point

x: Oceanic trenches commonly occur at subduction zones, where one plate descends beneath another.
The Telegraph Plateau lies south of Iceland in the North Atlantic and was used as a route for transatlantic cables.
The Sunda (Java) Trench is the Indian Ocean's deepest trench, the Ninety East Ridge runs along 90 degrees E, and India's claim to the Afanasy-Nikitin Seamount is contested by Sri Lanka.

secs.t: Ocean deposits → types and make-up

x: Calcareous ooze, siliceous ooze and red clay are pelagic deposits.
Calcareous ooze consists mainly of the lime shells of tiny organisms, including globigerina and pteropods.
Red clay consists of fine inorganic clay and volcanic dust.
Terrigenous deposits (gravel, sand, silt, mud from land) settle mainly on the
continental shelves and slopes
(APPSC G1 2024, statement I correct).

secs.t: Ocean temperature and salinity — distribution, factors and ranking — Temperature — horizontal distribution

x: In the tropics the western sides of oceans are warmer, but in temperate latitudes the westerlies reverse this and make the eastern sections warmer, as the
North Atlantic Drift
does off NW Europe.

The annual range of ocean temperature is smaller in the vast Pacific than in the Atlantic: a larger, more extensive body of water heats and cools more slowly, so its temperature varies less over the year.

secs.t: Ocean temperature and salinity — distribution, factors and ranking — Temperature — vertical distribution and heat

x: Tropical oceans have a warm surface layer to about 500 m (20-25 degC), a thermocline from about 500-1,000 m where temperature falls fast, and a cold deep layer near 0-4 degC.
Polar seas have only a single cold layer, in mid-latitudes the warm surface layer forms only in summer, and the tropical thermocline (about 500-1,000 m) is where temperature drops fast with depth.

secs.t: Ocean temperature and salinity — distribution, factors and ranking — Water bodies → salinity ranking

x: Exam angle: the APPSC G2 2023 key is
Lake Van > Dead Sea > Great Salt Lake
(NCERT figures).
Lake Van
in Turkey is a closed soda lake and the world's largest alkaline lake, with salinity of about 330 per mille.
Lake Van has a salinity of approximately 330 per mille, followed by the Dead Sea at about 238 per mille and the Great Salt Lake at about 220 per mille.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The
Centre for Marine Living Resources and Ecology
(CMLRE) released the first National Report on Deep-Sea and Distant-Water Fishery Resources of the EEZ.
NIOT's Nellore seafront facility tests deep-sea mining and LTTD desalination equipment, and its station has also started new deep-sea buoys.
The Deep Ocean Mission was approved in June 2021 at Rs 4,077 crore and is run by the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES).

rows.title: Physical and chemical characteristics of ocean water - temperature and salinity distribution

secs.t: Distribution of earth's water — data and ranking

x: The descending order is oceans, polar ice caps and glaciers, groundwater, and rivers and streams.
Approximately
97 percent
of the Earth's water is stored in the oceans.

secs.t: Salinity — definition, salts and factors

x: The average salinity of ocean water is about
35 per mille
, equivalent to approximately 35 grams of dissolved salts per kilogram of water.
Ocean salts are supplied by weathered materials transported by rivers and by volcanic and hydrothermal emissions from the sea floor.
By ions, chloride and sodium are the dominant constituents of seawater, followed by sulphate and magnesium.

secs.t: Seas and regions → salinity (horizontal distribution)

x: Subtropical regions generally have high evaporation and low rainfall, resulting in relatively high surface salinity.
Heavy equatorial rainfall lowers salinity near the equator, while melting ice and low evaporation lower salinity near the poles.
The Arabian Sea is saltier than the Bay of Bengal, where the discharge of the Ganga and Brahmaputra supplies substantial fresh water.

secs.t: Density and clines → terms

x: The Black Sea is a meromictic basin in which upper and lower layers rarely mix, and chemical differences such as oxygen and hydrogen sulphide are important.
Temperature, salinity and pressure influence density, and density differences cause sinking and rising movements of water.
Cold polar water is denser and sinks; the resulting density-driven movement contributes to ocean currents and carries water towards the equator.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Sharks carrying CTD tags are being tested as mobile ocean-data collectors to support hurricane forecasts.
The OMNI deep-sea buoys record temperature, salinity and ocean currents in real time for cyclone and Indian Ocean Dipole forecasting.
Ocean uptake of excess heat and carbon dioxide produces warming effects and contributes to declining pH, with ocean pH around 8.1.

rows.title: Ocean movements - waves, tides (types and causes), ocean currents of the world
sub: Group-II S2-15: Ocean movements - tides, waves and currents; El Nino and La Nina

secs.t: Waves → terms and meaning

x: Swells are long-period waves generated by storms far from the place where they are observed.
Kallakkadal is a swell surge produced by long-period swells generated by storms in the southern Indian Ocean.
Tsunami is a Japanese term meaning '
harbour wave
A rip current is a narrow and fast-moving channel of water flowing away from the shore.

secs.t: Tides — causes, types and timing

x: Storm surges are caused by winds and pressure changes; they are weather-driven and irregular, unlike tides.
Semi-diurnal tides have two highs and two lows; diurnal tides have one high and one low; mixed tides are unequal in height; spring tides have the highest range.
Perigean tides occur when the Moon is
closest to the Earth
, thereby increasing its gravitational tidal influence.

secs.t: Tidal range places and tidal energy

x: The
Gulf of Khambhat
has a tidal range of about 5–10 metres and an estimated tidal-energy potential of approximately 7,000 MW.
At Chandipur,
the sea recedes several kilometres from the shoreline
at low tide.
Tidal energy is harnessed through tidal-range systems, such as barrages across estuaries, and tidal-stream systems using underwater turbines.

secs.t: Ocean currents — definition, drivers and gyres — Definition and drivers

x: Solar heating, wind, gravity, the Coriolis force and density differences all influence ocean currents.
Trade winds
push surface water westward and drive the equatorial currents.
Solar heating expands equatorial water and creates a slight surface slope.
Warm currents generally move poleward from the equator, while cold currents carry polar water equatorward.

secs.t: Ocean currents — definition, drivers and gyres — Gyres

x: Gyres are large circular systems formed by winds, Coriolis force and land barriers.
Major gyres generally flow
anticlockwise
in the Southern Hemisphere and clockwise in the Northern Hemisphere.
The Sargasso Sea is bounded by the
North Atlantic Drift
in the north, the Gulf Stream in the west, the Canary Current in the east and the North Equatorial Current in the south.

secs.t: Ocean currents of the world → warm or cold, ocean

x: Exam angle: "which is not a warm/cold current", "which does not flow in the N. Atlantic", current-ocean matching.
The Benguela Current is a cold South Atlantic current flowing along south-western Africa, particularly Namibia.
The Agulhas and Brazil currents are warm currents, whereas the Humboldt or Peruvian Current is a cold current.
Humboldt (South Pacific, Peru-Chile) and Benguela (South Atlantic, Namibia) are both cold currents.

secs.t: Indian Ocean currents — seasonal reversal, WICC, South Indian Ocean gyre

x: The North Indian Ocean is unique among the major oceans in having currents that reverse seasonally with the monsoon winds.
In winter, during the northeast monsoon, North Indian Ocean circulation becomes anticlockwise and the northeast monsoon current flows westward.
The WICC flows northward, or poleward, during November–February and turns southward during the southwest monsoon.

secs.t: Effects of currents → places (climate, deserts, fishing grounds, fog)

x: The Atacama is associated with the Humboldt Current, Namib and Kalahari with the Benguela Current, Sonoran with the California Current, and Peru's fishery with Humboldt-related upwelling.
The
North Atlantic Drift
, an extension of the Gulf Stream, carries warm water towards north-western Europe and helps keep its coasts mild and ports ice-free in winter.

secs.t: ENSO — terms, persons and indices — El Nino and La Nina

x: El Nino recurs about every 3-7 years.
El Nino means '
the Christ child
', a name historically associated with the timing of the warm current along the Peru coast.
Trade winds are stronger than usual during La Nina.
Weaker easterlies allow warm western-Pacific water to slide eastward.

secs.t: ENSO — terms, persons and indices — Definitions and data

x: Exam angle: "El Nino and La Nina are storms" is the false statement. They are climate patterns.
El Nino and La Nina describe the oceanic component of ENSO, while the Southern Oscillation describes its atmospheric pressure component.
A sustained negative SOI indicates El Nino; a positive SOI indicates La Nina.

secs.t: Institutions → role in coastal hazard forecasting

x: INCOIS provides ocean forecasts and PFZ advisories, IMD issues cyclone and multi-hazard warnings, NIOT operates OMNI buoys, and ITEWS serves as the regional tsunami provider.
NIOT's OMNI buoys measure ocean
temperature, salinity and currents
in real time.
ISRO
sanctioned the project using AI and satellite tools for rip-current detection and beach safety.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: INCOIS installed a second Coastal Flood Monitoring System at Kollam harbour for Kallakkadal forecasts.
The satellite tracked an eastward Kelvin wave, meaning warm water moving east along the equatorial Pacific, an early El Nino signal.
The IMD warned that a developing super El Nino could weaken the 2026 South-West Monsoon.
RTGS Vijayawada relays satellite-based cyclone, high-wave and fish-shoal alerts to fishermen.

rows.title: Ocean-atmosphere interaction - El Nino, La Nina, ENSO, Indian Ocean Dipole, Walker circulation

secs.t: El Nino — definition, types and terms

x: The stated IMD criterion is a warming of at least 0.5°C above average for five consecutive overlapping three-month periods in the central equatorial Pacific.
El Nino Modoki has central Pacific warming flanked by cooler waters on both the eastern and western sides, forming a tripole pattern.
The Japanese term Modoki means ‘
similar but different
’, reflecting its resemblance to but distinction from normal El Nino.

secs.t: El Nino and La Nina → impacts and contrast

x: Exam angle: El Nino is a climate pattern,
not a storm
; statement sets on Peru warm current, 3-7-year recurrence and meaning of the name.
During El Nino the upwelling of cold nutrient-rich water off Peru stops, which is why phytoplankton fall and fisheries collapse.
La Nina is the cold phase of ENSO; stronger trade winds push warm water westward and enhance cold upwelling in the eastern Pacific.

secs.t: Walker circulation and ENSO monitoring

x: Normal Walker circulation has rising air over the warm western Pacific and Indonesia, sinking air over the cool eastern Pacific, and easterly trade winds at the surface.
El Nino weakens the Walker circulation and shifts it eastward, reducing convection over India.
NASA's Sentinel-6 Michael Freilich
tracks Kelvin waves, which can provide an early signal of El Nino development.

secs.t: IOD and MJO — discoverers; IOD phases and monsoon link

x: The IOD is measured by the Dipole Mode Index (DMI); the SOI (Tahiti minus Darwin) measures the Southern Oscillation.
The IOD can develop independently of ENSO; a positive IOD may offset the effects of El Nino, as observed in 1997.
The strong positive IOD in 1997 helped save India from drought even though a Super El Nino was present.

secs.t: Madden-Julian Oscillation → features and monsoon effect

x: The MJO convection rises up to 10 km, weakens in the eastern Pacific while continuing aloft around the globe, and shifts the heavy-rain zone eastward.
By shifting the zone of heavy rain eastward, the MJO contributes to
active and break spells of the monsoon

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The IMD forecast projected a below-normal monsoon at 92% of the Long Period Average, whose reference value was stated as 87 cm.
The study indicated that El Nino may reduce the number of post-monsoon Bay of Bengal cyclones.
Walker first described the Southern Oscillation in the 1920s, the Indian Ocean Dipole was identified in 1999, and the last El Nino mentioned was in 2023–24.

rows.title: Biological characteristics of oceans - marine ecosystems, coral reefs, bleaching, upwelling zones

secs.t: Marine ecosystems and ocean zones → terms

x: Hydrothermal vent
s are marine ecosystems that support chemosynthetic life, unlike rivers and freshwater lakes.
Estuaries, salt marshes, mangroves and kelp forests are all marine or coastal marine ecosystems.
The neritic zone extends from the high-water line across the continental shelf to about
200 metres depth
The
epipelagic (sunlit) zone
holds the highest percentage of marine habitats and life, because light there allows photosynthesis.

secs.t: Plankton and upwelling zones → places

x: Coastal upwelling occurs when winds drive surface water away from the coast, allowing cold, nutrient-rich subsurface water to rise.
Peru–Chile is associated with the Humboldt Current, California with the California Current, Namibia with the Benguela Current, and Somalia with the Findlater Current and southwest monsoon.
El Niño suppresses the Peru upwelling system, reducing phytoplankton abundance and thereby contributing to fishery collapse.

secs.t: Coral reefs — composition, conditions, types and features

x: Exam angle: APPSC 2024 paired "rainforests of the sea" with "breaks wave power" - both true but the second does not explain the first.
A fringing reef grows close to the shore, a barrier reef is separated from the coast by a lagoon, and an atoll encloses a central lagoon.
Coral reefs cover less than one per cent of the ocean floor but support more than 25 per cent of all marine species, giving them exceptionally high species richness.

secs.t: Coral reef places → India and world, FIRSTs and largest

x: The Great Barrier Reef lies off north-eastern Australia, is about 2,300 km long, includes approximately 3,000 reefs and 900 islands, and became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1981.
Indian reef regions include the Gulf of Mannar, Gulf of Kutch, Andaman and Nicobar, Lakshadweep and Malvan; the Andaman and Nicobar region has the highest diversity among them.

secs.t: Coral bleaching — meaning, triggers and events (data)

x: Rising sea-surface temperature and marine heatwaves
are currently the strongest global drivers of coral loss associated with bleaching.
The fourth global bleaching event began in 2023, ended around mid-2025, and was the fastest and most extensive, affecting 84 per cent of reef areas in 83 countries.
The reported Indian sites were the Gulf of Mannar, Palk Bay, Lakshadweep, Andaman and Nicobar Islands and the Gulf of Kachchh.

secs.t: Ocean acidification and algal blooms → terms and data

x: Excess nitrogen and phosphorus from farm runoff and sewage cause eutrophication, which can produce harmful algal blooms.
Red tides are toxic blooms, mostly involving dinoflagellates, that can discolour water, kill fish and contaminate shellfish.
The Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (
INCOIS
) issues alerts on algal blooms and coral bleaching.

secs.t: Marine protected areas — targets and frameworks

x: Aichi Target 11 set the goal of protecting
10 per cent
of coastal and marine areas by 2020.
The 30x30 target seeks protection of 30 per cent of land and 30 per cent of oceans by 2030.
Marine protected areas, no-fishing zones and sanctuaries reduce pressures on reefs and help them recover.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: A giant Pavona clavus (potato patch coral) colony was reported near Kadmat Island, Lakshadweep.
The NGT clearance directed the Environment Ministry to protect and regenerate coral reefs; coral loss remained a central objection to the project.
Andhra Pradesh has no true coral reefs, while its fisheries rely on Bay of Bengal plankton productivity that is threatened by marine heatwaves.

rows.title: Hydrological disasters - floods, flash floods, cloudbursts, droughts, tsunamis, storm surges
sub: Group-II S2-26: Natural hazards and disasters - classification and causes

secs.t: India's vulnerability — data: hazard shares, regions, global rank

x: About 58.6% of the landmass faces moderate-to-very-high earthquake risk, over 40 million ha (~12%) is flood-prone, and about 68% of the cultivable area is drought-vulnerable.
Approximately
of the old 7,516.6 km coastline was considered exposed to cyclones and tsunamis.
Cyclones are especially associated with the east coast, while drought is prominent in Rajasthan and the Deccan interior.

secs.t: Disaster losses and displacement — data

x: The
Internal Displacement Monitoring Centre
, headquartered in Geneva, publishes the annual Global Report on Internal Displacement.
India lost approximately
of its GDP annually to natural disasters during 1990–2024.
More than 4,000 deaths were reported in India from climate-induced disasters in 2025, with the heaviest toll in
Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand

secs.t: Floods — meaning, causes, types and committees

x: Heavy rainfall, poor drainage, low infiltration, deforestation, dam failure and siltation from soil erosion are all recognised causes of floods.
Flooding in the Krishna-Godavari region can be especially severe when
Srisailam, Nagarjuna Sagar and Hirakud
release water together.
Rashtriya Barh Ayog = National Flood Commission.
Flood insurance is a non-structural measure.
The
Ministry of Water Resources
set up the Expert Committee in 2012.

secs.t: Cloudbursts, flash floods and GLOFs → places and events

x: The Nepal flash floods of 26 August 2026 are a GLOF case: glacier retreat enlarges proglacial lakes that then burst; UNDP counts 26 GLOFs in Nepal since the 1970s.
An ISRO study attributed the Dharali flash flood to the collapse of an ice patch on the
Srikanta Glacier
The HKH monsoon paradox refers to declining or erratic seasonal rainfall occurring alongside an increase in short, intense cloudbursts.

secs.t: Urban flooding → causes, cities and AP City Flood Alert

x: Urban flooding is associated with unplanned concretisation, blocked natural drains and canals, encroached lakes and extreme rainfall.
The platform was first planned for
Vijayawada
and was subsequently proposed for all Urban Local Bodies.
The platform gives 48-hour rainfall forecasts plus 6-hour flash-flood warnings, using satellite DEM and ~30 years of Budameru data.

secs.t: Droughts — types, triggers, effects and drought-prone regions

x: Hydrological drought is the fall in rivers, reservoirs and aquifers (iii); agricultural drought is a soil-moisture deficit causing crop failure (i); socio-economic drought is water/food shortage hitting livelihoods and markets (ii).
Rayalaseema faces monsoon failure, crop losses, distress migration and severe groundwater depletion, aggravated by deep borewells.
The normal SW-monsoon rainfall is
on the 1971-2020 base; meteorological drought is measured against this long-period average.

secs.t: Tsunamis — meaning, behaviour, risk zones and the 2004 event

x: Tsunamis may result from tectonic earthquakes, submarine landslides, volcanic eruptions and large asteroid or meteorite impacts.
Most tsunamis affecting India originate in the Indian Ocean, particularly from the Sunda-Andaman subduction zone; the Makran zone poses a threat to India’s west coast.

Andaman and Nicobar Islands are in the very-high-risk zone; Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Puducherry and Odisha are in the high-risk zone; Kerala, Karnataka, Goa, Maharashtra and Gujarat are in the moderate-risk zone.

secs.t: Storm surges, cyclone-prone coasts and coastline data

x: A storm surge is an abnormal rise in sea level caused mainly by cyclone winds and low atmospheric pressure.
Sea-level rise magnifies storm-surge impacts and may result in permanent inundation of low-lying land.
Mangroves and shelter belts anchor sediment and buffer storm surges, while dune stabilisation and seawalls strengthen coastal defence.
Cyclones affect 13 coastal States or Union Territories and 84 coastal districts.

secs.t: Landslides and avalanches → zones and agency

x: Landslides are mostly a hilly-terrain hazard.
Unregulated construction on unstable slopes
is one of the factors increasing landslide frequency.
The
Geological Survey of India
(GSI) is the nodal agency for landslides.

secs.t: Major disasters → year and place (India, industrial, world)

x: The correct sequence is Latur earthquake in 1993, Odisha super cyclone in 1999, Bhuj earthquake in 2001 and Indian Ocean tsunami in 2004.
The HSDPR scheme provides for setting up
two tertiary and ten secondary CBRN medical management centres
during 2021–26.
The NIDM Southern Campus at Kondapalli, Andhra Pradesh, prepares safety audits for chemical corridors and port clusters.
Nuclear hazards arise from plant accidents and from
improper disposal of radioactive waste

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Floods, droughts and cloudbursts are identified as hydro-meteorological hazards, while tsunamis are classified as geological hazards.
NIOT Nellore’s OMNI buoys provide inputs to the tsunami warning system.
India ranked second in the World Risk Index 2025, with floods and storms dominating its risk profile, while China and Indonesia have higher seismic risk.

rows.title: Disaster management framework - hazard vs disaster, DM Act 2005, NDMA, early warning systems
sub: Group-II S2-27: Disaster management - DM Act 2005, NDMA, NDRF, mitigation and preparedness

secs.t: Terms → meaning (hazard, vulnerability, disaster, risk) and hazard types

x: A
hazard
is a potentially damaging event.
Risk increases with hazard, exposure and vulnerability, while stronger
coping capacity
reduces it.
Kutcha housing, weak health infrastructure and weak early warning increase vulnerability.
Section 2(d) focuses on a catastrophe causing substantial loss that exceeds the coping capacity of the
affected community
The relationship is expressed as Hazard × Vulnerability = Disaster.

secs.t: Evolution of DM in India → year, milestone and FIRSTs

x: The sequence is NCDM in 1995, the Disaster Management Act in 2005, NDRF in 2006 and the Indian Tsunami Early Warning Centre in 2007.
In the 1990s, a Disaster Management Cell was established under the
Ministry of Agriculture
in response to the UN International Decade for Natural Disaster Reduction.
The 2009 policy emphasised prevention, mitigation, community participation and mainstreaming disaster risk reduction.
The NDMP 2016 provided short-term, medium-term and long-term time frames of five, ten and fifteen years respectively.

secs.t: DM Act 2005 → bodies, sections and heads — Background and objective

x: The
Ministry of Home Affairs
is the nodal ministry for overall coordination of disaster management in India.
The Act promoted a proactive approach centred on
prevention, mitigation and preparedness
instead of only relief after a disaster.

secs.t: DM Act 2005 → bodies, sections and heads — Bodies and key sections

x: NIDM is responsible for
training, research and capacity building in disaster management
The NDRF was raised in 2006 and operates under the superintendence of the NDMA.
NPDRR is a multi-stakeholder platform and is headed by the Union Home Minister.
NDMA is headed by the Prime Minister, NEC by the Union Home Secretary, SDMA by the Chief Minister, and DDMA by the District Collector with an elected local representative as co-chairperson.

secs.t: DM Act 2005 → bodies, sections and heads — NDRF — the specialist response force

x: NDRF is a specialist force drawn from central paramilitary forces, with search-and-rescue teams, engineers and dog squads, functioning under the superintendence of NDMA.
SDRFs have not yet been established in all states, increasing pressure on the NDRF when several disasters occur simultaneously.
The suggested measures are mandatory SDRFs and joint NDRF–SDRF training.

secs.t: Disaster funds and notified disasters → sections

x: The NDRF is a Central fund used to supplement or top up the State Disaster Response Fund during severe calamities.
The SDRF is associated with Section 48, serves as the first relief fund for notified disasters, and has a 75:25 Centre-State contribution ratio for general States.
The National and State Disaster Mitigation Funds are intended for long-term risk reduction and mitigation rather than immediate relief alone.

secs.t: DM plans and the DM (Amendment) Act 2025 → provisions

x: Hazard-specific plans are associated with Section 35 and Ministry Disaster Management Plans with Section 37.
The 2025 amendment provides for Urban Disaster Management Authorities in
every Municipal Corporation city except Delhi and Chandigarh
The 2025 amendment makes the
Municipal Commissioner
the head of the UDMA.

secs.t: Disaster management cycle and IMD colour code

x: Mock drills, stockpiles and early warning through CAP-SACHET are all preparedness measures undertaken before a disaster.
Green means all well, yellow means be aware, orange means
be prepared
and red means take action.
Mitigation includes embankments, mangroves and zoning; preparedness includes plans, warnings and drills; response includes rescue and relief; recovery includes restoration and rebuilding.

secs.t: Safety drills, awareness and community-based DRR

x: Mock drills, Aapda Mitra volunteers and tsunami escape-route signage are preparedness tools; entering flowing floodwater is unsafe and is not a preparedness measure.

Tsunami Ready recognition uses 12 indicators, is renewable every 4 years, and India targets 100 villages (verified by the National Tsunami Ready Recognition Board under MoES, chaired by the Director, INCOIS).

secs.t: Early warning systems → agency and location

x: The
India Meteorological Department
, under the Ministry of Earth Sciences, issues warnings for cyclones, heavy rain, heat and lightning.
The
Geological Survey of India
is the nodal agency for landslide hazard zonation, susceptibility mapping and the Landslide Atlas.
MHEW-DSS was developed by IMD in 2024 under Mission Mausam; it is a webGIS multi-hazard warning platform with reach of about 80 per cent of the population.

secs.t: Technology in DM → tools and terms

x: Google Earth Engine is a cloud platform that processes extensive satellite-image archives and can support rapid flood mapping.
CAP is used to integrate and disseminate public warnings through compatible alerting systems.
GIS stores and overlays spatial data, analysing flood patterns and topography for hazard mapping and proactive action.
NDEM is maintained by
ISRO
, which also runs the Disaster Management Support Programme.

secs.t: APSDMA — structure, functions and AP cyclones

x: APSDMA runs the State Emergency Operations Centre, coordinates districts, operates early warnings and undertakes pre-disaster planning and post-disaster restoration.
Cyclone risk reduction measures include IMD warnings, shelters, evacuation, shelter belts and mangrove protection or restoration.
APSDMA is the apex statutory State body for disaster-management policy and plans and is responsible for the State Emergency Operations Centre and early warning functions.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: 12 to 14 categories.
The India Disaster Resource Network inventory is described as outdated.
A proposal has been made for
an annual NDMA State Disaster Vulnerability Index
Andhra Pradesh is associated with 13–14 Bay of Bengal low-pressure systems annually, mostly from the northern Bay, which can flood the Godavari and Krishna basins.

rows.title: Marine resources - fisheries, minerals, polymetallic nodules, EEZ, blue economy

secs.t: UNCLOS maritime zones, EEZ and Acts

x: The territorial sea (12 nm) gives full sovereignty subject to innocent passage; the contiguous zone (24 nm) lets the state enforce customs, fiscal, immigration and sanitary laws; and the high seas carry freedom of navigation, overflight and research.
India's EEZ is about 2.37 million sq km (~24 lakh sq km), the world's 18th largest, much of it added by the Andaman-Nicobar and Lakshadweep islands.

secs.t: Seabed minerals and India's ISA contracts

x: The Central Indian Ocean Basin nodule contract dates to 2002, the Central and South West Indian Ridge sulphide contract to 2016, and the Carlsberg Ridge sulphide contract to 15 September 2025.
Gas-hydrate exploration under the National Gas Hydrate Programme covers the Krishna-Godavari basin, the Mahanadi region and the Andaman region.

secs.t: Deep Ocean Mission — components and Samudrayaan

x: The Deep Ocean Mission was approved in June 2021 with an outlay of
₹4,077 crore over five years
Matsya 6000 is an indigenous submersible designed to carry three crew members to a depth of 6,000 metres in the Central Indian Ocean.
The Nellore seafront facility tests nodule-mining crawlers, riser pipes, slurry pumps, LTTD desalination and wave-energy units.

secs.t: Offshore minerals and hydrocarbons → Act, blocks and places

x: Chavara is known for beach placer minerals, especially monazite and ilmenite, not as an offshore petroleum basin.
The noted beach placer locations are Chavara in Kerala, Manavalakurichi in Tamil Nadu, Chatrapur in Odisha and the Andhra Pradesh coast.
Monazite is associated with thorium, whereas ilmenite is an important titanium-bearing mineral found in beach placers.

secs.t: World fisheries → fishing grounds, conditions and nations

x: The mixing of warm and cold currents produces plankton-rich waters, which support abundant marine life and fish populations.
Norway, Japan and
Iceland
are fishing-dependent countries, but Iceland's exports lean most heavily on fish.
Japan is associated with cultured Akoya pearls, China leads by freshwater-pearl volume, India's Gulf of Mannar has pearl beds, and Pinctada radiata in the Persian Gulf has been affected by pollution.

secs.t: Indian fisheries — data, zones and schemes

x: Mechanised boats are barred in the 0–5 nautical mile inshore zone, although enforcement is weak.
A two-month, or 61-day, annual ban applies to mechanised fishing in territorial waters.
PMMSY (2020) is under the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying; the Ministry of Earth Sciences runs the Deep Ocean Mission.

secs.t: Blue economy — terms, sectors and SAGAR

x: The blue economy involves sustainable use of ocean, coastal and inland waters to promote economic growth, employment and conservation.
The Draft Blue Economy Policy Framework, 2021, is associated with the
Ministry of Earth Sciences
SAGAR means “
Security and Growth for All in the Region
.” It was articulated as India's Indian Ocean vision in 2015 at Mauritius.

secs.t: Marine resources of Andhra Pradesh → data and places

x: The State contributes about 30% of national fish production, 31% of shrimp exports and recorded 41.38 LMT output in 2024–25.
The 10 fishing harbours are being constructed under PMMSY, not Sagarmala.
The Krishna-Godavari basin has offshore oil and gas, the northern coast has beach sand minerals, and NIOT Nellore and CMFRI centres support marine research.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Supreme Court directed Tamil Nadu to frame a “specified channel” through territorial waters so that purse-seine vessels can reach the EEZ.
The Centre of Excellence on Blue Economy is located at Vignan's University, Vadlamudi, in Guntur.
The stated criticism is that degradation of inshore areas pushes fishers offshore, while the FAO has described the increase from deep-sea resources as only marginal.

rows.title: Continental resources - land, forest, water, mineral and energy resources; conservation
sub: Group-II S2-29: Natural resources of India - land, water and forest resources and their distribution

secs.t: Resources — types, depletion and global milestones

x: Forest
s, animals, plants and micro-organisms are biotic resources because they originate from living organisms.
Fossil fuels are non-renewable and forests and fish are renewable.
Stock refers to resources that exist but cannot presently be used because suitable technology is unavailable.
Deep bore tubewells for irrigation contribute to groundwater depletion, brick production removes topsoil, and agricultural expansion causes loss of biodiversity habitats.

secs.t: Terms → meaning: land, forest and water

x: The nine-fold classification includes forests, non-agricultural uses, barren and unculturable land, permanent pastures, miscellaneous tree crops, culturable wasteland, current fallow, other fallow and net sown area.
Indian Remote Sensing (
IRS
) data are used for wasteland mapping and National Wastelands Monitoring.
Soil erosion, waterlogging, salinisation, nutrient depletion, falling water tables and soil pollution are causes of land degradation.
Silviculture is the science and practice of
raising and tending forest trees
, including regeneration, thinning and rotation.

secs.t: FIRSTs and superlatives — land, forest, water, minerals

x: India is the world’s largest groundwater user and accounts for approximately
one-quarter
of global groundwater extraction.
Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan and Delhi
are identified as the regions worst affected by groundwater over-exploitation.
India signed the first ISA contract for exploration of polymetallic sulphides on the
Carlsberg Ridge in the Arabian Sea

secs.t: Resource regions → resource (subcontinent and world)

x: The Peninsular plateau is the mineral heartland; the Himalaya and NE hills have forests, hydropower and jhum lands; the Indo-Gangetic plains have alluvium and groundwater; and the Thar/north-west has scarce water and traditional harvesting.
Katanga is noted for copper and cobalt; Minas Gerais for iron ore, gold and diamonds; the Mesabi Range for iron ore; and Witwatersrand for gold.

secs.t: Critical minerals, deep-sea deposits and gemstones

x: The deposits are rich in
copper, zinc, lead, iron, silver and gold
; manganese, cobalt, nickel and copper characterise polymetallic nodules.
Ruby and sapphire are varieties of corundum, while emerald is beryl.
The Lithium Triangle comprises
Chile, Argentina and Bolivia
US Project Vault is described as a
$12 billion mineral stockpile

secs.t: Traditional water harvesting systems → region

x: Exam angle: APPSC asked Eri (2024), Ahar-pyne (2024) and Zabo (2024) directly.
Ahar-pyne is practised in
South Bihar
; the ahar is a catchment basin and the pyne is a channel.
Kuhl consists of diversion channels in Himachal Pradesh and Jammu, Katta consists of temporary check dams in Karnataka, and Bawari or Baoli means stepwells in Rajasthan and Delhi.

secs.t: Dams and projects → river → state; Interlinking of Rivers

x: The Ramganga Project, including the Kalagarh dam, is in Uttarakhand and irrigates areas of
Uttar Pradesh
The National Perspective Plan contains 30 links, comprising 14 Himalayan and 16 Peninsular links.
The
National Water Development Agency
runs the National Perspective Plan for interlinking of rivers.
Ken-Betwa
is the flagship ILR link implemented under the NWDA's National Perspective Plan.

secs.t: Data — water availability, demand and scheme outcomes

x: Per-capita water availability declined from more than 5,000 m³ at Independence to about 1,400 m³ at present.
The stated figures are 27 million farmers benefited and 24.61 million hectares of irrigation potential created or restored.

secs.t: Institutions → role

x: Jal Shakti is the nodal ministry.
The ISA, created under UNCLOS, is based in
Jamaica

secs.t: Forest laws, policies and movements

x: The Forest Rights Act, 2006 gives
Gram Sabhas
authority over the management, protection and regeneration of community forest resources.
Chipko is a Himalayan movement.
The Arabari experiment of 1972 preceded JFM, Central guidelines were issued in 1990, and JFM was associated with the National Forest Policy, 1988.
NFP 1988 formally introduced JFM.

secs.t: Water and watershed schemes → year → provision

x: The Hariyali guidelines of 2003 provided for implementation of watershed projects through
Panchayati Raj Institutions
Under PMKSY, the
Accelerated Irrigation Benefits Programme
is intended to accelerate completion of major and medium irrigation projects.
Har Khet Ko Pani covers Command Area Development and Water Management, surface minor irrigation, repair-renovation-restoration of water bodies and groundwater development.

secs.t: Mineral Acts and amendments → year → provision

x: The 2026 amendment bars States from taxing mineral rights or mineral-bearing lands except within limits prescribed by the Centre.
The criticism refers to the 2024 nine-judge Supreme Court verdict in
Mineral Area Development Authority v. SAIL
The verdict held that royalty is not a tax and recognised State taxing powers over mineral rights under Entry 50 and mineral-bearing land under Entry 49 of the State List.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The warning at the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi concerned the weaponisation of
critical minerals
Gandikota reservoir is on the Pennar and serves drought-prone Rayalaseema as part of the Telugu Ganga system; this explains Assertion A.
River interlinking has been criticised because monsoons and climate change can make supposedly surplus basins unreliable.
Pattiseema lift water supported
the Krishna delta
during the El Niño-related deficit.

units.title: Physical Geography of the World, India and Andhra Pradesh - Physical Divisions, Earthquakes, Landslides, Drainage, Climate and Monsoon, Vegetation, Parks and Sanctuaries, Soils, Rocks and Minerals

rows.title: World - continents, major mountain systems, plateaus, plains and deserts

secs.t: Definitions, types and superlatives

x: The Himalayas and Atlas are young Alpine fold mountains, while the Appalachians and Urals are old mountain ranges.
A steep hill above about 600 metres is generally termed a
mountain
in the stated geomorphological classification.
World plains generally lie below 200 metres, are commonly formed by rivers and support dense populations because of their level and fertile land.

secs.t: Countries → borders and coasts

x: Bolivia and Paraguay
are the landlocked countries identified in South America in this classification.
Luxembourg borders Belgium, Germany and France.
Venezuela
's coast is on the Caribbean/Atlantic side, not the Pacific.

secs.t: Mountain ranges → location

x: The Urals are old fold mountains, the Alps are young fold mountains, and the Andes run along the Pacific side of South America.
The
Atlas
Mountains of Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia separate the Mediterranean and Atlantic coastal areas from the Sahara.
The
Andes
, running along the Pacific side of South America, are the longest continental range.

secs.t: Highest peak of each continent → country; Seven Summits climbers

x: Aconcagua is the highest peak in South America and the
tallest mountain outside Asia
, at 6,961 metres.
Denali, Kilimanjaro, Elbrus and Vinson Massif are respectively the highest peaks of North America, Africa, Europe and Antarctica.
The Bass list uses Kosciuszko in Australia, whereas the Messner list uses Puncak Jaya in Indonesia for Australia/Oceania.

secs.t: Plateaus and plains → type and location

x: The
Deccan Plateau
is a lava or continental plateau and is regarded as one of the oldest plateaus.
The Tibetan Plateau is the highest major plateau; Colorado is cut by the Grand Canyon; the Bolivian Altiplano lies within the Andes; and the Mongolian Plateau is in Central Asia.
The Anatolian Plateau lies in Turkiye between the Pontic and Taurus mountain ranges.

secs.t: Deserts → countries and type; aeolian landforms

x: The Kalahari extends across Botswana, Namibia and South Africa.
The Atacama lies in Chile and is a very dry coastal desert associated with a cold current.
The Sahara is the largest hot desert, the Namib is among the oldest, Great Victoria is Australia's largest desert, and the Thar lies in India and Pakistan.

secs.t: Regional physiographic names → country/continent

x: The Terai is a marshy zone south of the Bhabar, occurring in Nepal and along India's Himalayan foothills.

St Marys River connects Superior and Huron, the Straits of Mackinac connects Michigan and Huron, and the Detroit River connects Huron and Erie.

secs.t: Himalayas — dimensions, origin, structure and classification counts

x: The Himalayan arc extends for approximately
from Nanga Parbat in the west to Namcha Barwa in the east.
The Himadri has asymmetrical folds; the Himalayan slope towards the plains is steeper, while the Tibetan side is gentler.
The three principal longitudinal parallel ranges are Himadri or Greater Himalaya, Himachal or Lesser Himalaya and Shiwalik or Outer Himalaya.

secs.t: Ranges north to south → features

x: Karakoram and Zaskar are Trans-Himalayan ranges, Ladakh continues as Kailash in Tibet, and the Kashmir Valley separates Zaskar from Pir Panjal.
From north to south, the sequence is Karakoram, Ladakh, Himadri, Himachal and Shiwalik.
Pir Panjal is a major range of the Himachal Himalaya extending for about 300 km in the Jhelum-Beas sector.

secs.t: Superlatives, FIRSTs and traps

x: The Trans-Himalaya formed before the Himalayas.
Kanchenjunga belongs to the Himadri and lies on the India-Nepal boundary.

secs.t: Regional divisions → between rivers

x: The standard Burrard boundaries are Indus–Sutlej, Sutlej–Kali, Kali–Teesta and Teesta–Dihang.
Nanga Parbat, Rakaposhi and Haramosh
are prominent peaks of the Punjab or Kashmir-Himachal Himalaya.
The Kumaon Himalaya lies between the Sutlej and Kali and includes the lakes Nainital and Bhimtal.
The Himalaya makes a knee-bend at the
Dihang gorge
near Namcha Barwa and then turns southwards as the Purvanchal hills.

secs.t: Peaks → range, division, country

x: Kamet is in the Himadri, Kumaon/Garhwal, Uttarakhand.
Godwin Austen or K2 is 8,611 metres high and belongs to the Karakoram.
Namcha Barwa marks the eastern end of the Assam Himalaya and is located in Tibet, China.

secs.t: Glaciers → range and location

x: Pindari, Milam and Kafni
glaciers are associated with the Kumaon Himalaya of Uttarakhand.
Siachen lies in the Karakoram's Nubra region and marks Ladakh's northern limit, while Baltoro, Biafo and Hispar are in the Karakoram sector of Gilgit-Baltistan.
Gangotri Glacier is located in the Greater Himalaya of Uttarakhand and is the source of the Bhagirathi at Gaumukh.

secs.t: Mountain passes and tunnels → state

x: Rohtang (Pir Panjal, HP, 3,978 m) links Kullu with Lahaul-Spiti; Lipulekh in Uttarakhand lies at the India-Nepal-China tri-junction on the Kailash-Mansarovar route; and Bomdi La in Arunachal Pradesh is on the Tawang-Lhasa route.
The Atal Tunnel runs under the Rohtang Pass (Pir Panjal, HP), and the Jawahar Tunnel is at the Banihal Pass (Jammu-Srinagar).

secs.t: Purvanchal hills → state; Molasse basin

x: Patkai Bum is in Arunachal Pradesh on the Myanmar border.
After the knee-bend near Namcha Barwa and the Dihang gorge, the Himalayas turn south as the Purvanchal hills.
The Garo-Khasi-Jaintia and Naga hills generally run east-west, joining the north-south Mizo and Rakhine hills.
The Molasse Basin is associated with Mizoram and consists of soft, unconsolidated deposits.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Himalayas define India's northern boundary, act as a climatic barrier, and Shiwalik debris contributed to the formation of the Indo-Gangetic Plain.
Nanga Parbat marks the western end of the Himalayas, while Namcha Barwa marks their eastern end.

x: 32,87,263 sq km is about 2.4% of world land.
India's mainland extends from 8°4′ N to 37°6′ N latitude and from 68°7′ E to 97°25′ E longitude.
India's mainland extends about 3,214 km from north to south and 2,933 km from east to west, entirely in the Northern Hemisphere.
About 15,200 km (15,106.7 km in some sources).

82°30' E passes through Mirzapur and near Kakinada.

Himachal

The Trans-Himalaya, situated north of the Himadri, includes the
Karakoram, Ladakh and Zaskar
ranges.
The principal structural zones are arranged from north to south as the Indus–Tsangpo Suture, Main Central Thrust, Main Boundary Thrust and Himalayan Frontal Fault.

The lagoons and backwaters of the Malabar Coast are locally called
kayals

secs.t: Northern Plains and Indian Desert — regions and features

x: Exam angle: the APPSC GS 2025 key orders desert features as arid climate → dunes → thorny bushes → seasonal streams.
The Northern Plains are aggradational plains formed mainly by alluvium deposited by the Himalayan and peninsular river systems.
The Punjab Plain was formed by the tributaries of the Indus and contains doabs.
The Molassis Basin is located in
Mizoram in the Purvachal hills
and consists of soft, unconsolidated deposits.
Luni is a seasonal river and ends in the Rann of Kutch; it does not reach the Arabian Sea as a perennial river.

secs.t: Peninsular Plateau — sub-divisions and the Deccan Traps

x: The Deccan Plateau lies south of the Narmada and is largely composed of basaltic rocks.
The Peninsular Plateau is mineral-rich, the Nilgiris mark the meeting point of the two Ghats, and the Deccan Plateau is a stable inverted triangle.
The Peninsular Plateau is the largest and oldest division, a Precambrian Gondwana shield and a triangular block of igneous and metamorphic rocks.

secs.t: Western vs Eastern Ghats; hill ranges → location

x: The Western Ghats are continuous south of the Tapti, whereas the Eastern Ghats are discontinuous and eroded.
The Western Ghats are locally known successively as Sahyadri, Nilgiri, Anaimalai, Palani and Cardamom from north to south.
Papikondalu, Nallamala, Erramala, Seshachalam and Velikonda are associated with the Eastern Ghats in Andhra Pradesh.
The Cardamom Hills continue the Western Ghats, while the Eastern Ghats consist of khondalite and charnockite and have an average height of about 610 metres.

secs.t: Peaks → state and height order

x: Anamudi is in Kerala and rises to 2,695 metres.
The correct descending order is Nanga Parbat, Kamet, Anaimudi and Doddabetta, with approximate heights of 8,126 m, 7,756 m, 2,695 m and 2,637 m respectively.
Nanga Parbat lies at the western end of the Himadri in the J&K–PoK region and is about 8,126 metres high.

Bhorghat and Thalghat
are the Sahyadri pair.

All three statements correctly describe Pal Ghat, its location between the Nilgiris and Anaimalai hills, and its approximate dimensions.
Nathu La
is in Sikkim and forms part of the India–Tibet trade route; it is also one of the highest motorable passes.

secs.t: Coastal plains → states; emergent vs submergent

x: Emergent coasts result from land rise or sea fall and are associated with wide plains, bars, lagoons and deltas.

The coastal plains were separated from Gondwana during the
Cretaceous–early Tertiary period
Faulting
contributed to the relatively straight character of the Indian coastline.

Port Blair was renamed
Sri Vijaya Puram
Minicoy is the largest and southernmost island, while the Amindivi and Cannanore groups lie north and south of 11° N respectively.

secs.t: Himalayan drainage — types, character and terms

x: Himalayan rivers receive water both from rainfall and from the melting of snow, which helps them maintain flow throughout the year.
In the plains, the gentle gradient causes Himalayan rivers to meander, shift their channels and form ox-bow lakes and floodplains.
The four broad groups are Himalayan drainage, Deccan drainage, Coastal drainage and Inland drainage of western Rajasthan.

x: The
Beas
originates near the Rohtang region, not in the Mansarovar–Kailash area.
The Indus rises at Singge Khabab in the
Kailash range near Mansarovar
The Brahmaputra rises at the
Chemayungdung Glacier
in the Kailash range, east of Lake Mansarovar.

secs.t: Indus system — course and tributaries → Greek/Vedic names

x: Ravi was known to the Greeks as Hydraotes.
The Indus flows northwest between Ladakh and Zaskar, turns south at Nanga Parbat through an antecedent gorge and meets the Arabian Sea near Karachi.

secs.t: Ganga system — course, tributaries by bank, confluence order

x: Exam angle: "south-based tributary" = Betwa/Son/Yamuna group; Burhi Dihing and Dhansiri are Brahmaputra tributaries, not the Ganga's (PYQ 2024: neither statement correct).
The Son is the second-largest right-bank tributary after the Yamuna and joins the Ganga near Maner, close to Patna.
The
Yamuna
, rising at Yamunotri and joining at Prayagraj, is the westernmost and longest tributary of the Ganga.
Below Prayagraj the order is Tons, Gomti, Ghaghara, Son, Gandak, Kosi and Mahananda.

secs.t: Brahmaputra — names by country, tributaries

x: The river, known as the Tsangpo or Yarlung Zangbo in Tibet, turns south at
Namche Barwa
Dibang and Lohit
join the Dihang near Pasighat/Sadiya, after which the combined river is called the Brahmaputra.
The Teesta is about 414 km long, rises at Tso Lhamo Lake and has the Rangeet as its largest tributary.

x: The Salal project is a 690 MW NHPC project on the
Chenab
and is identified as India’s first project in the region under the treaty.

Baglihar, Salal and Dul Hasti are projects on the
Chenab
River in Jammu and Kashmir.

Wular is located in Jammu and Kashmir and is the largest freshwater lake of India; it is not a brackish high-altitude lake of Ladakh.

Ropar

rows.title: India - Peninsular drainage: east-flowing and west-flowing rivers, river basins, watershed
sub: Group-II S2-18: India - drainage system: Himalayan and Peninsular rivers

secs.t: River types — Himalayan vs peninsular; east- vs west-flowing

x: Himalayan rivers are generally perennial and form deep antecedent gorges, while Peninsular rivers are usually seasonal and flow through broad, shallow, graded valleys.
Peninsular rivers are particularly useful for hydropower generation, while east-flowing rivers also support delta irrigation.
Antecedent rivers rise in the Trans-Himalaya and retain their courses by cutting through rising ranges.

secs.t: West-flowing and rift-valley rivers → features

x: Narmada and Tapi flow through rift valleys, but as west-flowing rivers they generally form estuaries rather than large deltas.
The
Mahi
crosses the Tropic of Cancer twice and ultimately reaches the Gulf of Khambhat.
The Aravallis give rise to west-flowing Luni and Sabarmati, east-flowing Banas and north-flowing Sahibi; Luni ends in the Rann of Kutch.

secs.t: River sources → hills and plateaus

x: Both the Narmada and Son originate at
Amarkantak in the Maikal range
of Madhya Pradesh.
The Krishna originates at Mahabaleshwar.
The Western Ghats are described as the Water Tower of Peninsular India because they provide the sources of the
Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri
river systems.
The Godavari rises in the Brahmagiri-Trimbakeshwar hills of Nashik.

secs.t: Data — river lengths and basin rankings

x: The order is Godavari (1,465 km), Krishna (about 1,400 km), Narmada (1,312 km), Mahanadi (858 km) and Tapi (724 km).
The relative order is Godavari, Krishna and Mahanadi, while the Narmada and Kaveri basins are approximately equal in size.
The Brahmaputra is about 2,900 km long overall, but only 885 km lies in India.

x: Pravara, Manjira and Manair join the Godavari from the right bank.

Sileru is a tributary of Sabari, is known as Machkund in its upper course, and joins Sabari at the AP–Chhattisgarh–Odisha tri-junction.
Vedavathi, also called Hagari, is a tributary of Tungabhadra and therefore belongs to the
Krishna
river system.
Indravati and Sabari
are both left-bank tributaries of the Godavari (APPSC GS 2025 key).

secs.t: Himalayan tributaries, prayags and doabs

x: The Raichur Doab is the land tract lying between the
Krishna and Tungabhadra
rivers.

is identified with the confluence of the Ganga and Yamuna and the traditionally associated mythical Saraswati.
Nandprayag is Alaknanda–Nandakini, Karnaprayag is Alaknanda–Pindar, Rudraprayag is Alaknanda–Mandakini and Devprayag is Alaknanda–Bhagirathi.
The Sind Sagar or Thal Doab lies between the Jhelum and the Indus rivers.

the Goa–Karnataka border
Sivasamudram, Chunchanakatte and Hogenakkal are all waterfalls associated with the Kaveri River.

Varahi
river (PYQ 2025).

Charaichung was established in 1633 by Pratap Singha and is called
Asia's first protected bird site

Ken-Betwa

Par-Tapi-Narmada concerns Gujarat and Maharashtra; Tapti Basin Mega Recharge concerns Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra; and Aghanashini-Vedavathi includes a 194-km pipeline to Vani Vilas Sagar.
The Srisailam project on the Krishna feeds the
Telugu Ganga and Veligonda
systems.

x: The Godavari is known as
Dakshin Ganga or Dakshina Ganga
Both statements are correct: Sir Arthur Cotton proposed linking rivers in the 19th century, and the National Perspective Plan (1980) is implemented via the NWDA.

secs.t: Acts, tribunals and programmes → year → provision

x: Water is placed in Entry 17 of the State List, subject to
Entry 56 of the Union List
concerning regulation and development of inter-State rivers and river valleys.
Water disputes between States are referred to tribunals under the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956, connected with Article 262 of the Constitution.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Climate change can alter rainfall and river-flow patterns, thereby weakening the assumption of permanently surplus basins used in the interlinking paradigm.
Telangana opposed the Polavaram–Nallamala Sagar link, the Cauvery basin has been projected to remain dry until 2050, and climate change challenges surplus-basin assumptions.
Under the Indus Waters Treaty, the eastern rivers Ravi, Beas and Sutlej are allocated to India, while the western rivers Indus, Jhelum and Chenab are mainly allocated to Pakistan.
The Godavari meets the sea at
Antarvedi
through seven distributaries forming the Konaseema delta.

rows.title: India - climate: mechanism of the monsoon, theories, seasons and their characteristics
sub: Group-II S2-17: India - climate and the monsoon mechanism; seasons and rainfall distribution

secs.t: Monsoon — meaning, wind type and features

x: Monsoons lie mainly within 20°N-20°S. Statement 2 is wrong: the monsoon is not steady and is unequally distributed, with breaks and variability.
'Mausim' is Arabic for
season
, reflecting the seasonal reversal of these winds.

secs.t: Theories and persons → core idea

x: The sudden onset of the south-west monsoon in the first week of June is called the
monsoon burst
Al Masudi
, a tenth-century scholar, noted the seasonal winds associated with the monsoon system.
Sir Edmund Halley's thermal theory, proposed in 1686, attributes the monsoon to differential heating of land and sea.

The northward shift of the subtropical westerly jet is associated with onset, while its return south of the Himalayas accompanies withdrawal; the tropical easterly jet extends from the South China Sea to East Africa.

secs.t: Terms → meaning

x: The Mascarene High is
a permanent high-pressure cell in the southern Indian Ocean near Madagascar
and helps drive cross-equatorial flow.
Nautapa is the traditional nine-day peak of summer heat in north India and occurs just before the arrival of the monsoon.
OMT is measured during January-March and has been identified as a better predictor of monsoon rainfall than sea-surface temperature.

secs.t: Seasons → months

x: IMD winter is January-February.
The IMD south-west monsoon season extends from
June to September
North-western and central India experience their hottest conditions from April to June, and heat waves generally peak in May-June.
The six traditional seasons are Vasanta, Grishma, Varsha, Sharad, Hemanta and Shishira.

secs.t: Local storms and winds → region

x: Exam angle:
Kaal Baisakhi
→ West Bengal.
Mango showers
Karnataka
Blossom showers aid coffee flowering in Kerala and nearby Karnataka.
The Loo is a hot, dry and dusty afternoon wind of the northern and north-western plains and is also locally experienced in Rayalaseema.
Kaal Baisakhi strikes
West Bengal
(also Odisha and Assam) in the hot season (APPSC GS 2025 key).

secs.t: SW monsoon — onset dates and the two branches

x: Exam angle: both statements are correct: "Kerala receives the SW monsoon first" and "the Bay branch soaks Meghalaya". Monsoons lie mainly within
20 deg N-20 deg S
and relief governs SW-monsoon rain.
The southwest monsoon normally reaches Bhopal around 15 June and Delhi around 25 June.
The Arabian Sea branch strikes the Western Ghats first, giving very heavy rain at Agumbe and Hulikal on the Ghats crest.
The Western Ghats force uplift on their windward side, leaving a rain-shadow region to their east.
The LPA of the south-west monsoon for 1971–2020 is
(about 87 cm).

secs.t: Rainfall extremes and rain-shadow regions → place

x: The lee of the Western Ghats includes interior Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, Rayalaseema and parts of Tamil Nadu; Ladakh lies in the rain shadow behind the Himalayas.
The leeward Deccan lies in the Western Ghats’ rain shadow, Ladakh lies behind the Great Himalaya and is a cold desert, and the Hagari valley has the lowest rainfall in Andhra Pradesh, below 51 cm.

secs.t: Retreating monsoon, NE monsoon and western disturbances → region

x: Bay of Bengal cyclones
bring bimodal rainfall to the south during the October–November retreating monsoon season.
Western disturbances are temperate cyclones originating in the Mediterranean region and reaching north-western India through Iran, Afghanistan and Pakistan.
Mediterranean western disturbances bring about 10–15 cm of rain to north-west India, benefit rabi crops and produce snowfall in Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand.

secs.t: Koeppen climatic regions → code → area

x: Exam angle: the APPSC G1 2024 matching key is short dry season → west coast; dry summer → Coromandel; dry winter → Ganga plain; steppe → NW.

As (monsoon with dry summer) is the Coromandel coast; Cwg (monsoon with dry winter) is the Ganga plain; BWhw (hot desert) is extreme western Rajasthan; Amw (short dry season) is the west coast south of Goa.

secs.t: Institutions, missions and models → year

x: MoES launched it in 2012.
SEFS was associated with 2007, the Monsoon Mission Coupled Forecasting System with 2012 and the Multi-Model Ensemble with 2021.
Mission Mausam was launched on 14 January 2025 with IMD Vision 2047.
The Bharat Forecast System provides forecasts at 6 km resolution, including 10-day rainfall forecasts.
India had 47 Doppler weather radars, compared with 14 in 2014.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The
Indian Ocean Dipole
was being monitored as a possible offset to the influence of El Nino.
The forecast was about 90% of the long-period average, and the 43% June deficit led to contingency planning.
The Sileru-Sabari valleys are the wettest parts of Andhra Pradesh, receiving about 140–152 cm, while the Hagari valley is the driest, receiving less than 51 cm.

secs.t: Terms → meaning: variability, ENSO, drought types

x: That is the stated El Niño threshold.
La Niña generally strengthens the monsoon and is associated with colder winters and more Bay of Bengal cyclones.
Meteorological drought = rain deficit.

secs.t: Regions → rainfall gradient, variability, drought and floods

x: Rainfall decreases eastward to westward across the northern plains in the sequence Kolkata, Patna, Prayagraj, Delhi and Bikaner.
The monsoon lasts less than 75 days in western Rajasthan, where it arrives late and leaves early, and more than 120 days in the south-west peninsula, where it arrives first.
Himalayan rivers swell during the monsoon, and cloudburst-induced flash floods are increasing in the Himalaya and the north-east.

secs.t: Data — IMD categories, LPA bands, deficient years, extents

x: For the all-India season, rainfall below 90 percent of the LPA is classified as
deficient
The cited deficient years are 2015, when actual rainfall was 86 percent of LPA, and 2023, associated with the 2023–24 El Niño.
About
68 percent
of India’s agricultural or cultivable land is drought-prone in varying degrees.

secs.t: Drought declaration and flood mitigation

x: The Manual for Drought Management uses
rainfall deficit, vegetation, soil moisture and water indicators
for declaring drought.
Embankments, drainage channels, sea dykes and real-time flood forecasting are recognised mitigation measures.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Meghalaya recorded the worst deficiency at 59 per cent, Manipur recorded 43 per cent deficiency, and Andhra Pradesh recorded 42 per cent deficiency, ranking third worst.
Andhra Pradesh has an average annual rainfall of about 966 mm.
The highest rainfall in Andhra Pradesh occurs in
the Sileru–Sabari valleys
, where it ranges from about 140 to 152 cm.
