secs.t: Forest types — classification and superlatives

x: The classification associated with H.G. Champion and G.S. Puri recognises
5 major types and 15 sub-types
Tropical moist deciduous forests account for about 37%, tropical dry deciduous forests about 28.6%, and tropical wet evergreen forests about 8%.

secs.t: Forest types → rainfall, region, species

x: Tropical wet evergreen forests require more than 250 cm of rainfall and occur in the Western Ghats, Assam, Meghalaya, Manipur, Tripura, Nagaland and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

Moist deciduous forests include teak, sal and mahua; dry deciduous forests include teak, sandalwood and Terminalia; thorn forests include Acacia, Ziziphus and Prosopis; tidal forests include Rhizophora and Avicennia.
Sholas are temperate forest formations of the Nilgiris, Anaimalai and Palani hills, generally occurring as stunted evergreen patches with grasslands in the Western Ghats.

secs.t: Himalayan altitudinal zones → altitude → species

x: Sub-tropical chir pine occurs around 1,000–1,800 metres.
All three statements correctly describe Himalayan vegetation zones and their characteristic species or altitude.
The sequence upward is tropical sal foothills, subtropical chir pine, temperate forests, subalpine birch-rhododendron forests and alpine meadows.
Temperate Himalayan forests include
oak, deodar, blue pine and silver fir
The southern or windward slopes generally carry denser forests than the northern slopes.

secs.t: Tree species → forest type → region

x: Jackfruit is an evergreen tree associated with the Western Ghats, not with Himalayan alpine meadows.
Sandalwood is associated with dry deciduous forests of South India.

secs.t: Mangroves and tidal forests → state/UT

x: Mangroves possess specialised stilt and knee roots, occur in intertidal deltaic areas and may be submerged during high tide.
Andhra Pradesh had 421.43 sq km of mangrove cover in ISFR 2023, showing an increase of 13.01 sq km.
Pairs 1-3 are correct: Bhitarkanika (saltwater crocodiles) is in Odisha, Pichavaram near Chidambaram in Tamil Nadu, and Coringa WLS near Kakinada in AP.

secs.t: Grasslands → region; local names

x: Sehima-Dichanthium occurs on black soils; Phragmites-Saccharum in marshy localities; Deschampsia-Deyeuxia in alpine regions; and Bothriochloa in high-rainfall paddy tracts.
Banni is a vast tropical grassland situated in the Kutch region of Gujarat.
Sabai grass is used for making rope and paper.

secs.t: Terms → meaning: forest cover classes and silviculture

x: Forest cover includes land exceeding one hectare with canopy density of 10% or more, regardless of ownership.
Coppice
regeneration arises from stool shoots after felling and is generally managed on a short rotation, particularly for fuelwood.
High forest provides a seed-raised, long-rotation timber crop, while the selection system retains an uneven-aged forest by removing mature trees singly or in groups.

secs.t: Data — ISFR 2023 figures, states and forest fires

x: ISFR 2023 reported forest cover of 7,15,343 sq km or 21.76%, tree cover of 1,12,014 sq km or 3.41%, and combined forest and tree cover of 25.17%.
Dry deciduous forest
s are especially vulnerable to fires because of their seasonal dryness and accumulation of dry biomass.
Andhra Pradesh had the largest fire-affected area in 2023–24, measuring about 5,286.76 sq km, and ranked third in large-fire events.
About
of India's forest cover is prone to frequent fires (ISFR 2015; APPSC 2025 key), and dry deciduous forests are the most vulnerable.

secs.t: Acts, policies and legal classes of forest

x: The National Forest Policy, 1988 set a target of
of the total area under forest and tree cover.
The National Forest Policy, 1988 prescribed a target of
forest and tree cover in hills and mountains.
CAMPA
manages the compensatory afforestation funds.
Mining is banned inside National Parks and Sanctuaries, and the Supreme Court has barred mining within 1 km of every such area unless a larger eco-sensitive zone is notified.

secs.t: National Parks and Tiger Reserves → state; Project Tiger

x: Keoladeo National Park is situated at Bharatpur in
Rajasthan
and is also a Ramsar site.
Madhav Tiger Reserve is situated in Shivpuri,
Madhya Pradesh
, and is the 58th tiger reserve.
Satkosia Tiger Reserve comprises
Satkosia Gorge and Baisipalli Wildlife Sanctuary
; Debrigarh is not part of its stated composition.
Amangarh
Tiger Reserve is in Uttar Pradesh and serves as the buffer of Corbett Tiger Reserve.
Guru Ghasidas–Tamor Pingla was the 56th, Ratapani the 57th in 2024, and Madhav the 58th in 2025.

secs.t: Species projects and bird sanctuaries → site

x: Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary is the second home for cheetahs and Veerangana Durgavati Tiger Reserve is the third.
The Great Indian Bustard is associated with Rajasthan and Gujarat, numbers fewer than 150, and is protected through the modified power-line directions.
The first artificial-insemination breeding of the Great Indian Bustard was conducted at
Jaisalmer

x: Andhra Pradesh forests are mainly dry deciduous, and Nallamala is the biggest forest tract in the State.
The plan proposes bringing
gaur from Central India and tigresses from Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh
to NSTR.
Andhra Pradesh has three National Parks, thirteen Wildlife Sanctuaries, one Tiger Reserve, one Biosphere Reserve and the Koundinya Elephant Reserve.
The eviction issue in Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve has raised concerns regarding
tribal rights
38,436.58 sq km = 30,084.96 sq km of forest cover + 8,351.62 sq km of scrub.

Conservation Reserves are declared by the State on government land, local rights remain unaffected, and management committees include panchayats.
The Supreme Court extended
a 10-kilometre mining buffer
to all wetland Conservation Reserves.

The stated counts are 127 Conservation Reserves, 75 Community Reserves, 33 Elephant Reserves and 18 Biosphere Reserves.

2.6 per cent
of India’s area.

The
Cold Desert
BR was added to the WNBR in 2025 as India's first high-altitude cold desert BR.
The Great Rann of Kutch is the largest Indian Biosphere Reserve, with an area of approximately 12,454 square kilometres.

Pench National Park, located in Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra, inspired Rudyard Kipling’s
The Jungle Book
Keoladeo National Park is in Bharatpur, Rajasthan, not Alwar.
Balpakram is in Meghalaya, not Manipur (PYQ 2023).

The Great Indian Bustard is protected in Desert National Park of Rajasthan and Rollapadu Wildlife Sanctuary of Andhra Pradesh.
The Great Indian Bustard population is stated to be below 150, Rollapadu is one of its habitats, and the 2024 Supreme Court order addressed underground power lines for its conservation.

Panna
Tiger Reserve was declared a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in 2020.

The Western Ghats were inscribed as a natural World Heritage Site in 2012.
Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers National Parks were inscribed in 1988; the property was extended in 2005.

secs.t: World-famous national parks → country and feature

x: Serengeti National Park is in Tanzania and is famous for the great wildebeest migration.
Banff National Park is in Canada and is located in the Rocky Mountains.
Yellowstone
(USA, 1872), known for geysers such as Old Faithful, is the world's first national park.

x: Tamil Nadu issued eviction notices in Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve after the Supreme Court order in A.
John Kennedy v. State of Tamil Nadu
Andhra Pradesh has one tiger reserve, Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam, one elephant reserve formed by Koundinya and Rayala, and one Biosphere Reserve, Seshachalam.
The notified forest area of Andhra Pradesh is 37,421.11 square kilometres, constituting
22.96 percent
of the State's area.

x: The Ramsar definition includes all four categories: marshes, fens, peatlands, natural or artificial water, waters of different salinities and qualifying shallow marine water.
JP Narayan Bird Sanctuary/Surha Tal and Shekha Jheel are in Uttar Pradesh, Khichan and Menar are in Rajasthan, and Kopra Reservoir is in Chhattisgarh.
Glaw Lake lies within Kamlang Tiger Reserve, supports the white-bellied heron and is Arunachal Pradesh's first Ramsar site.

painted storks and spot-billed pelicans
The Rushikulya mouth hosts the
olive ridley arribada
, the mass nesting congregation of olive ridley turtles.
Bharatpur is Keoladeo in Rajasthan with both Ramsar and UNESCO World Heritage status; Pitti is in Lakshadweep and Sultanpur is in Gurugram, Haryana.

Gharial and Gangetic dolphin
Bhitarkanika in Odisha is known for its saltwater crocodiles and mangrove ecosystems.

Rollapadu protects the

x: Mining within 10 km requires approval from the National Board for Wildlife and the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
Elephant reserves can overlap with Tiger Reserves, Wildlife Sanctuaries and reserved forests.
The 2017 count estimated India's elephant population at 29,964.
Odisha's three ERs are Mayurbhanj, Mahanadi and Sambalpur.

x: A growing share of India's tigers is living outside notified reserves, which raises the possibility of conflict with human communities.
The All India Tiger Estimation 2022 recorded approximately
63–67 tigers
in the State's Tiger Reserve.
Corbett was the first Tiger Reserve in 1973, Chilika was the first Ramsar site in 1981, and Glaw Lake became the newest Ramsar site in 2026.

rows.title: India - soil types, characteristics and distribution; soil erosion and conservation
sub: Group-II S2-19: India - soils: types, distribution and conservation

secs.t: Soil — composition, classification and types

x: A good soil is approximately composed of 45% mineral matter, 5% organic matter, 25% water and 25% air by volume.
Soil organic carbon binds particles into aggregates, improves infiltration and supports microbial activity.
Residual or in situ soils dominate Peninsular India, whereas drifted or ex situ soils dominate North India.

secs.t: Soil terms → meaning

x: Exam angle: Khadar = new alluvium, Bhangar = old. Pairing black soil with basalt and laterite with leaching is asked every year.
The normal sequence is O, A, B, C and R: organic litter, topsoil, subsoil, weathered parent material and bedrock.
The
B horizon
is the subsoil zone where minerals washed down from upper horizons accumulate.

secs.t: Soil types → regions and crops

x: Exam angle: "New alluvium is called..." (Khadar); which state has laterite.
The classification recognises
eight
major soil types: alluvial, black, red and yellow, laterite, arid, saline and alkaline, peaty and marshy, and forest and mountain soils.
Laterite soil can support tea, coffee, rubber and cashew cultivation when adequately manured.
Laterite soil occurs in the Western Ghats, Rajmahal Hills and North-Eastern states, besides other regions including parts of Andhra Pradesh.
Arid soil is sandy, deficient in nitrogen and humus, and its agricultural productivity can improve with irrigation.
Forest and mountain soils are humus-rich, occur on slopes and are generally poor in potash and phosphorus.
Regur (black cotton) soil from Deccan basalt is suited to cotton, jowar, chillies and tobacco.

secs.t: Black, laterite, peaty and Karewa soils → properties and places

x: Black soil has more than 62% clay, retains moisture well, develops deep summer cracks and is known for its self-ploughing character.
Black soil is comparatively rich in
calcium, potassium and magnesium
, but deficient in nitrogen, phosphorus and humus.
Peaty and marshy soils form in areas of heavy rainfall and high humidity where waterlogging permits organic matter to accumulate.
Peaty and marshy soils occur in Kerala, the Sundarbans, coastal Odisha and Tamil Nadu, north Bihar and Almora.
Karewas are old lake-bed deposits of unconsolidated gravel and mud.

secs.t: Problem soils and land degradation → causes and remedies

x: Unscientific irrigation practices combined with inadequate drainage promote salinity, alkalinity and waterlogging.
Without preservation measures, about
of the world's arable land could be affected by salinity by 2050, caused largely by unscientific irrigation and poor drainage.
Climate change is a general additional driver of land degradation and is not confined only to Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh.
The FAO 2026 report ranks soil-biodiversity loss 4th of 7 threats, after erosion, soil organic carbon loss and nutrient mismanagement.

secs.t: Soil erosion — types and factors — Types of erosion

x: Rills are small water-cut channels, wind erosion involves the three stated movements, and tunnel erosion removes soil below the surface and can form sinkholes.
Parts of Australia and Africa are associated with tunnel erosion, in which subsurface removal may create sinkholes, not sheet erosion.
Wind erosion is worst where soil is bare, dry and fine-textured and winds are strong and frequent.

secs.t: Soil erosion — types and factors — Factors controlling erosion rate

x: Slope, vegetation and land use, and soil type and texture are important factors.
When rainfall intensity exceeds infiltration capacity, water runs off or evaporates rather than recharging the soil.
RUSLE is used to predict long-term water erosion on slopes.
Clay soils hold more soil organic carbon, whereas steep slopes are more prone to losing carbon-rich topsoil.

secs.t: Soil conservation methods → how they work

x: Contour ploughing slows runoff along contour lines; terracing creates steps; check dams trap sediment and limit gully growth; shelter belts reduce wind speed.
Strip cropping alternates strips of erosion-resistant crops, such as grass, with row crops to reduce wind- and water-induced erosion.
Crop rotation improves fertility, cuts pest build-up and helps prevent erosion.

secs.t: Schemes and programmes — Soil Health Card, watershed, mapping

x: The Soil Health Card scheme was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 19 February 2015 at Suratgarh in Rajasthan.
The scheme tests 12 parameters: N, P, K, S, Zn, Fe, Cu, Mn, B, pH, EC and organic carbon.
The slogan of the Soil Health Card scheme is “
Swasth Dharaa, Khet Haraa
The target is 7,500 Village-Level Soil Testing Labs for 2023-26, with Rs 1.5 lakh aid per lab.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Kurnool is promoting Pre-Monsoon Dry Sowing on a target area of 92,000 acres along with Jeevamrutham to conserve soil moisture.
Both statements are true, and the large area under agriculture together with its employment share explains why soil health has direct livelihood significance.
Deterioration in soil management reinforces, rather than eliminates, the need for sustainable agricultural practices.

rows.title: India - rocks and mineral belts; distribution of metallic and non-metallic minerals
sub: Group-II S2-30: Mineral resources of India - metallic and non-metallic; mineral belts

secs.t: Rock systems and mineral belts → minerals

x: The North-Eastern Plateau belt is rich in
coal, iron ore, manganese, mica, bauxite and copper
The belt spans Karnataka, Goa, the TN uplands and Kerala, and Kerala is noted for monazite.
The Central belt covering Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh contains iron ore, including Bailadila, manganese including Balaghat, coal and limestone.
The Southern belt includes Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu and is associated with iron ore, gold, manganese, chromite and lignite; Neyveli is a major lignite area.

secs.t: Deposit types and ores → metal

x: Magnetite has up to about 70–72 per cent iron, haematite about 60–70 per cent, limonite 40–60 per cent and siderite is the lowest-grade ore.
Beach sands of Srikakulam and Visakhapatnam contain ilmenite, rutile, zircon, garnet and monazite.
Gold, tin and platinum
are associated with placer deposits formed in alluvial sands.
Monazite is an important source of
thorium and rare earths
and occurs in coastal sands, including those of Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.

secs.t: Metallic minerals → states, deposits and mines — Mineral → leading areas

x: Keonjhar and Bonai in Odisha are iron-ore areas.
Odisha leads in
bauxite
deposits, particularly in Kalahandi, Sambalpur and Koraput.
Malanjkhand (Balaghat) is a copper area of Madhya Pradesh.
Ramagiri is located in Anantapur district of Andhra Pradesh.

secs.t: Metallic minerals → states, deposits and mines — Mine → mineral

x: Most of Andhra Pradesh's iron ore is
haematite
, and Anantapur ranks first in the State for iron ore.
Visakhapatnam Steel Plant gets its iron ore mainly from
Bailadila
in Chhattisgarh.
These agency areas hold bauxite, and mining clashes with PVTG rights and Eastern Ghats ecology.
Koderma is associated with mica, Bailadila with iron ore, Khetri with copper and Zawar with lead-zinc.

secs.t: Mica and non-metallic minerals → states and uses

x: Mica occurs in pegmatite veins hosted by granite, gneiss and schist.
Phlogopite and muscovite
are the main mica minerals; phlogopite is magnesium mica.
The major mica belts are Nellore, Koderma–Gaya–Hazaribagh and Ajmer–Bhilwara.
Mica is used in electrical and electronic industries because it is an effective
electrical insulator
Mangampet in Kadapa is among the world's largest deposits of
barytes

secs.t: Mineral production and trade — data

x: A record 30 mineral blocks became operational in FY 2025–26, marking a first.
Gujarat
led with 4 limestone blocks, followed by MP with 3, Rajasthan with 2 and AP with 1.
India is self-sufficient in iron ore and is a net exporter, with exports of about 21 million tonnes in 2022–23 and 46 million tonnes in 2023–24.
Odisha
had the highest share, at 44.11%, in the value of mineral production in 2021–22.

secs.t: Critical minerals — list, mission and overseas partners — Critical minerals list

x: An expert committee under the
Ministry of Mines
identified 30 critical minerals in June 2023.
Over 90% of coking-coal reserves are in Jharia.

secs.t: Critical minerals — list, mission and overseas partners — National Critical Mineral Mission

x: 1,200 projects by 2030-31, 50 overseas assets and a national stockpile are in the mission.
The Central Sector scheme covers e-waste, lithium-ion batteries and other scrap.
GSI’s ‘Uncover India’ project is being carried out with
Geoscience Australia
to probe deep-seated deposits.

secs.t: Critical minerals — list, mission and overseas partners — Overseas partners → mineral

x: KABIL is a joint venture of National Aluminium Company Limited, Hindustan Copper Limited and Mineral Exploration Corporation Limited.
The Andhra Pradesh Mineral Development Corporation (
APMDC
) is to facilitate value addition following comprehensive mineral mapping.
The Feb 2025 agreement was with
Argentina
, where KABIL holds 15,703 ha in Catamarca for lithium.

secs.t: Acts, Articles, cases and policy on mining — Administration and MMDR Act 1957

x: Minor minerals (building stone, gravel, sand) are regulated by the States.

secs.t: Acts, Articles, cases and policy on mining — Amendments → change

x: States must approve adding a critical mineral to a lease within 30 days.
The 2025 amendment did not place all minor minerals under exclusive Central regulation.
The Bill, passed in August 2026, sought uniform rates by restricting States' power to tax mineral rights and mineral-bearing land.

secs.t: Acts, Articles, cases and policy on mining — Royalty and judgments

x: The 2015 amendment introduced auction-only allotment and created the District Mineral Foundation and the National Mineral Exploration Trust.
In July 2026 the SC upheld the Centre's royalty formula, based on an Average Sale Price that includes royalty, DMF and NMET.
PMKKKY uses District Mineral Foundation funds for the welfare of mining-affected people and areas and provides for a yearly audit.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Boksampalli gold blocks, covering 1,740 hectares and containing gold, PGE and iron ore, are to be
auctioned
The MMDR Amendment 2026 has been criticised for eroding state fiscal autonomy, and bauxite mining conflicts involve the FCA, FRA and PVTG rights.
Swarnagiri was renamed from Jonnagiri, lies in Tuggali mandal of Kurnool district and belongs to the Jonnagiri greenstone belt.
AP is nicknamed '
Ratna Garbha
' (womb of gems) for its mineral wealth. 'Annapurna' and 'Dhanya Kosh' describe granary roles, and Swarna Bhoomi is not the stated nickname.

rows.title: India - earthquake zones, landslide-prone areas, cyclone-prone coasts; seismic zoning map

secs.t: Hazard profile of India — data and concepts

x: About 40 million ha is flood-prone, but that is about 12% of the land, not 40%.
Approximately 5,700 km of India’s nearly 7,516 km coastline is exposed to cyclone and tsunami hazards.
The relationship is expressed as
hazard multiplied by vulnerability equals disaster
The DM Act 2005 moved India's approach from relief to prevention, mitigation and preparedness.

secs.t: Seismic zoning map and BIS codes

x: Exam angle: "zones merged" (I into II), and Zone VI as a proposed-then-withdrawn change.
The proposed BIS revision used
Probabilistic Seismic Hazard Assessment
, abbreviated as PSHA.
The Centre rolled back the proposed revision in March 2026 after criticism concerning its methodology and cost; consequently, the four-zone map continued to apply.
IS 1893 specifies seismic design criteria, IS 13920 covers ductile detailing, and the National Building Code is applicable to building safety provisions.

secs.t: Hazards → regions — earthquakes and landslides

x: The GSI estimates that approximately
12.6–15 per cent
of India’s area, or about 0.42 million square kilometres, is landslide-prone.
The Western Ghats and Nilgiris are landslide-prone because of steep escarpments and orographic rain, not permafrost.
Landslide Hazard Zonation divides hill areas into homogeneous units by susceptibility, hazard or risk; such maps are probabilistic, not exact forecasts.

secs.t: Cyclone and tsunami coasts → warning centres

x: Cyclones affect both coasts, but the east coast receives far more because the Bay of Bengal generates about four times as many cyclones as the Arabian Sea.
The seven IMD cyclone warning centres are Chennai, Mumbai, Kolkata, Ahmedabad, Thiruvananthapuram, Visakhapatnam and Bhubaneswar.
ISRO’s DMS maps coastal vulnerability and runs the NDEM database.

secs.t: Major disasters → type and place

x: The 1967 Koyna earthquake (Maharashtra) is the classic case of reservoir-induced seismicity.
Koyna occurred in 1967, Killari in 1993, Bhuj in 2001 and the Indian Ocean Tsunami in 2004.
The snow avalanche at Badrinath-Mana resulted in the death of Border Roads Organisation workers.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: APSDMA is chaired by the Chief Minister and runs the State Emergency Operations Centre
The debate concerns the use of probabilistic seismic hazard assessment for zoning and the associated cost implications for the built environment.
The NDMA-Ministry of Panchayati Raj project works through panchayats in 81 districts across 20 States.

rows.title: Andhra Pradesh - location, extent, districts, physiographic divisions

secs.t: Formation, area and rank — FIRSTs, Act and data

x: Exam angle: read whether the question asks about "States" or "States and UTs".
The seven mandals came from Khammam, the transfer followed the 2014 Polavaram ordinance and amendment, and Chinturu division is now in Polavaram district.
In 1960, the Pataskar award transferred most of Tiruttani taluk to Tamil Nadu and some villages of Tiruvallur to Andhra Pradesh.

secs.t: Physiographic divisions → key facts

x: The coastal plains, particularly the Godavari and Krishna deltaic region, are known as the Rice Bowl of Andhra Pradesh.
Mahendragiri is associated with Srikakulam and the Eastern Ghats, not the Rayalaseema plateau.
The Rayalaseema plateau forms part of the Deccan and consists of drought-prone uplands.
Archaean Dharwar rocks occur in
Anantapur, Chittoor and Kadapa
and are more than 2,500 million years old.

secs.t: Districts → counts and headquarters

x: The district counts were 20 in 1956, 23 after the three additions, 13 in residual Andhra Pradesh after 2014, and 26 from 4 April 2022.
Polavaram district was created for the rehabilitation and resettlement of Polavaram-project villages.
The APPSC-G1 2022 key gives
Parvathipuram Manyam
as the smallest district by area.

secs.t: Regions → districts

x: Uttarandhra, also called Kalinga Andhra, comprises
ASR, Anakapalli, Parvathipuram Manyam, Visakhapatnam, Vizianagaram and Srikakulam
Uttarandhra had 6 districts, the rest of Coastal Andhra had 12, and Rayalaseema had 8 districts.
Rayalaseema borders Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Telangana.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Coastal Andhra is characterised here by its river deltas, dominant share of farm output and highest population density.
Andhra Pradesh is identified as the first linguistic State in the context of the formation of Andhra State in 1953 and Andhra Pradesh in 1956.
The current 28-district structure includes the new districts of
Polavaram and Markapuram
Andhra Pradesh has 28 districts in the current classification, including the new Polavaram and Markapuram districts.

rows.title: Andhra Pradesh - coastline, deltas, hill ranges (Eastern Ghats, Nallamala, Seshachalam)
sub: Group-II S2-21: Andhra Pradesh - major physiographic features and coastline

secs.t: Area, latitude, longitude and borders

x: 1,60,205 sq km is the area left after the 2014 bifurcation, before the 7 Polavaram mandals were added.
The 82.5° E meridian passes through
Kakinada
in Andhra Pradesh and is associated with Indian Standard Time.
Yanam, a Puducherry enclave of about 30 square kilometres, is located in
the Godavari delta
of Andhra Pradesh.

secs.t: Physiographic regions and deltas → districts

x: From east to west and from the coast towards the interior, the broad sequence is Coastal plains, Eastern Ghats and Western plateau.
All four statements correctly describe the Eastern Ghats hill region of Andhra Pradesh, including its districts, elevation, forests and tribal belts.
The Godavari delta is known as Konaseema; its central delta is about 150 km wide and is noted for coconut and banana cultivation.

secs.t: Coastline — length, rank and end points

x: Exam angle: "recalculated" questions want 1,053.07 km; "2nd longest" is the pre-2025 answer.
Exam angle: the 2025 paper offered both 1,068.69 and 1,053.07; the first is Tamil Nadu's figure.
The increase resulted from GIS retracing at 1:250,000 scale and does not represent an actual physical change in India's coastline.
Srikakulam has the longest district coast (193 km).

secs.t: Coastal plain — names, dimensions and mangroves

x: The AP coastal plain is approximately 950 km long, about 60 km wide on average, rises up to 150 metres and is called the Rice Bowl.
The Andhra coastal plain is an emergent, broad coast built by river deposition and characterised by large deltas.
Coringa is at the Godavari estuary near Kakinada, while the Krishna Wildlife Sanctuary represents mangroves at the Krishna estuary.

secs.t: Coastal lakes and lagoons → district

x: Sriharikota Island
separates Pulicat Lake from the Bay of Bengal.
Kolleru Lake is associated with
Eluru
district; it lies between the Krishna and Godavari deltas.
Uppalapadu is in Guntur district and is a bird sanctuary tank known for pelicans and painted storks.
Kolleru is a freshwater lake of about 305 sq km between the two deltas, while Pulicat is a saltwater lagoon shared with Tamil Nadu.

secs.t: Eastern Ghats — features, rocks and limits

x: The Eastern Ghats join the Western Ghats near the Nilgiris, not the Anaimalai hills.
The Eastern Ghats are discontinuous and eroded hills, dissected by the Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri rivers.
All three statements correctly describe the relative age, average height and northern dimensions of the Eastern Ghats.
The
Vamsadhara, Nagavali and Sabari
rivers rise in the Eastern Ghats.

secs.t: Eastern Ghats ranges → local names and districts

x: Exam angle: "Eastern Ghats in Srikakulam are called ___" and "Seshachalam belongs to ___" are direct recall questions.
The Nallamala range lies between the
Krishna and Penna
basins.
The Chenchus, a Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group living in the Nallamala region, are associated with the ITDA at
Srisailam
The
Seshachalam
hills, including the Tirumala hills, are noted for their red sanders forests.
In Srikakulam the Ghats are called
Mahendragiri (Mahendra Girulu)
, running into Odisha.

secs.t: Highest peaks → height and location

x: Jindhagada
, located near Araku, is identified in Andhra Pradesh publications as the highest peak of the Eastern Ghats.
Arma Konda is 1,680 m, Galikonda is 1,643 m and Sintram Gutta is 1,620 m.
Arma Konda, also known as Sitamma Konda, is recorded as 1,680 metres high and located in the ASR district of Andhra Pradesh.

secs.t: Hill stations and waterfalls → district

x: Horsley Hills is located in
Annamayya
district near Madanapalle and the Karnataka border.
Maredumilli is associated with the Polavaram district arrangement through the Rampachodavaram agency division.
Talakona is in Tirupati district, not Guntur.
Ethipothala Falls lies on the Chandravanka near Nagarjuna Sagar in Palnadu district.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Gaur are to be translocated from Central India to NSTR and Nallamala from September 2026 with support from the Wildlife Institute of India.
NSTR was established in 1983, covers about 3,728 square kilometres, and lies in Andhra Pradesh (the Telangana part is now Amrabad Tiger Reserve).
NCCR found 38% of the east coast eroding against 30% of the west coast; Uppada in Kakinada is AP's worst spot.

rows.title: Andhra Pradesh - drainage: Godavari, Krishna, Penna, Vamsadhara, Nagavali; reservoirs and canals
sub: Group-II S2-23: Andhra Pradesh - drainage system: Godavari, Krishna, Penna and minor rivers

secs.t: River system — data, FIRSTs and basin States

x: Mahendra Tanaya and Bahuda
are rivers shared by Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.
Palar is associated with Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, not Odisha and Chhattisgarh.
The Godavari has the largest peninsular basin, followed by the Krishna and the Mahanadi.
The
Narmada and Cauvery
basins are approximately equal in size.
India has 20 basins: 12 major basins with areas over 20,000 sq km each and 8 composite basins.

secs.t: Rivers → origin, length and mouth

x: Exam angle: match river → origin hills (Vamsadhara - Jayapur; Machkund - Mudugal; Gundlakamma - Nallamala; Pennar - Nandidurga).
The Gosthani originates in the Eastern Ghats, has a length of about 120 km and forms an estuary near Bheemunipatnam.
Mahendra Tanaya, which originates in the Mahendragiri hills, is a tributary of the
Vamsadhara
The total lengths are Godavari 1,465 km, Krishna about 1,400 km, Penna 597 km and Vamsadhara 254 km.
The Godavari rises at Trimbakeshwar near Nashik, runs 1,465 km and meets the Bay of Bengal at Antarvedi; it is called 'Dakshina Ganga'.

secs.t: Penna (Pennar) → course and tributaries

x: Gandikota gorge, also called the Gandikota canyon, is formed by the Penna in
YSR Kadapa district
Papagni
is a right-bank tributary of the Penna and originates from Chikkaballapur via the Nandi Hills.
Cheyyeru joins at Gundlamada in Kadapa and is associated with the Annamayya dam; Sagileru joins near Kamalapuram, while Chitravathi joins at Gandikota.

secs.t: Deltas — distributaries, islands and landforms

x: At Dowleswaram, the Godavari splits into the two main distributaries,
Gautami and Vasishta
The seven mouths include Gautami, Vasishta, Vainateya, Tulya, Bharadwaja, Kaushika and Athreya.
Diviseema, also called Divi island, lies between the two branches of the Krishna formed at Puligadda.
Bhavani Island is a Krishna river island near
Prakasam Barrage at Vijayawada
and is used as a tourism destination.

secs.t: Projects, barrages and tanks → river and district

x: Exam angle: "Anantaraja Sagar / Cumbum tank is in which district / on which river".
Polavaram is a multipurpose dam constructed on the
Godavari
River.
Sir Arthur Cotton Barrage is situated at Dowleswaram near Rajahmundry on the Godavari River.
Gotta Barrage is constructed on the Vamsadhara River in Srikakulam district.
Sunkesula Barrage is constructed on the
Tungabhadra River
in Kurnool district and forms the head of the KC Canal.
The total irrigation potential created was
106.15 lakh acres

secs.t: Polavaram, Pattiseema and canals → purpose and beneficiaries — Polavaram

x: The Polavaram Left Main Canal carries Godavari water towards North Coastal Andhra and Visakhapatnam.
The design figures are 194.6 TMC storage, irrigation potential of 7.20 lakh acres, 960 MW generation and diversion of 80 TMC to the Krishna.
The project was reported to be 89 percent complete and targeted for dedication by
March 2027, before the Pushkarams

secs.t: Polavaram, Pattiseema and canals → purpose and beneficiaries — Pattiseema

x: Pattiseema lifts Godavari water into the Polavaram Right Main Canal, which carries it to the Krishna at
Prakasam Barrage
The Telugu Ganga Project takes Krishna water from Srisailam, supplies Chennai, irrigates 2.75 lakh acres in Kurnool and Kadapa, and was conceived by N. T. Rama Rao.
The route runs from Srisailam through the Penna basin at Somasila, then Kandaleru, and finally Poondi in Tamil Nadu.

secs.t: Polavaram, Pattiseema and canals → purpose and beneficiaries — Other canals → purpose

x: Total irrigation is about 4.47 lakh acres.
Galeru-Nagari carries Krishna flood water to
Kadapa and Chittoor
districts.

secs.t: River links and waterways → rivers linked — National links and waterway

x: AP's 2026 plans include intra-linking from the Vamsadhara to the Penna, completing the Vamsadhara-Nagavali link by December, and taking about 200 TMC of Godavari water to the Nagarjunasagar ayacut via Nallamala Sagar and Veligonda.
Godavari–Penna Phase-I involves 73 TMC through a five-stage lift, Package-I was reported at 21%, and Telangana opposes the proposed Polavaram–Nallamala Sagar link.

secs.t: River links and waterways → rivers linked — Banakacherla / Polavaram-Nallamala Sagar

x: Telangana argues that the project involves excess use of the Krishna share and violates the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 and the Godavari Water Disputes Tribunal award of 1980.
The project is now being pursued as the
Polavaram–Nallamala Sagar project

secs.t: Tribunals, Acts and river boards

x: Bahuda, Vamsadhara and Nagavali are covered by inter-state agreements, while Godavari waters are governed through a tribunal award.
The Brijesh Kumar Tribunal, or KWDT-II, dealt with the Krishna dispute and submitted its report in 2010, followed by a further report in 2013.
The Vamsadhara water dispute is between
Andhra Pradesh and Odisha
; the final award was given in 2017.
Babli barrage is a Maharashtra barrage on the Godavari upstream of
Sriramsagar
and was disputed by undivided Andhra Pradesh.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The third warning level was crossed at
Bhadrachalam
Telangana objects to Pattiseema; there is no unconditional Telangana endorsement.
The KRMB committee limited water from
Srisailam and Nagarjunasagar
to drinking use only because of El Niño conditions.

rows.title: Andhra Pradesh - climate, rainfall regions, cyclone vulnerability, drought-prone areas
sub: Group-II S2-22: Andhra Pradesh - climate, rainfall regions and cyclone vulnerability
Group-II S2-28: Cyclone, flood, drought and tsunami management with reference to Andhra Pradesh

secs.t: Climate — seasons and extremes → place

x: Lambasingi is noted for
snow-like frost
and temperatures falling to about 2°C.
Winter is January–February, summer is March to mid-June, the south-west monsoon is mid-June to September, and the retreating monsoon is October–December.
Occasional winter rain comes from retreating systems and western disturbances, not the SW monsoon (June-September).
Mango showers are pre-monsoon showers in April-May that help mangoes ripen.

secs.t: Rainfall — monsoon shares and data — Seasonal shares

x: July
is generally the wettest month in Andhra Pradesh during the South-West Monsoon season.
The
Coromandel coast of Tamil Nadu
receives most of its rainfall from the north-east monsoon rather than the south-west monsoon.
Andhra Pradesh lies between the predominantly south-west-monsoon regime of most of India and the north-east-monsoon regime of Tamil Nadu; about one-third of its rainfall occurs in October–December.

secs.t: Rainfall — monsoon shares and data — Normal and annual rainfall

x: The
South-West Monsoon
contributes about two-thirds, or approximately 65–70%, of Andhra Pradesh's annual rainfall.
Rayalaseema and the southern coastal districts
depend more on the North-East or retreating monsoon than other parts of the State.
The June–December total was 960.3 mm against a normal of 860.0 mm, representing a positive deviation of 11.7%.

secs.t: Regions → hazards; drought-prone Rayalaseema — Region → main hazards

x: Coastal Andhra faces cyclones and related coastal hazards; Rayalaseema and southern Prakasam face chronic drought and groundwater depletion; inland plains face rising heat waves.
The coast is exposed to cyclones and storm surge, the Godavari–Krishna deltas to floods, and semi-arid Rayalaseema to drought.
Although the Andhra Pradesh coast was hit in 2004,
Tamil Nadu
was the worst-affected State.

secs.t: Regions → hazards; drought-prone Rayalaseema — Rain-shadow Rayalaseema — causes

x: Rural distress is particularly severe in drought-prone Rayalaseema and rain-fed
Prakasam, Anantapur, Kurnool and Kadapa
Both statements are true, and the rain-shadow location explains the limited south-west monsoon rainfall of Rayalaseema.
Failure of the
north-east monsoon
can cause chronic droughts in Rayalaseema and southern Prakasam.
Anantapur
, in rain-shadow Rayalaseema, is the lowest-rainfall district of AP.

secs.t: Regions → hazards; drought-prone Rayalaseema — Watershed and resilience projects

x: Watershed projects may improve groundwater, but crop yields can remain flat when crop diversification and soil management are neglected.
Veligonda Phase-I moves Krishna water to
Prakasam, Nellore and Kadapa
WDC-PMKSY 2.0 develops degraded and rain-fed land through
integrated natural-resource management
under the Department of Land Resources.
Gandikota reservoir is situated on the Pennar River in YSR Kadapa district and forms part of the Telugu Ganga system.

secs.t: Cyclone vulnerability — coast, districts and cyclones → landfall — Coastline and exposure

x: Cyclone activity along the Andhra Pradesh coast peaks during
October to December
3rd after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu.

secs.t: Cyclone vulnerability — coast, districts and cyclones → landfall — Vulnerable areas

x: Storm surges can inundate villages up to
10 km
inland.
Srikakulam, Vizianagaram and Nellore
are identified as highly cyclone-prone coastal districts.

secs.t: Cyclone vulnerability — coast, districts and cyclones → landfall — Major cyclones → landfall

x: Exam angle: year of Hudhud (2014), state hit by Titli.
The Diviseema cyclone struck Diviseema in the Krishna delta on 19 November 1977 and produced a huge storm surge.
Hudhud made landfall at Visakhapatnam in October 2014, Titli affected the Srikakulam–Odisha coast in October 2018, and Michaung occurred near Bapatla in December 2023.

secs.t: Cyclone mitigation — measures and lessons

x: Accurate warnings and timely evacuation
contributed significantly to the sharp fall in deaths during cyclones such as Phailin and Fani.
Cyclone shelters, evacuation plans, IMD early warning, coastal shelter belts and mangroves are mitigation measures.
Multipurpose shelters, raised platforms, all-weather evacuation roads and storm-surge barriers are all structural cyclone-mitigation measures identified in the guidelines.

secs.t: Flood forecasting and control — framework and anicuts

x: The Godavari delta was affected by
floods, cyclones and famine
, prompting construction of the anicut.
The Godavari Anicut is now the Sir Arthur Cotton, or Dowleswaram, Barrage near Rajamahendravaram.
The Krishna and Godavari River Management Boards advise both States on
water releases for flood and drought mitigation
under Schedule 11.

secs.t: Acts, institutions and cases — drought, APSDMA and early warning — Laws and APSDMA

x: The
Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority
(APSDMA) is a statutory body under the Disaster Management Act, 2005 and the Andhra Pradesh Disaster Management Rules, 2007, and is the chief nodal agency for disaster management in the State.

secs.t: Acts, institutions and cases — drought, APSDMA and early warning — Drought declaration and monitoring

x: The Crop Weather Watch Group functions under the
Ministry of Agriculture
and meets weekly during the monsoon.
The Supreme Court directed that the drought manual be updated and the
National Disaster Mitigation Fund
be set up.
The Ministry of Agriculture handles drought along with pest attacks, hailstorms and frost/cold waves.

secs.t: Acts, institutions and cases — drought, APSDMA and early warning — Recent initiatives (2026)

x: The City Flood Alert was developed through collaboration among
RTGS, APSDMA and IIT Gandhinagar
The platform provides 48-hour rain forecasts and 6-hour flash-flood warnings.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The CMIP6 projection indicates excess southwest monsoon rainfall for Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu and a rise exceeding 1°C in 40 coastal districts by 2040.
Andhra Pradesh faces the combined risks of east-coast cyclones, hazards associated with two major deltas and drought in its interior, requiring multi-hazard planning.
Odisha’s evacuations during Phailin and Fani and Andhra Pradesh’s response to Hudhud are cited as models of warning-led, zero-casualty management.

secs.t: Forest types → region and species

x: Littoral and mangrove forests occur in the Godavari–Krishna deltas and Pulicat, not in the inland Rayalaseema districts of Anantapur, Kadapa and Kurnool.
Araku and Paderu lie in the northern Eastern Ghats, Papikondalu has moist deciduous forests, and thorn and scrub vegetation is associated with Rayalaseema.
Rhizophora
, along with Avicennia and Excoecaria, is associated with the littoral and mangrove forests of these coastal areas.

secs.t: Valuable species → region

x: Red sanders is endemic to the Seshachalam, Palakonda and Veligonda ranges of Andhra Pradesh.
The teak wood bank is located at
Kapavaram
Thermal-imaging drones
have been used against red sanders smuggling in the Seshachalam region.

secs.t: Forest cover — density and legal classes (data)

x: Open Forest
was the largest class, covering 14,363.50 sq km.
The notified forest area is approximately 85.8% Reserved Forest, 13.6% Protected Forest and 0.6% Unclassed Forest.
The protected-area network covers 8,139.88 sq km, equivalent to 4.99% of the State's area.

secs.t: Districts and places → forest cover and fires

x: YSR Kadapa
had the largest forest area among the pre-2022 districts.
Visakhapatnam
had the highest forest cover and Krishna had the lowest among the pre-2022 districts.
All four locations—Horsley Hills, Mallappa Konda near Kuppam, Mallaiahkonda and the Somala belt—were identified as fire-prone zones.
Andhra Pradesh recorded
of fire-affected forest in 2023-24, the highest in India.

secs.t: Forest produce — revenue, output and craft wood banks

x: The craft wood banks supply timber to artisans on a no-profit basis.
Andhra Pradesh recorded forest revenue of
₹32.81 crore
During April–December 2024–25,
timber production was 1,562.886 cmt against a target of 24,925.69 cmt
NTFP in Andhra Pradesh is worth
more than ₹500 crore
a year, far above the State's forest revenue of ₹32.81 crore in 2023-24.

secs.t: Agencies → function: GCC, TRIFED, APFDC

x: The Andhra Pradesh Forest Development Corporation is the Government’s agent for exporting red sanders wood and beedi leaf.
The Girijan Co-operative Corporation buys minor forest produce from tribals.
TRIFED was established in 1987 under the Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act, 1984, and functions under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs.
Clonal eucalyptus occupies the largest APFDC plantation area, covering 33,584 hectares.

secs.t: Acts, programmes and Finance Commission on forests

x: CAMPA funds
compensatory afforestation through an Annual Plan of Operation
Vanam-Manam increases green cover outside reserved forests; 5.29 crore seedlings had been covered in 2024–25 up to December.
The 2026 change allows commercial plantations on degraded forest land and is linked to the national goal of 33% forest cover.
The 16th Finance Commission included open forests in the devolution forest criterion using
density-based weights

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The reported green-cover gain was 1,445 sq km, but only
156 sq km
represented true forest.
The criticism is that planting drives, including the target of 140 crore saplings under “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam”, can increase tree cover without creating natural forests.
The Rekapalli revolt of 1879 was directed against
British forest laws

sub: Group-II S2-25: Andhra Pradesh - natural vegetation, forests, national parks and sanctuaries

secs.t: Protected areas → district, area and feature

x: Exam angle: chronology of notification, sanctuary → district after the 2022 district reorganisation, species → sanctuary.
The Rajiv Gandhi Wildlife Sanctuary (Tiger Reserve) extends over
Nandyal, Prakasam and Palnadu
districts and forms part of the Nallamala landscape.

Gundla Brahmeswaram (Nandyal-Prakasam, the extended core of NSTR in the Nallamala) is a dry deciduous forest sanctuary where the new Critically Endangered (CR) herb Euphorbia chalamensis was recorded in 2026.

secs.t: Chronology of notification → year

x: The notification years are Pulicat 1976, Coringa 1978, Koundinya 1990 and Kolleru 1999.
The sequence used in the APPSC 2025 answer key is Nelapattu, Rollapadu, Koundinya and Kolleru from oldest to newest.
The recorded sequence for Papikonda is Reserved Forest in 1882, Wildlife Sanctuary in 1978 and National Park in 2008.

secs.t: Tiger, biosphere and elephant reserves — Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve

x: NSTR lies in the Nallamala hills of the Eastern Ghats along the Krishna.
Tiger reserves are managed on
a core-buffer model under the National Tiger Conservation Authority
, in accordance with the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972.
Its Andhra Pradesh core areas lie in Nandyal, Prakasam and Palnadu, and the reserve is managed by the Srisailam circle.

secs.t: Tiger, biosphere and elephant reserves — Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve

x: The migration was attributed to drought in the
Hosur-Dharmapuri reserve forests and Bannerghatta
The
Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve
(4,755.997 sq km, 2010) is AP's only biosphere reserve.
AP has one elephant reserve, formed by the Koundinya Sanctuary and the
Rayala Elephant Reserve
(Anantapuramu circle); Koundinya is AP's only Asian elephant habitat.

secs.t: Forest regions and mangroves → species and type

x: Red Sanders is endemic to the
southern Eastern Ghats
of Andhra Pradesh and is characteristic of the Seshachalam and Palakonda belts.
The forest-bearing hills identified in Andhra Pradesh are
North Simhachalam, West Balaghat, South Palakonda and Nallamala
State economic survey documents describe Andhra Pradesh’s mangroves as the second-largest ecosystem, whereas ISFR 2023 places Gujarat second nationally.

secs.t: Bird sanctuaries, wetlands and IBAs → district and birds

x: Nelapattu
in Tirupati district is associated with spot-billed pelican breeding.
Telineelapuram and Telukunchi are in Srikakulam, Uppalapadu is in Guntur, and Kolleru lies between the Krishna and Godavari deltas.
The mass mortality at Telineelapuram involved the
spot-billed pelican
, Pelecanus philippensis.
The coastal wetlands of Andhra Pradesh also receive migrant ducks such as northern pintails, and painted storks.

secs.t: Flagship species → protected area; man-animal conflict

x: Exam angle: APPSC-G1 2024 match - Coringa-saltwater crocodile, Rollapadu-GIB, Sri Lankamalleswara-Jerdon's courser.
Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary is associated with the saltwater crocodile and mangrove vegetation.

Jerdon's courser (a critically endangered nocturnal bird) is protected in Sri Lankamalleswara WLS, the dwarf goat kanchu mekha is linked with Papikonda NP, the golden gecko with Sri Venkateswara NP (Tirumala hills), and flamingos with Pulicat WLS.

secs.t: Distractors from other states; NP vs WLS

x: Mrugavani National Park, Kasu Brahmananda Reddy National Park and Eturunagaram Wildlife Sanctuary are located in Telangana.

Jerdon's courser is found in Sri Lankamalleswara WLS (Kadapa), kanchu mekha in Papikonda NP, the golden gecko in the Tirumala hills, and Red Sanders is endemic to the Seshachalam (with Palakonda and Veligonda) hills of the southern Eastern Ghats.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Chilika is not a tiger reserve.
ZAAP
manages the zoos at Visakhapatnam and Tirupati.
The protected-area network of Andhra Pradesh includes India’s largest tiger reserve and the Red Sanders endemic-tree belt under special protection.
Rajiv Gandhi NP (2.30 sq km) is the smallest NP.

secs.t: AP soils — types, area ranking, largest and smallest — Area ranking

x: Skeletal soil
s occur in minor amounts, particularly in heavily eroded tracts of Andhra Pradesh.
Red soils are widely distributed in Rayalaseema, including Anantapur, Sri Sathya Sai, Kadapa, Nandyal and Kurnool, and also occur in coastal uplands.
Laterite soils constitute approximately 1 per cent of the area of Andhra Pradesh and occur mainly in coastal pockets and hills.

secs.t: AP soils — types, area ranking, largest and smallest — Soil categories (2024-25)

x: The classification records 22 categories; 10 predominant categories cover more than 88 per cent, with the two stated categories accounting for 20.42 and 18.65 per cent respectively.
Granitoid-gneiss bedrock underlies much of Andhra Pradesh, although several other formations and deposited soils also occur.

secs.t: AP soils — types, area ranking, largest and smallest — Red soil sub-types → share

x: Exam angle: match red-soil sub-types with % (loamy sub-soil 30, clay base 12, red loamy 9).
The APPSC-GS 2024 key accepted that red soils cover more than 60 per cent of the State and have
six
sub-groups (among them red earths with loamy subsoil, red soils with clay base, red loamy and red sandy soils).

secs.t: Soils → districts and regions

x: Fertile land in Andhra Pradesh lies along the
Krishna, Godavari, Penna and Vamsadhara
river systems.
Black soils cover about 25% of Andhra Pradesh, with deep black soils at Adoni and Alur and important areas in the Kunderu basin, Guntur, Palnadu, Prakasam and Kurnool.
The Krishna-Godavari deltaic tracts are characterised by highly fertile
deltaic alluvial soil

secs.t: Soils → parent rock, formation and properties

x: Black soils are rich in calcium, potash and magnesium, but poor in nitrogen, phosphorus and humus; they also retain water well.
Deep cracks formed on drying loosen and turn the soil, giving black soil its
self-ploughing
character.
Laterite soils are generally less fertile and poor in organic matter; their fertility is low despite the presence of iron and aluminium oxides.

secs.t: Soils → crops

x: Black soils, also called black cotton soils, are suited to cotton, jowar, chillies, tobacco, oilseeds and wheat.
Black gram
is specifically identified as doing best on black soils, while mango and cashew suit lateritic soils and coffee suits hill soils.
Paddy suits deltaic alluvium, cotton suits black soil, groundnut suits red soil and mango suits laterite soil.

secs.t: Terms → meaning: local and scientific soil names

x: Severe erosion in Rayalaseema can leave skeletal soils with
no nutritive value
Regur or Regadi means black cotton soil, Vertisols are black soils, Chalka denotes red sandy soil and Bhangar denotes old alluvium.
Dubba is a local red-soil sub-type.

secs.t: Problem soils, erosion and degradation → areas and causes

x: Deltaic salinity is also associated with poor drainage, faulty irrigation and saline water intrusion; it is not caused exclusively by natural coastal processes.
Clay soil
s hold more soil organic carbon, whereas sandy soils and steep slopes lose it through leaching and erosion.
Drought and wind erosion in Anantapur and Sri Sathya Sai, coastal erosion at Uppada, salinity and waterlogging in deltas, and topsoil loss through Podu cultivation in ASR and Parvathipuram Manyam.

secs.t: Schemes and responses — Soil Health Card, reclamation, natural farming

x: SMWSIPDCL
stands for Salinity Mitigation & Water Security, and it targets salinity and water-security issues in Andhra Pradesh.
Soil Health Cards provide soil-sample analysis and village-wise nutrient mapping, helping farmers understand soil nutrient status.
Since 2022-23, Soil Health and Fertility has been operated under the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (
RKVY

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Karnataka has mostly red soil, followed by black soil.
The North Coastal zone is associated with laterite, the Godavari zone with alluvium, and the Scarce Rainfall zone with red soil.
The seed component consisted of
sunn hemp, dhaincha and green gram
, which are used to help rebuild soil fertility through green manuring.

secs.t: AP minerals — "Ratna Garbha", shares of India and FIRSTs

x: “Ratna Garbha” means the
treasure house of minerals

AP is a leading producer of barytes, limestone, mica and granite; it holds India's largest mica reserves (40.5%) and production (70.2%); and Karnataka (25-28%, IMYB 2022), not AP, has the largest limestone reserves.
Rajasthan
has the Jaipur–Udaipur mica belt and ranks second in the stated comparison.

secs.t: Rocks → geological formation, region and minerals

x: Archaean
rocks, including extensive gneiss, occupy most of Andhra Pradesh and contain iron, manganese, copper, lead and gold.
The Cuddapah formation is Proterozoic, approximately 1.6 billion years old, and occurs mainly in the Kadapa, Nandyal, Kurnool, Annamayya and Prakasam areas.
Coastal sands containing ilmenite, rutile, zircon, garnet and monazite extend broadly from
Srikakulam to Nellore

secs.t: Minerals → district / place — APPSC 2023 match and full list

x: Exam angle: APPSC 2023 match - Mica-Nellore, Coal-West Godavari, Bauxite-East Godavari; Manganese is the fourth pair.

Diamonds occur in Krishna district and the Cuddapah-Vindhyan formations; AP's iron ore is mostly haematite; heavy-mineral beach sands run from the Srikakulam to the Krishna coast; and asbestos comes from the Cuddapah system of YSR Kadapa.

secs.t: Minerals → district / place — Key deposits (quick revision)

x: Thorium comes from monazite, which occurs with ilmenite, rutile and zircon in coastal beach sands (e.g.
Mangampet (YSR Kadapa) = barytes; Tummalapalle (YSR Kadapa) = uranium; Gudur (Nellore) = mica; Bhavanapadu (Srikakulam) = beach sand minerals.
Mangampeta is the barytes deposit in YSR Kadapa, Tummalapalle is the uranium mine in YSR Kadapa, and Jonnagiri is the gold mine in Kurnool.

secs.t: Mines and minerals → features (mica, gold, uranium, critical minerals)

x: The state policy promotes beneficiation plants for
low-grade iron ore and CDW-grade barytes
The Gudur-Nellore belt, muscovite white / phlogopite amber / biotite black, and minor-mineral status from 2015.
The Swarnagiri mine is operated by GeoMysore Services under a 30-year lease and is located in Tuggali mandal of Kurnool district.

secs.t: Granites and dimension stones → district; MMDR Act

x: Chimakurthy is known for Galaxy or black granite, while Srikakulam Blue, Pista Green of Kadapa and Chilli Red of Anantapur are other noted granite varieties or localities.
Minor minerals (building stone, gravel, clay, sand) are regulated by the States; major minerals in the First Schedule of the MMDR Act, 1957 come under the Centre.

secs.t: Oil and gas — KG basin fields → operators

x: Kakinada offshore, Amalapuram/Konaseema and Krishna offshore are associated with the KG basin.
Natural gas is targeted to rise from approximately 6.7% to
of the energy mix by 2030.
Mumbai Offshore, Krishna-Godavari, Assam and Cambay are all identified as major natural-gas basins in India.
JHBDPL
is associated with the Pradhan Mantri Urja Ganga gas-pipeline project.

secs.t: Water, marine and forest resources → places

x: Godavari, Krishna and Pennar are the major basins, while Vamsadhara and Nagavali occur in the north.
Andhra Pradesh has 30,084.96 sq km of forest cover, which accounts for 23.59% of the State’s area.
Red sanders (Pterocarpus santalinus) is endemic to the Seshachalam, Palakonda and Lankamalla hills of Rayalaseema.
The Girijan Cooperative Corporation, headquartered at Visakhapatnam, buys minor forest produce from tribals at fair prices.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Planned manganese processing clusters are associated with Vizianagaram, while port-based mineral processing is planned along the Andhra Pradesh coast.
Swarnagiri gold mine was opened in Andhra Pradesh during June–July 2026, while the Meghalaya Assembly opposed uranium mining.
Bauxite mining in the Eastern Ghats raises ecological concerns and issues relating to PVTG rights under the Forest Conservation Act and Forest Rights Act.

rows.title: Climatic change and climatic regions - world, India and Andhra Pradesh

secs.t: Climatologists → classification schemes and regions

x: Trewartha modified Koeppen's temperature-rainfall approach and made it simpler for application to India.
Trewartha's Caw corresponds broadly to Koeppen's
Cwg
for the Ganga plain, both indicating a humid subtropical or monsoonal climate with dry winter.
Thornthwaite used precipitation effectiveness expressed through moisture conditions and thermal efficiency represented by potential evapotranspiration.

secs.t: Climate of AP — type, latitude and climatic regions → districts

x: Andhra Pradesh is classified as Aw, the tropical wet and dry or savannah climate.
Andhra Pradesh has a tropical monsoon climate and lies approximately between 12°41'N and 19°07'N.
The humid coast has high humidity and heavy rain; the deltaic region is fertile and river-fed; Rayalaseema is semi-arid; and the hills have cool micro-climates with local rain.

secs.t: AP rainfall and temperature → highest, lowest and agro-climatic zones

x: Rainfall is highest in the Sileru and Sabari valleys and decreases towards the drier Rayalaseema region.
The Hagari valley receives less than 51 cm of rainfall and represents the lowest-rainfall zone.
Rayalaseema lies in the rain-shadow of the south-west monsoon and receives its peak rainfall in October-November from the north-east monsoon.

secs.t: Climate change data — India and world

x: 2024 was India's warmest year since 1901 and recorded 446 heatwave days, the highest number since 2000.
2025 was about 1.43°C above pre-industrial levels, 2015-2025 were the eleven warmest years, and Himalayan heavy rainfall rose by about 50% since the 1950s.
The forecast of a below-normal 2026 monsoon for most of Andhra Pradesh cited
El Nino
as a contributing factor.

secs.t: Climate change impacts on AP — coast, deltas, heat and rainfall

x: The erosion at Uppada near Kakinada and along the Krishna coast is linked to rising seas and cyclonic waves.
The Godavari delta is sinking, and the rate of land subsidence exceeds the regional rise in sea level.
The projection indicates possible excess south-west monsoon rainfall in Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu and warming above 1°C in around 40 coastal districts by 2040.

secs.t: Climate action plans — NAPCC, SAPCCs and AP SAPCC 2025-30

x: The eight NAPCC missions are Solar, Enhanced Energy Efficiency, Sustainable Habitat, Water, Himalayan Ecosystem, Green India, Sustainable Agriculture and Strategic Knowledge.
Adaptation spending was 5.6% of GDP in FY 2022, while SAPCCs moved from mitigation plans during 2010–15 to district-level, risk-based adaptation planning from 2020 onwards.
Renewables to 40% of the mix, 120 GW of RE projects and two green hydrogen hubs of 60 MW are among the eight measures.

Population density is the number of persons living per unit area, generally expressed per square kilometre.
The required proportion of male workers engaged outside agriculture is at least 75 percent, not 50 percent.

, often described as the explosion decade in the relevant classification.

17.5 per cent
of the world's population; UN WPP 2024 now puts it at 17.7 per cent.

31.1 per cent
of India's population in Census 2011, amounting to about 37.71 crore persons.

The 60-plus population is projected to increase from about 100 million in 2011 to
230 million
by 2036, or about one in seven Indians.

The 2011 order was Uttar Pradesh (16.49%),

(9.29%), Bihar (8.58%), West Bengal (7.55%) and undivided Andhra Pradesh (7.00%).

secs.t: Thinkers and books → population theories

x: Exam angle: UPPSC 2024 asked the Malthusian blanks (geometric, arithmetic).
Paul Ehrlich
wrote The Population Bomb in 1968 and warned of famine resulting from overpopulation.

Warren Thompson is associated with demographic transition theory, Frank Notestein with its formal three-stage formulation, Edwin Cannan with optimum population, and Paul Ehrlich with The Population Bomb.

secs.t: Terms → meaning — transition, dividend, TFR — Demographic transition stages

x: Stage 2 is characterised by high but declining death rates, high birth rates and population explosion; India during 1951–81 is an example.
India overall is placed in Stage 3, characterised by falling birth rates, low death rates and slowing growth.
The sequence is high stationary, early expanding, late expanding, low stationary and declining.

secs.t: Terms → meaning — transition, dividend, TFR — Terms

x: Exam angle: the age group (15-64) and the "rise in share of working people" definition are the most-asked points.
Demographic dividend can operate through greater labour supply, higher savings and investment, a lower dependency ratio and the release of human capital.
AP's median age is 32.5 against India's 28, its under-14 share is projected to fall from 25% (2011) to 15% (2036), and its 60+ share to rise from about 10% to 19% (2036) and 23% (2047).

secs.t: Data — demographic history and India's dividend window — Demographic history

x: The British period was marked by high birth and death rates, frequent famines and epidemics, and generally poor demographic conditions.
In 1951, overall literacy was 18.33%, with male literacy at 27.2% and female literacy at 8.9%.
Population-control efforts were continued during the Sixth, Seventh and Eighth Plans.
Population declined during 1911-21; after 1921 it grew continuously, so 1921 is called the 'great divide'.

secs.t: Data — demographic history and India's dividend window — Dividend window estimates

x: India's demographic dividend window is projected to span five decades, from
The workforce is projected to rise from 833.8 million in 2021 to a peak of 1,009 million in 2041, then decline to 998.1 million by 2051.
The 15–59 workforce is projected to peak in 2041; the demographic dividend window is expected to close after that point.

secs.t: TFR — NFHS and SRS values, states above and below replacement — National values

x: NFHS-6 reported an overall TFR of 2.0, an urban TFR of 1.6, and 31 of 36 States/UTs below the replacement level.
Andaman and Nicobar Islands recorded the lowest TFR at 0.9, while Bihar recorded the highest at 2.7 in NFHS-6.
All three statements are correct according to the SRS 2024 figures specified: TFR was below 2.1 for the fifth straight year, six states were above 2.1, and Delhi recorded 1.2.

each had a stated TFR of 1.3.

recorded the highest TFR in SRS 2021, at 3.0.

of married women in NFHS-5, compared with 36% in NFHS-4.
Clinical Outreach Teams work in 146 districts and are paired with wage-loss compensation for sterilisation acceptors.

70 basis points
Kerala and Tamil Nadu are ageing fastest, 18.7% of elderly women live alone, 78% lack pension cover and 70% depend on others.
Around 2020, India's median age was about 28, compared with 37 in China and the United States, 45 in Japan and up to 49 in Western Europe.

secs.t: Andhra Pradesh — low fertility, ageing and Population Management Policy

x: The February 2026 policy shifts the emphasis from population control to managing ageing and deriving benefits from the demographic dividend.
Andhra Pradesh had a TFR of 1.5, a demographic goal of 1.8 and a contraceptive prevalence rate of 71.1% against India’s 66.7%.

x: Southern States that reduced fertility face concerns about
lower tax devolution and fewer seats after delimitation
China, Japan and South Korea

secs.t: Terms → meaning — sex ratio, CSR, SRB, "missing women"

x: The biological norm is about
105 boys per 100 girls
, equivalent to roughly 950 girls per 1,000 boys at birth.
All three statements describe the normal biological pattern: more boys are born, male child mortality is naturally higher, and the corresponding ratio is about 950 girls per 1,000 boys.
Nobel laureate
Amartya Sen
introduced the concept of ‘missing women’ in 1990 to describe the demographic deficit of women, particularly in Asia.

secs.t: National trend — sex ratio and child sex ratio, 1901 to 2011

x: India's child sex ratio fell from 976 (1961) through 964 (1971), 962 (1981) and 945 (1991) to 927 (2001), and to about 918-919 in 2011 (provisional 914).
India’s child sex ratio was 927 in 2001; the 2011 figure was reported as 918 or 919 depending on the source, while 914 was the provisional figure.

secs.t: States and UTs → highest and lowest

x: Exam angle: match-the-state-with-value questions; memorise the four values above plus Kerala and Haryana.

Nagaland and Lakshadweep jointly
recorded the lowest CRS 2024 sex ratio at birth, at 865 each.

secs.t: Groups → sex ratio — religion, caste, tribe, rural-urban

fewer male births
Son preference, female foeticide, neglect of girls, maternal mortality and male-selective migration are identified causes; equal treatment of girls is not a cause of adverse sex-ratio trends.

reverse the declining child sex ratio
through multi-sectoral action.

, or 72.98% when expressed more precisely.

x: PLFS is a sample survey: it uses the same 7+ definition of literacy as the Census, but different samples, so its rates are not directly comparable with Census figures.
The figures were 67.35% in 2011 and 71.40% in PLFS 2025, Andhra Pradesh remained below India, and the widest gap was in the tribal ASR district.

rows.title: India - occupational structure: main and marginal workers, work participation rate, cultivators and agricultural labourers
sub: Group-II S2-53: Occupational structure and work participation - India and Andhra Pradesh

secs.t: Terms → meaning — worker categories, Census Town, PLFS indicators — Census worker categories

x: The Census Town criteria are population of 5,000 or more, 75 per cent or more of male main workers in non-agricultural activities, and population density of at least 400 persons per sq km.
The Census Town criteria remained unchanged since 1981 and were retained for
Census 2027
The Census categories include students, household-duty persons, dependants, pensioners, rentiers, beggars or vagrants and others.

secs.t: Terms → meaning — worker categories, Census Town, PLFS indicators — PLFS indicators

x: Exam angle: WPR's denominator is total population; LFPR's includes the unemployed.
Headline PLFS rates are generally reported for
persons aged 15 years and above
, unless the question specifies another age range.
The working-age group aged 15–59 rose to 66.4% of the population, while the 0–14 age group declined to 24%.

secs.t: Terms → meaning — worker categories, Census Town, PLFS indicators — Activity status

x: Under UPSS, a person is considered employed if he or she worked for at least 30 days in the year.
CDS records the activity status
for each day of the reference week
Usual status uses a reference period of 365 days.
Claudia Goldin
's U-curve says women's work participation first falls as an economy develops and then rises.

secs.t: Census 2011 workforce data — categories, trend and states — India shares (Census 2011)

x: India had 4,818.89 lakh workers; main workers constituted 75.2 per cent.
Other workers
made up 41.6% of all workers in Census 2011, more than agricultural labourers (30.0%), cultivators (24.6%) and household industry workers (3.8%).
There were 7,288.27 lakh non-workers in 2011, amounting to about 60% of the population.

secs.t: Census 2011 workforce data — categories, trend and states — Trend and the 2011 shift

x: Agriculture’s share of workers declined from 58.2% in 2001 to 54.6% in 2011, while the secondary and tertiary shares increased.
Scheduled Castes are described as being concentrated largely among marginal farmers and landless agricultural labourers.
Both statements are true, and the greater need for manual labour in subsistence-based activities explains the relatively higher WPR in these regions.

secs.t: PLFS data — sectoral distribution, LFPR, WPR and unemployment

x: For July–September 2025, agriculture accounted for 42.4% of total employment, self-employment 55.8%, and casual labour 18.9%.
The youth unemployment rate for persons aged 15–29 was
9.9 per cent
in annual PLFS 2025.
The annual PLFS 2025 figures were 59% for LFPR, 57% for WPR and approximately 3% for unemployment rate.

secs.t: Female work participation — trend, causes and feminisation

x: Men’s out-migration
has increased women’s participation in farm work, even though women hold only 12.8% of operational holdings.
Mechanisation, greater participation of girls in education, lack of flexible hours, workplace distance, safety concerns and family duties have contributed to low female work participation.
MGNREGS
was cited as one reason for the higher female work participation rate in rural areas.

secs.t: Andhra Pradesh — occupational structure, WPR and districts — AP shares (Census 2011)

x: Dividing 230.81 lakh workers by 495.77 lakh population gives an approximate WPR of
, higher than the all-India rate.
Agricultural labourers
formed 47.9% of all workers in Andhra Pradesh, followed by other workers at 34.8%.
Agricultural labourers constituted the largest component of Andhra Pradesh’s main workforce, numbering
86.12 lakh
, or about 45% of its main workers.

secs.t: Andhra Pradesh — occupational structure, WPR and districts — Districts

x: Chittoor had the highest cultivator share and West Godavari the highest agricultural-labourer share.

secs.t: Andhra Pradesh — occupational structure, WPR and districts — WPR and LFPR

x: Female work participation was 39.6% in rural areas and 22.8% in urban areas, making the rural rate higher by 16.8 percentage points.
AP's female LFPR (PLFS 2023-24) is 35.8%, above India's 31.7%, yet the WPR of urban young women (15-29) in AP is only 15.9%, the lowest of any group.

secs.t: Employment Acts and programmes — MGNREGA, PMEGP, NAPS

x: MGNREGA was launched on 2 February 2006 at Bandlapalli in Anantapur, Andhra Pradesh.
MGNREGA provides for up to
100 days
of wage work per rural household per year.
The cited combination was Direct Benefit Transfer, PMGKY and more than 10 lakh Self-Help Groups.
PMEGP was launched in 2008 by merging the Prime Minister’s Rozgar Yojana and the Rural Employment Generation Programme.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The one-hour CWS criterion can classify a person as employed even when work is insufficient, thereby hiding underemployment.
A lower unemployment rate may reflect
distress entry into low-productivity work
rather than the creation of decent or secure employment.
Andhra Pradesh’s LFPR is 47.5%; the rural rate is 50.1% and the urban rate is 41.3%.

rows.title: India - Scheduled Caste population: distribution and concentration

secs.t: SC population data — India and Andhra Pradesh

x: The Scheduled Caste population included about 1,035.35 lakh males and 978.43 lakh females, giving an approximate sex ratio of 945 females per 1,000 males.
In 2011, approximately 76% of Scheduled Castes lived in rural areas and 24% in urban areas; their shares were about 18.5% of the rural population and 12.6% of the urban population.
The Scheduled Caste population of Andhra Pradesh rose from 32.73 lakh in 1971 to
84.69 lakh

secs.t: States, UTs and districts → SC number, share and concentration

x: The 83rd Amendment of 2000 removed the need for Scheduled Caste reservation in Arunachal Pradesh panchayats because the State is wholly tribal.
SCs are not notified in Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep.
Scheduled Castes are relatively dense in fertile alluvial plains such as Punjab, the Ganga plain, West Bengal and coastal deltas, where settled farming historically used landless labour.

secs.t: Acts, amendments and rules on SC status

x: Scheduled Caste status is available to Hindus, Sikhs and Buddhists.

secs.t: Socio-economic profile of SCs — issues vs national average

x: Scheduled Caste unemployment was 5.5% against 5% nationally, while SC infant mortality was 44 against 32.
Scheduled Castes are predominantly associated with marginal farming and landless agricultural labour.
The enrolment shares were OBC 49%, General 27%, Scheduled Caste 17% and Scheduled Tribe 10%.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Census 2027 is described as the first enumeration of all castes in independent India, rather than an enumeration limited to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
A post-2026 delimitation may re-fix Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe reserved seats according to new Census shares, creating a fear of seat loss among southern States.
