rows.title: India - Scheduled Tribe population: distribution, major tribes and tribal regions
sub: Group-II S2-59: Tribal groups of India - distribution and characteristics

secs.t: ST population — Census 2011 data and state extremes

x: About 89.97 per cent of the Scheduled Tribe population was rural, and its sex ratio was 990 females per 1,000 males.
The literacy rate among Scheduled Tribes was about 59 per cent, compared with about
73 per cent
for the country as a whole.
The latest figure cited is 705 notified Scheduled Tribe groups in 30 States and Union Territories.
Punjab
, Haryana, Delhi, Chandigarh and Puducherry have no notified Scheduled Tribe population.

secs.t: Largest tribes and FIRSTs — rank, size, firsts

x: The Census 2011 count of about 1.7 crore out of roughly 10.4 crore STs is closer to 16%; the 38% figure appears in some sources but is not consistent with that Census calculation.
Bharia
of Madhya Pradesh were the first PVTG to receive habitat rights, followed by Kamar and Baiga of Chhattisgarh.

secs.t: Articles, Schedules and ST Orders → provisions — Articles → provision

x: The Fifth Schedule provides for the Governor's special powers and a Tribes Advisory Council in relation to Scheduled Areas.
Article 244(2)
applies the Sixth Schedule provisions concerning autonomous districts to Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.
The Fifth Schedule provides for a Tribes Advisory Council of up to 20 members, about three-fourths of whom are ST members of the State Legislative Assembly.

secs.t: Articles, Schedules and ST Orders → provisions — Tribal welfare minister - Article 164(1) states

x: The
94th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2006
made the relevant changes.
The States specified are
Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha
The Pahari ethnic group and Paddari tribe were included in 2024, while Sippis were among the communities added in 1991.
A Group of Ministers made the proposal.

secs.t: Committees and commissions on STs → chair and mandate

x: Exam angle: APPSC-G2 2025 asked the chair of the 2013 high-level committee - Virginius Xaxa.
The Virginius Xaxa Committee, whose report concerned 2013–14, suggested measures including
agro-based training institutions, labour-intensive processing, organic farming and eco-forestry

Verrier Elwin dealt with Multi-Purpose Tribal Development Blocks; Dhebar examined tribal conditions and land alienation; Lokur dealt with ST criteria; and Dilip Singh Bhuria was associated with PESA 1996.
The Lokur criteria include primitive traits, distinctive culture, geographical isolation, shyness of contact with the community at large and backwardness.

secs.t: PVTGs — criteria, timeline, state count and measures

x: Great Andamanese are from the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Chenchu from Andhra Pradesh, Toda from Tamil Nadu and Baiga from Madhya Pradesh.
Great Andamanese, Jarawa, Onge and Sentinelese are classified as Negrito groups, whereas Shompen is classified as Mongoloid.
The four PVTG criteria are pre-agricultural technology, low literacy, economic backwardness and a declining or stagnant population, so the first three options are criteria.

secs.t: Tribal zones → tribes and odd one out

x: The western group includes Bhil, Mina and Warli; the southern group includes Chenchu, Koya and Konda Reddi; island groups include Jarawa, Onge and Shompen; and Khasi, Garo and Naga belong to the North-East.
Muria and Maria are Gond sub-groups associated with the Bastar region, and Muria is known for the ghotul youth dormitory.
Gond, Baiga and Muria are associated with central or middle India, whereas
Kadar
is a southern tribe of the Anamalai Hills.

secs.t: Tribes → State / UT and habitat

x: Exam angle: the APPSC 2023 match was Gaddis-HP, Jarawas-A&N, Santhals-Jharkhand, Bhutias-Sikkim. Jarawa and Onge = A&N.
Exam angle: 4-pair matching of tribe with state, and "odd one out" by region.
Santhals are linked with Santhal Parganas, Gonds with Gondwana and Bastar, Bhils with the Aravalli-Vindhya-Satpura belt, and Todas with the Nilgiris.
Changpas inhabit the Changthang plateau of Ladakh, practise nomadic pastoralism involving pashmina goats and yaks, and have ST recognition since 1989.

Gaddis are transhumant shepherds of Bharmour (Chamba) in Himachal Pradesh; Jarawas live in the Andaman forests; Santhals are mainly in Jharkhand (Santhal Parganas); Bhutias are one of Sikkim's four STs with Lepcha, Limbu and Tamang.

secs.t: Cultural markers and economic types → tribe

x: Raj, Madia and Dhurve are identified as sub-groups of the
Gond
tribe.
Niyam Raja and the Niyamgiri festival are associated with the
Dongria Kondh
The Munda are associated with the Magha/Ba festival and sasandiri burial stones.
The Konyak Naga were the last to practise head-hunting; the Tangkhul Naga are known for Longpi pottery.

secs.t: Tribal languages → family and preservation initiatives

x: Bhili belongs to the Indo-European group.
Adi Vaani covers Bhili, Gondi, Mundari and Santali, not Kurukh.
Dictionaries are being compiled for the endangered
Mavila and Malaveduvan
languages of Kerala.
Santali entered the Eighth Schedule through the 92nd Amendment, 2003, and is written in Ol Chiki.

secs.t: Schemes and Acts for STs → key facts

x: The EMRS norm is one school in every block with
more than 50% ST population and at least 20,000 tribal persons
PMJVM is implemented by TRIFED and uses Van Dhan Vikas Kendras for
Minor Forest Produce
-related activities.
PM-JANMAN (Nov 2023, 2023-24 to 2025-26) has a total outlay of
Rs 24,104 crore
, of which the Centre's share is Rs 15,336 crore, so 15,336 is only the central share.

secs.t: STs in Andhra Pradesh — data and habitat

x: In Andhra Pradesh, tribal settlements are concentrated in the Eastern Ghats, the north coastal hill tracts, the Godavari basin and the Nallamala belt.
The Scheduled Caste population was 84.69 lakh, constituting 17.08% of the population of the 13-district Andhra Pradesh of 2011.
The Scheduled Tribe population was 27.39 lakh, constituting 5.53% of Andhra Pradesh’s population.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The debate concerns competing Jain and Santhal claims over the religious significance of Parasnath and Marang Buru.
The Scheduled Areas of Andhra Pradesh cover 16,267.63 square kilometres, amount to 10.15 percent of the State's area and extend across five districts.
The Supreme Court held that the Hindu Succession Act does not apply to notified Scheduled Tribes.

rows.title: India - rural and urban components; level of urbanisation and its regional pattern

secs.t: Rural and urban components — Census data and FIRSTs

x: India had 6,40,867 villages, of which 5,97,608, or about 93.2%, were inhabited.
About
83.3 crore
people lived in rural India in 2011.
During
, urban India added more people than rural India for the first time since Independence.
7,935 towns in 2011 = 4,041 statutory + 3,894 census towns.

secs.t: Components and drivers of urban growth

x: Urban growth occurs through natural increase, rural-to-urban migration, reclassification of settlements and expansion of town boundaries to include villages.
Industrialisation, trade and commerce, better health and education
, and transport links attract people towards cities.
A failed monsoon can reduce rural employment and push people to seek livelihoods in cities, making it a
push factor

secs.t: Regions and AP districts → level of urbanisation

x: Mizoram
is identified as the north-eastern exception, being relatively more urbanised than the general regional pattern.
The southern and western group of relatively more urbanised States includes
Goa, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Maharashtra and Gujarat
Low urbanisation is associated with the stagnant middle and lower Ganga plains, Telangana, unirrigated western Rajasthan, north-eastern tribal hills and flood-prone peninsular tracts.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The 16th Finance Commission projected 41% urbanisation by 2031, raised the urban bodies' share of local grants from 36% to 45%, and the 41% projection is lower than the EAC-PM satellite-based 2015 estimate of 63%.
The binary rural–urban definition can leave fast-urbanising areas under panchayats, where finances may be weak.

rows.title: Racial groups of India - Risley and Guha classifications
sub: Group-II S2-58: Racial groups of India - classifications of Risley and Guha

secs.t: Basis of racial classification — terms and indices

x: Platyrrhine
refers to a broad nose with a nasal index of 85 or above.
Topinard classified a stature of 170 cm or more as tall and a stature under 160 cm as small.
For a living head, a cephalic index of 82 and above is
brachycephalic
(round-headed), 77-81.99 is mesocephalic and 76.99 and below is dolichocephalic (long-headed), so 83 is brachycephalic.

secs.t: Racial types → diagnostic traits

x: Yellow complexion, oblique eyes, high cheek bones, sparse hair and medium height are characteristic descriptions associated with the
Mongoloid
type.
The Negrito type is described by dark skin, woolly or frizzy hair, short stature and a broad flat nose.
Proto-Australoids have dark skin and wavy hair; Nordic people are tall and fair; and Risley's Dravidian type has a long head, broad nose and dark complexion.

secs.t: Scholars → classifications and statements

x: Eickstedt proposed the four main groups
Weddid, Melanid, Indid and Mongolid
on physical and regional criteria.
S.S. Sarkar used the
cephalic index
and identified six ethnic elements, including dolichocephals and others.
Griffith Taylor's theory holds that primitive races are pushed to peripheral areas, with the Andaman Islands cited as an example.

secs.t: Risley's seven types → region

x: Risley used ‘Dravidian’ for
South India and Chota Nagpur
Punjab, Rajasthan and Kashmir were associated with the Indo-Aryan type.
Paniyans and Santals are cited as representative examples of the
Dravidian
type in Risley's classification.

secs.t: Guha's six racial groups → region and peoples

x: The Negrito type is associated mainly with the Andaman Islands and traces in the southern hills.
Negrito corresponds to the Andaman communities; Proto-Australoid to Santhal, Bhil, Chenchu, Munda and Ho; Mongoloid to the Himalayan and north-eastern peoples; and Nordic to north-western India.
Sema Nagas and Lepchas are examples of Palaeo-Mongoloid, while Tibetans of Sikkim represent Tibeto-Mongoloid.

secs.t: Tribal groups and regions → racial element

x: The
Santhal
is the standard example of a Central Indian tribe associated with the Proto-Australoid racial element.
The Chenchus of the Nallamala region are classified as
Proto-Australoid
South Indian tribal groups are described as having a Proto-Australoid base, with a Negrito strain among certain hill foragers; Risley classified the Paniyan as Dravidian.

secs.t: Institutions → location — Anthropological Survey of India

x: AnSI was founded at Varanasi in 1945 and moved to Kolkata in 1948.
AnSI undertakes research and documentation in physical and cultural anthropology, including the study of communities.
It is cited as a reference for caste and DNT enumeration.
Jagdalpur
is a sub-regional centre, not one of the seven regional centres.

secs.t: Criticism of race classification and genetic studies

x: Modern evidence shows that humans share over 99% of their genetic material and all belong to Homo sapiens, making rigid racial divisions scientifically subjective.
The 2009 genetic research framework describes most Indians as having mixed ANI and ASI ancestry; the abbreviations mean Ancestral North Indians and Ancestral South Indians.
The study found differences in
gut microbiomes
, suggesting that environment rather than genes accounted for the observed difference.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Only Guha lists Negrito and Proto-Australoid separately.
India argues caste is not race and rejected the observations as 'politically motivated'.
The plea followed the killing of
Anjel Chakma
and concerned racial prejudice and slurs against people from the North-East.
The Rakhigarhi DNA findings showed no “Steppe Pastoralist” gene, challenging certain Aryan-invasion interpretations.

rows.title: Religious composition of India - distribution and change over decades
sub: Group-II S2-61: Religious groups of India and Andhra Pradesh - composition and distribution

secs.t: Religious composition — Census 2011 data and categories

x: Exam angle: match community to its share (Sikhs 1.7, Christians 2.3, Buddhists 0.7, Jains 0.4).
Exam angle: absolute Christian population (about 2.8 crore / 28 million), highest-growth religion (Islam), matching religion to % share, ascending/descending order.
The six major religions, ORP, Religion Not Stated and the newly added No Religion option were separately recognised in the stated Census classification.

secs.t: Change over decades — growth rates and share shifts

x: Exam angle: "highest growth rate" = Islam. Jains are the slowest-growing community.
The Hindu share has slowly declined, the Muslim share has steadily risen, and the Sikh and Buddhist shares have dipped over the long run.
Muslims
grew 24.6% in 2001-11, the highest and the only community faster than the national rate (APPSC 2025 key).

secs.t: Sex ratio and literacy by religion — highest and lowest

x: Exam angle: "lowest sex ratio" (Sikh) and "highest literacy" (Jain) are the recurring one-liners.
The literacy ranking was Jain, Christian, Buddhist, Sikh, Hindu and Muslim, in descending order.
The order was Christians (1,023), Buddhists (965), Jains (954), Muslims (951), Hindus (939) and Sikhs (903).
The national average sex ratio in 2011 was 943.

secs.t: Religion → States and concentration areas

x: Exam angle: "largest number of Buddhists" = Maharashtra. Map questions pair NE hills with Christians and Ladakh/Sikkim with Buddhists.
Buddhist share is highest in Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh; Punjab is the only Sikh-majority State; and Jain share is highest in Maharashtra, Delhi and Gujarat.
Christians are the largest single religious group in Arunachal Pradesh, but they constitute only about 30 percent and therefore do not form a majority.
The fuller eight-unit list is
Lakshadweep, Mizoram, Nagaland, Meghalaya, Jammu and Kashmir, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur and Punjab

secs.t: Explaining the distribution — persons, events and factors

x: Maharashtra's large Buddhist population is linked to Dr B. R.
Ambedkar's mass conversion at Nagpur in 1956
Muslims often live in majority neighbourhoods because of security concerns, cultural preservation and rental discrimination.
The rise is attributed to
poorer economic status and lower female education
Islam arrived with Arab merchants and later spread through the Turkish Sultanate, Mughals and Sufis.

secs.t: Religious composition of Andhra Pradesh

x: All three statements correctly describe the minority population of Andhra Pradesh in APSES 2024–25: it is mostly urban, has a large Below-Poverty-Line segment and has a low share in economic support schemes.
The highest Muslim shares in Andhra Pradesh are associated with the Rayalaseema districts of
Kurnool, YSR Kadapa and Anantapur

secs.t: Schemes, Acts and bodies for minorities — Central schemes

x: Pre-matric covers Classes IX-X, Post-matric has a Rs 2.5 lakh income ceiling, and Merit-cum-Means (2007) covers professional/technical UG-PG.
PMJVK is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme, supports infrastructure in Minority Concentration Areas and, after revision from 2022-23, covers all districts including 112 Aspirational Districts.
The stated audit requirement applies to waqfs earning over ₹1 lakh; a mandatory audit of every waqf irrespective of income is not specified.

secs.t: Schemes, Acts and bodies for minorities — AP minority welfare

x: The Minorities Finance Corporation corresponds to post-matric RTF, the Christian Corporation to ₹150.92 crore and pilgrimage assistance, the Waqf Board to payments to Imams and Mouzzans, and the Haj Committee to 1,652 pilgrims.
The AP State Urdu Academy provides free computer training in 36 centres and CEDM coaching involving ₹5 crore.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Andhra Pradesh has the stated State Minorities Commission, separate Minorities and Christian Minorities Finance Corporations and a Waqf Board; its Christian population is 6.82 lakh and Urdu is the second official language.
The debates include the demography narrative in relation to fertility data and the fact that religious minorities constitute only about 5% of higher-judiciary appointees.

The President released digital editions of the Constitution in Santhali; first-time editions were also produced in Kokborok and Kashmiri.

Persian was the official language and Telugu was spoken by the people

The Coastal dialect region, especially the Krishna-Godavari area, is regarded as the base of standard Telugu.

Coastal, Rayalaseema, Kalinga/Uttarandhra and Telangana

Youth voices on multilingual education

Bhasha Sangam was a 2018 initiative under
Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat
Bhasha Sangam encouraged school students to learn simple sentences in all 22 scheduled languages.

The three-language formula

secs.t: Migration — definitions and types

A
refugee
is forced to leave and cannot return because of fear of persecution based on race, religion, nationality or social or political group.
Return migration means going back to the previous place after the cause that led to migration has ended.

secs.t: Migration streams → where they dominate

x: Rural-to-urban migration is dominated by males moving for employment and is an important force driving urbanisation.
Women dominate intra-state rural-to-rural movements, particularly those associated with marriage, while men dominate inter-state rural-to-urban movements for work.
For inter-state female migrants by last residence in 2011, the migration pattern began with the
urban-to-urban
stream.

secs.t: Causes of migration — push and pull factors, by gender

x: Low farm productivity is a push factor operating at the area of origin.
Political instability, not political stability, is a push factor.
All three conditions encourage rural-to-urban migration: cities generate labour demand, regional development is uneven, and rural areas may offer few employment opportunities.
Information networks associated with groups such as Keralites and Sikhs can influence migration.

secs.t: Migration theories and terms → proponent

x: Everett S. Lee
propounded the push-pull theory in his 1966 work, “A Theory of Migration”.
Ravenstein is associated with the laws of migration, Zelinsky with the mobility transition model, Taylor with migration zone theory, and place utility with the desirability of a destination.
Net migration = in-migration minus out-migration.

secs.t: Migration data — Census 2011, PLFS, MoSPI survey

the first full migration survey since 2007–08
The earlier definition covered 1–6 months, whereas the revised definition covers 15 days–6 months.
455.8 million migrants by place of last residence, about 37.6% of 121 crore.

The India-UAE corridor is the fifth-largest global corridor and is dominated mainly by workers.

Large-scale migration can produce slums, ghettoisation and a socially divided or “double” city.

Contractors required licences, and migrant workers were entitled to displacement allowance and journey allowance.
The OSH Code covers workers who migrate on their own, provides for annual travel allowance and supports portability of PDS and social security.

x: ONORC gives NFSA ration portability anywhere.
E-Shram (2021) is a One-Stop-Solution linked to 15 central schemes, with a gig and platform worker module.

Rural distress, informal employment, lack of job security and rising LPG prices in 2026 were identified as factors associated with distress migration and return migration to villages.
The Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration was adopted at
Marrakech in December 2018

India received a record USD 135 billion in FY 2024–25, with an increasing contribution from skilled professionals in developed countries rather than mainly from West Asia.
India remained the top remittance recipient in 2024, receiving US$137 billion and being the only country to receive more than US$100 billion.

Seasonal labour leaves drought-prone Rayalaseema as well as the north-coastal districts of Andhra Pradesh.
Srikakulam fishermen migrate seasonally to
the Gujarat coast
The migration streams are Gulf migration and distress migration to Hyderabad, Bengaluru and Chennai from drought-prone Rayalaseema.

Migration is the main component of the rural-urban growth difference because
natural increase differs little between rural and urban areas

UN-Habitat released it at the World Urban Forum, Baku.

15) calls cities 'critical economic infrastructure'.

category extends from 0.550 to 0.699.

secs.t: Food crops → season, temperature, rainfall and soil

x: Wheat is a rabi crop requiring a cool growing season, about 50–75 cm rainfall and warm, sunny conditions during ripening.
Rice grows best under high humidity, temperatures above 25°C and rainfall exceeding 100 cm, or equivalent irrigation.
Rice is well suited to clayey or loamy soils, particularly the deltaic and coastal alluvium.
Millets are mostly kharif crops and are climate-resilient, low-input crops of dryland and rainfed tracts.

secs.t: Food crops → leading producing states

x: The stated order for leading pulse-producing states is Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh and Karnataka.
Rajasthan is the leading bajra-producing state, and bajra is suited to the driest conditions and sandy soils.
Rajasthan is the largest producer of bajra, while Karnataka leads in ragi.
West Bengal
is called the Rice Bowl of India and is the largest rice producer.

secs.t: Green Revolution — persons, inputs, phases and regions

x: Norman Borlaug is associated with HYV Mexican dwarf wheat and received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970.
The New Agricultural Strategy began in 1965 and combined HYV seeds, fertilisers, irrigation and minimum support price with the objective of foodgrain self-sufficiency.
The strategy relied on HYV seeds, fertilisers, assured irrigation and MSP, with foodgrain self-sufficiency as its objective.
Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh recorded the biggest gains, while rice gains were notable in the deltas of Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.

secs.t: Green Revolution — limitations and issues

north-western India

millets, pulses and oilseeds

The Golden Revolution is associated with

per farmer.

rows.title: Industrial location - factors and theories (Weber); world industrial regions

secs.t: Theorists → location theories

x: Alfred Weber’s 1909 least-cost theory considers the combined
transport, labour and agglomeration
costs.

Edgar Hoover dealt with transport-cost structure and terminal costs; Walter Isard proposed the substitution principle; August Losch developed the maximum-profit and market-area approach; and P. Sargant Florence introduced the Location Quotient.
Both statements are true, and the emphasis on transport-cost structure and terminal costs explains why ports and break-of-bulk points are favoured.

secs.t: Location terms → meaning

x: An MI greater than one indicates that localised raw materials weigh more than the finished product, favouring a raw-material-oriented location.

Footloose industries are generally light, high-value, low in transport cost and low in pollution, and are not tied to a raw material or fixed location, e.g. diamond cutting, electronics, software and watch-making.

secs.t: Iron and steel regions of the world → country

x: The Atlantic Coast iron and steel region, including Baltimore and Bethlehem, is in the
USA
Anshan is located in
Liaoning in north-east China
; Benxi is another important centre in the region.
Steel is weight-losing: about four tonnes of iron ore, coking coal, limestone and dolomite produce one tonne of steel.

x: India’s crude steel production is 168.4 MT, capacity is 220 MT and the target for 2030 is 300 MT.
Steel leadership has moved to China and India, while the older Western industrial regions of Ruhr, Lorraine and the US Rust Belt have declined.
The Asian Tigers are
South Korea, Taiwan, Singapore and Hong Kong
, recognised as newly industrialising economies.

rows.title: India - industrial regions and industrial belts; factors of localisation
sub: Group-II S2-39: Major industrial regions of India and factors of industrial location

secs.t: Factors of location and industry orientation — Factors

x: Market-based industries such as bakeries and soft-drink production locate near consumers because their products are
weight-gaining or fragile
The steel belt lies on the Chota Nagpur Plateau because the principal raw materials are weight-losing and are therefore advantageously processed near their source.
Iron and steel, sugar and cement are generally raw-material-oriented; aluminium is power-oriented; and software is market-oriented or footloose.

secs.t: Factors of location and industry orientation — Footloose industries

x: Footloose industries use light inputs, incur negligible transport costs and are not tightly tied to a particular raw-material source.
A pure raw material has no weight loss, so transport cost is the same whether raw material or product is moved; the plant is free to locate anywhere between source and market.

secs.t: Industrial regions → centres and specialisation

x: Mumbai-Pune has engineering, petrochemicals, IT, automobiles and pharma; Hugli has jute, engineering, paper and chemicals; Gujarat has petrochemicals, refining, textiles and diamonds; Chotanagpur ('Ruhr of India') has steel, coal, heavy engineering and power.

Bengaluru-Tamil Nadu is associated with IT and advanced industries; Visakhapatnam-Guntur with steel and petroleum-related industries; Gurugram-Delhi-Meerut with automobiles and electronics; and Kollam-Thiruvananthapuram with cashew, coir and rubber.

secs.t: Industrial centres → industry

x: Exam angle: UPPSC matching sets (Muri-aluminium, Gurgaon-automobiles, Vizag-shipbuilding, Panki-fertilisers; Aonla-fertilisers, Modinagar-rubber).
Muri is associated with aluminium, Aonla with fertilisers, Koyali with an oil refinery, and Singrauli with coal and thermal power.
Pithampur specialises in automobiles, Sivakasi in safety matches and fireworks, Renukoot in aluminium through HINDALCO, and Aonla in fertiliser production.

secs.t: Regional imbalance — policies and criticism

x: The 1956 Industrial Resolution and the Fourth Plan (1969–74) sought balanced regional growth, leading to the placement of these steel plants away from raw-material bases.
The main criticisms include inadequate location factors, shortages of skilled labour, expensive subsidies and political concentration.
The Economic Survey 2025–26 noted that many Indian clusters are too small and face regulatory rigidities, limiting their integration into global value chains.

secs.t: Industrial and defence corridors → states and nodes — National Industrial Corridor Programme

x: CBIC is associated with Japan through JICA, VCIC with ADB, AKIC with the Eastern DFC and NW-1, and BMEC with the United Kingdom.
The programme comprises 11 corridors; approval of 12 new industrial smart cities raised the project count to 20, and implementation involves NICDC and NICDIT.
The integrated East Coast Industrial Corridor proposed in Budget 2026-27 includes a node at
Durgapur
under the Purvodaya initiative.

secs.t: Industrial and defence corridors → states and nodes — VCIC in AP

x: The Uttar Pradesh corridor has six nodes, the Tamil Nadu corridor has five nodes, and the two together have investment commitments of ₹74,756 crore.
India’s first Defence Industrial Corridor was announced along the
Chennai-Bengaluru
stretch.

secs.t: SEZs, NIMZs and industrial parks — Acts and schemes

x: Budget 2026-27 gave a one-time permission to sell to the Domestic Tariff Area at concessional duty, capped as a share of exports, not duty-free unlimited sales.
NIMZs are conceived as large integrated townships, bigger than SEZs, and differ from them in governance, exit and fiscal rules.
All four statements correctly describe BHAVYA: 100 parks, ₹33,660 crore, the period FY 2026–27 to 2031–32, challenge-mode selection and operation by NICDC.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: ADB support associated with the Andhra Pradesh industrial corridors is
US$ 840 million
India has more than 4,500 mapped industrial parks; manufacturing contributes about 16–17% of GDP, with a target of 25% by 2047.
The Andhra Pradesh Industrial Infrastructure Corporation (
APIIC
) is the nodal agency and manages 571 industrial parks.

secs.t: Steel — production data, process mix and FIRSTs

x: Crude steel production in 2025–26 was
, representing a 10.7 percent increase and approximately 9 percent CAGR since 2021–22.
The process mix is 43% BF–BOF, 22% EAF and 35% induction furnace.
Induction furnaces are suitable for small batches and are energy-efficient; they can melt scrap or sponge iron in secondary steel production.

secs.t: Steel policy, raw materials and green steel

x: Domestic coking coal is high in ash
, which makes imports necessary despite domestic production.
The policy targets 300 MT capacity and 255 MT crude steel production by 2030–31, requiring 437 MT iron ore and 161 MT coking coal.
The Ministry of Steel has Rs 455 crore for green-hydrogen pilots in steel till 2029-30.

secs.t: Aluminium — companies and plants → location

x: Exam angle: "Muri - Chhattisgarh" is the wrong pair; Muri is in Jharkhand.
Because aluminium smelting consumes 14,000–15,000 kWh per tonne, smelters are located near hydel or captive thermal power sources rather than being governed solely by proximity to mines.
NALCO uses Panchpatmali bauxite; its refinery is at Damanjodi and its smelter and captive power plant are at Angul in Odisha.

secs.t: Copper, zinc and lead — mines and smelters → location

Hindustan Copper Limited
Malanjkhand is
India's largest open-pit copper mine
and is associated with Hindustan Copper Limited.
India's global reserve share is under 2 per cent, it imports copper concentrate on a net basis, and Chile is the leading country mentioned for copper reserves.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The draft notification proposes binding emission-intensity cuts for 255 iron and steel plants from FY 2026–27.
The stated Indian intensity exceeds the world average, the sector contributes 10–12 per cent of national CO2 emissions, and EU CBAM creates exposure for Indian steel.
The alternatives mentioned were Bailadila, Goa, Neyveli, Salem and Hospet.

secs.t: FIRST modern industrial units → place and year

Fort Gloster was the unsuccessful 1818 mill, while C. N. Davar established the first successful mill at Mumbai in 1854; the industry later dispersed to other regions.
The super-phosphate factory was established at Ranipet in 1906, the aircraft factory at Bengaluru in 1940, the paper mill at Serampore in 1812 and TISCO at Jamshedpur in 1907.
The correct order is Mumbai cotton mill (1854), Rishra jute mill (1855), Kanpur woollen mill (1876), and Madras cement plant (1904).

hydel power, cheap labour and local cotton
All five factors contribute to the UP–Bihar concentration: suitable alluvial soil, level land, cheap labour, a dense market and bagasse for boiler fuel.
Cement plants are located near limestone deposits because limestone is a major and bulky raw material in cement manufacture.
Forest- and bagasse-based paper mills are generally located near bamboo or softwood forests or sugarcane belts.

secs.t: Industry → raw materials and location factors — Fertilisers and petrochemicals — feedstock

x: The fertiliser industry uses
naphtha, natural gas, coal, rock phosphate, sulphur and gypsum
; steel slag and coke may also be used as by-products.
Western-coast locations facilitate the import of coking coal, reduce its inland transport burden and provide access to export markets.
Vizag steel draws its iron ore mainly from
Bailadila
in Chhattisgarh (a PYQ fact).

x: Nasik, Pune, Satara, Sangli, Kolhapur and Sholapur
are identified with Maharashtra's cooperative sugar mills.
Shakkarnagar at Bodhan in Nizamabad grew around the
Nizam Sugar Factory
The committee recommended
a 70:30 revenue-sharing formula and removal of the minimum-distance rule
The Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) is set by the Centre, and several States announce a higher State Advised Price (SAP).

secs.t: Industry → centres, belts and clusters — Cement

x: The 2026 order is Rajasthan first, then AP, Telangana, Gujarat, Chhattisgarh and TN (only older sources rank AP first by capacity).
Satna and Katni are in Madhya Pradesh, Chittoor in Andhra Pradesh, Nalgonda in Telangana, and Khilari and Chaibasa in Jharkhand.
The limestone-bearing rock systems of Kadapa and Kurnool make Rayalaseema an important cement hub.

secs.t: Industry → centres, belts and clusters — Fertiliser and petrochemical centres

x: Exam angle: APPSC 2023 matched Iron & Steel - Jamshedpur, Jute - Kolkata, Oil refinery - Barauni, ICF - Perambur.

Sindri and the Chota Nagpur steel towns (Jamshedpur, Rourkela, Durgapur, Bhilai) use steel by-products such as slag and coke; Neyveli, Tuticorin, Ennore, Alwaye and Kochi form the Tamil Nadu-Kerala group; and Nangal, Bhatinda and Panipat form the North-West group.

secs.t: Iron and steel plants → state, river, collaborating country, owner

Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited (

) operates the Visakhapatnam Steel Plant.

secs.t: Aluminium, copper, shipyards and rail units → location

NALCO (1981) is a Navratna under the Ministry of Mines with plants at Damanjodi and Angul.

secs.t: Data — ranks, capacity, output and shares — Jute

x: The sugar industry is India's second-largest agro-based industry, next only to cotton textiles.
India is the largest consumer, the second-largest producer after Brazil, and contributes about 19 per cent of world sugar output.
Grain now provides approximately three-fourths of ethanol production, although molasses remains an important sugar-industry feedstock.
Maharashtra
(~9.9 MT) led sugar output, ahead of Uttar Pradesh (~8.9 MT) and Karnataka (~4.7 MT).

secs.t: Data — ranks, capacity, output and shares — Cement

x: India's per capita cement consumption is approximately 290 kg, while the world average is about 540 kg.
India is the second-largest fertiliser consumer.

secs.t: Acts, policies, schemes and committees

x: The Act provides for
100% of foodgrains and 20% of sugar
to be packed in jute bags.
India announced the National Jute Policy in 2005.
JUTE-ICARE
promotes certified seed and microbial retting with SONA.

secs.t: Terms, by-products and industrial nicknames

x: Portland Pozzolana Cement uses fly ash from thermal power plants and slag from steel plants.
Coimbatore is known as the Manchester of South India.
Ahmedabad is popularly known as the
Manchester of India
Jamshedpur
is called Tatanagar and the Steel City of India; it is also known as the Pittsburgh of India.

secs.t: Changes — sugar's north-south shift and steel's coastal shift

x: Tropical cane in South India generally has higher sucrose content and yield.
The North has many private mills (Bihar mostly non-cooperative), while cooperative mills are strong in the South, especially Maharashtra.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The transition involves nine sectors, including cement, fertilisers, paper, textiles, petrochemicals and refining.
Chittivalasa and Nellimarla have had jute mills since the 1920s, and Rajahmundry is associated with the paper industry.
Electricity has the highest weight (about 31%).
India became a net steel importer during April–October of 2025–26.

BHEL at Bhopal produces

EGoS - NPG - Technical Support Unit.

The Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047 targets

of port capacity.

secs.t: Regulators and ministries → basis and function

x: Exam angle: "regulator of telecom and broadcasting" = TRAI (not Prasar Bharati, which is the broadcaster).
TDSAT came from the 2000 amendment of the TRAI Act and adjudicates disputes and appeals against TRAI orders.
Running Akashvani and Doordarshan
is a function of Prasar Bharati.
PIB, the Central Bureau of Communication and Publications Division are MIB media units.

secs.t: Postal network → PIN code, Digi PIN, APT and services

x: The PIN has 6 digits and first digit 9 is the Army Postal Service (1-8 are geographical zones).
Digi PIN is a 10-digit alphanumeric code intended for precise delivery and forms part of the Advanced Postal Technology platform.
The APT platform was built by CEPT, hosted on MeghRaj 2.0 cloud and piloted in Karnataka circle.

secs.t: Telecom milestones → year (FIRSTs, policies, Acts)

x: The correct order is 1882, 1975, 1984 and 1994: first telephone exchange, SITE, C-DOT and National Telecom Policy 1994.
MNP was introduced within a circle in 2011 and full nationwide portability began on 3 July 2015.
The National Digital Communications Policy 2018 addressed technologies including 5G, the Internet of Things and machine-to-machine communication.

secs.t: Telecom data, 5G and 6G, and terms

x: 5G covers 99.9 per cent of districts and has 40 crore users.
The four principles are Samaveshit, Viksit, Tvarit and Surakshit.
Sanchar Saathi and ASTR are tools used in relation to telecom fraud management.
5G Standalone is pure 5G and does not depend on a 4G core.
Teledensity was 86.76% in 2025-26 and the Bharat 6G Vision is for 2030.

secs.t: Transmission media and submarine cables → features and links

x: Exam angle: "fastest form of data transmission" = optical fibre.
Optical fibre uses total internal reflection, has low loss, resists electromagnetic interference and forms the backbone of modern internet and data connectivity.
Copper media carry electrical signals, have lower bandwidth than optical fibre, suffer loss over distance and are comparatively interference-prone.

secs.t: Digital connectivity schemes → year and provisions — BharatNet

x: BharatNet was earlier called NOFN, targets Gram Panchayat connectivity, is funded by USOF and uses the fibre infrastructure of BSNL, RailTel and PGCIL.
The Amended BharatNet Programme includes PPP implementation, a larger State role, 100 Mbps scalable to 1 Gbps per Gram Panchayat and an approved outlay of ₹1.39 lakh crore.

secs.t: Digital connectivity schemes → year and provisions — Other schemes → year

x: The Visakhapatnam Declaration extended NeSDA to Ladakh and the North-East with the objective of bridging the digital divide.
Digital access has been held to form part of the right to life and personal liberty under
Article 21
PM-WANI, or Wi-Fi Access Network Interface, enables
public Wi-Fi through Public Data Offices and aggregators
RailWire
is RailTel’s public Wi-Fi service at railway stations.

secs.t: Mass media → FIRSTs, dates and Acts

x: The Ministry of I&B regulates private TV channels and MSOs/cable operators under the Cable Television Networks (Regulation) Act, 1995, and it licenses and operationalises Community Radio Stations (it also auctions private FM channels).
The 2023 Act replaced the 1867 law, the Press Registrar General administers registration, the earlier office was RNI, and the Press Council Act dates from 1978.

secs.t: AP digital connectivity → APSFL, BharatNet and towers — data

x: The Memorandum of Cooperation for Amended BharatNet in Andhra Pradesh provides for
last-mile connectivity to 3,942 villages and broadband to every household within 18 months
The AP FiberNet tribal expansion was funded through the Universal Service Obligation Fund, or
USOF
, now known as Digital Bharat Nidhi.
The CM set a 100-day tower drive and discussed an undersea cable landing station plus data centres with Sunil Bharti Mittal.

The stated AP figures include 10,660 post offices, while APSFL provides triple-play internet, IPTV and voice services.

NH-16

The proposal to connect every port from Mulapeta to Krishnapatnam by National Highways is described as being on the
Gujarat model
The five Sagarmala pillars are port modernisation, port connectivity, port-led industrialisation, coastal community development, and coastal shipping/inland water transport.
The completed Narketpally-Addanki-Medarametla road (125 km, PPP) links NH-65 (Pune-Machilipatnam) with NH-16 (Chennai-Kolkata).

, comprising 45,433 km of State roads and 8,744 km of National Highways.

women and transgender persons

₹9,417 crore
. ₹10,134 crore refers to another reported railway allocation figure, while the other values relate to works or highway expenditure.

secs.t: Greenfield ports and Dugarajapatnam → capacity, progress and plans

145 MTPA by 2030 and 300 MTPA by 2047

x: Vijayawada (Gannavaram)
Airport has DIGI YATRA and a new terminal costing ₹408.06 crore.

x: Cochin International Airport

Vizhinjam in Kerala is India's first deep-water transhipment port and first semi-automated container port; it was inaugurated in May 2025.

x: Andhra Pradesh has three national industrial corridors, one major port, 17 non-major ports and NH-16, supporting its role as an east-coast gateway to South-East Asia.

US$20 billion
blue economy by 2035.
The identified challenges include logistics cost, lack of dedicated freight rail to clusters, water-short inland nodes, CBI-stalled ports and land-acquisition delays.

rows.title: International trade - patterns, trade blocs, chokepoints; India's export and import composition
sub: Group-II S2-46: Trade - India's foreign trade composition and direction; major ports

secs.t: Trade policy phases, Acts and missions → year — Phase / Act → year and key features

x: From 1950 to 1990, India followed import substitution through an inward-looking policy lasting approximately four decades.
The 1991 policy included two-step rupee devaluation, movement toward a price-based mechanism and eased import licensing.
FTP 2023 shifted from incentives to remission of duties and emphasized ease of exporting, e-initiatives and Districts as Export Hubs.

secs.t: Trade policy phases, Acts and missions → year — Terms → meaning

x: DGFT runs the Mission through Niryat Protsahan and Niryat Disha.
The framework permits invoicing and settlement in Indian rupees through
Special Rupee Vostro Accounts
, or SRVAs.
The mechanism seeks to reduce dollar dependence, internationalise the rupee and facilitate trade with sanctioned or embargoed partners.
Export promotion is outward-looking and pushes manufactured exports.

secs.t: India's trade and port data — value, balance, rank, cargo

x: India's merchandise exports reached
US$ 441.78 billion
in FY 2025–26, an all-time high and an increase of 0.93%.
India’s merchandise trade deficit rose to
US$333.2 billion
in FY 2025–26, from US$282.5 billion in FY 2024–25.
FY26 merchandise imports of US$775 bn (up from US$721.20 bn) were driven by a jump in
gold and silver

secs.t: Commodities → share, rank and leading exporter — India's top export items
Commodities → share, rank and leading exporter — Exports vs imports

x: Electronics
was India's third-largest export category in FY 2025, after engineering goods and petroleum products.
India's import dependence is about 88–89% for crude oil, 47–51% for natural gas and 26% for coal.
Refined petroleum products and gems and jewellery are important exports, while crude petroleum and gold and silver are important imports.
Bulk imports include petroleum, cereals and pulses,
edible oils
, sugar, fertilizer, metals and ores.

secs.t: Commodities → share, rank and leading exporter — India's rank in world markets

x: India is first in rice exports, third in pharmaceutical exports by volume and seventh in refined petroleum exports.
India is the world's largest rice exporter, accounting for about 40% of global rice trade.
Brazil
is not included in that list.
Brazil leads sugar exports and India is second.

secs.t: Countries → share in India's trade (direction of trade)

x: The order is United States of America (19.77%), United Arab Emirates (8.37%), United Kingdom (3.32%) and China (3.26%).
Crude imports rose from Libya, Egypt, Brazil, the United States and Brunei, while imports from Russia and Saudi Arabia fell.
After Independence, India’s trade shifted away from the UK and Western Europe towards the United States and later towards Asia, including China, the UAE and ASEAN.

secs.t: Trade agreements → partner, year and key facts — Count and coverage

x: The June 2026 count states that India had 15 FTAs covering 27 countries and was in talks with 42 more countries.
India's FTAs could cover approximately 75% of exports, but their actual utilisation is only around 20–30%.
India concluded nine FTAs covering 38 countries, providing zero-duty access to markets that account for about 70% of world GDP.

secs.t: Trade agreements → partner, year and key facts — Agreement → year → key facts

x: The CECPA with Mauritius was concluded in 2021, the CEPA with the UAE and ECTA with Australia in 2022, and the TEPA with EFTA in 2024.
SAPTA was signed in 1993, SAFTA in 2004, the India-ASEAN Trade in Goods Agreement in 2009, and the India-UAE CEPA in 2022.
The
India-UAE CEPA
, signed in 2022, provided duty-free access for 90% of Indian exports and exports rose by 12% in the first year.

secs.t: Trade blocs and WTO → members and outcomes

x: SAFTA includes the eight SAARC countries, including Bhutan, Afghanistan and Maldives.
NAMA-11 is a coalition of developing countries in the WTO dealing with
non-agricultural market access
; India, Brazil and South Africa are among its members.
RCEP includes the ten ASEAN states plus China, Japan, South Korea, Australia and New Zealand.

secs.t: Chokepoints and world seaports → location and key fact — Chokepoint → connects / location

x: The Suez Canal can shorten the Europe–Asia route by
up to 7,000 km
compared with the route around the Cape of Good Hope.
The SUMED pipeline runs across Egypt from Ain Sukhna to Sidi Kerir and transports Gulf oil to Europe.
The
Cape of Good Hope
at the southern tip of Africa provides the long alternative route when the Suez Canal or Red Sea is unavailable.

secs.t: Chokepoints and world seaports → location and key fact — 2026 disruptions

x: The Strait of Hormuz was reported closed in early March 2026 during the US–Israel war on Iran.
After the Houthis took Perim Island, traffic through both
Hormuz and Bab-el-Mandeb
was reported disrupted in September 2026.
Fujairah and Khor Fakkan are UAE ports located outside Hormuz and reportedly took extra Indian cargo in 2026.

secs.t: Major ports of India → state, coast and feature — Count and coastline

x: Vadhavan
, approved on 19 June 2024, is counted as the 13th major port along with the 12 operational major ports.
Vadhavan, a greenfield deep-draft port approved on 19 June 2024, is in Palghar, Maharashtra.
The 13 major ports are governed by the Major Port Authorities Act, while about 200 non-major ports are administered under State Maritime Boards.

secs.t: Major ports of India → state, coast and feature — Port → state, coast, feature

x: Exam angle: port → state matching (Haldia → West Bengal, APPSC-GS 2018) and "which is not a west-coast major port".

at Kandla is a tidal port in the Gulf of Kachchh and is associated with a Free Trade Zone and Asia’s first EPZ in 1965.
Haldia is part of the Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port (Kolkata-Haldia) on the Hooghly in
West Bengal

x: Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority (
JNPA
), also known as Nhava Sheva, is India’s largest container port and its first 100 per cent landlord major port.
Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port, comprising
Kolkata-Haldia
, is the oldest major port and the only riverine major port of India.
Paradip led dry bulk, Sikka led liquid bulk, Mundra led container cargo in the performance index, and JNPA was the leading container port.

secs.t: Port types and terms → meaning and examples

x: Visakhapatnam has both artificial-harbour characteristics and a landlocked location.
Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust (JNPT) functions as a decongestion or satellite port for Mumbai.
China-border trade through
Lipulekh, Shipki La and Nathu La
has been suspended since 2020.

secs.t: Causes and issues — east vs west coast ports, FTA criticism

x: The first two statements are correct reasons for the east coast having fewer natural harbours.
The west coast is submerged and indented, with deep water close to the shore.
The east coast has a wide and shallow continental shelf formed by the deltas of the Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri, making natural harbours less common.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Exports to the Gulf fell by about
in March 2026 as a result of the West Asia war.
India’s share of ASEAN’s imports fell from 3.42% to
after the FTAs, a point raised in debates about trade performance.
About
of Andhra Pradesh’s exports go to the RCEP and USMCA blocs together.

rows.title: Trade of Andhra Pradesh - exports, port-based trade, SEZs
sub: Group-II S2-47: Trade of Andhra Pradesh - exports, port-based trade and SEZs

secs.t: AP exports — rank, FIRSTs and share by item

x: Andhra Pradesh was the sixth largest exporting State in FY 2024-25 and shipped 824 commodities to 194 countries.
All four statements are correct for FY 2024-25: marine products ranked first with 43%, ores ranked first, coffee ranked second and spices ranked third.
The FY 2024-25 figures recorded tobacco at 67% and marine products at 43%, while the FY 2023-24 table recorded marine products at 40%.

secs.t: AP export items → district, destination and port

x: Andhra Pradesh accounts for about
of India's shrimp exports, particularly white-leg shrimp produced in West Godavari, Krishna and Nellore.
Andhra Pradesh's white-leg shrimp is sold chiefly to
the United States and the European Union
Vizag (Parawada Pharma City) is identified with pharmaceutical exports.
The Phase-I Visakhapatnam District Export Hub covers marine products, engineering goods and health services.

secs.t: AP policies → objectives and targets

x: APEX 2022–27 promotes global market access, logistics, competitiveness, institutions and district-to-port ecosystems;
exclusive dependence on domestic markets
is not its objective.
The policy targets Rs 30 lakh crore investment and US$ 10 billion FDI.
The special purpose vehicle
NSHIP-AP Ltd
is building the Dugarajapatnam shipbuilding cluster.
The cluster aims to secure a
share of national shipbuilding capacity by 2047.

secs.t: Schemes and indices — DEH, ODOP and EPI

x: The September 2026 phased rollout merged One District One Product (ODOP) into Districts as Export Hubs and provided Dak Ghar Niryat Kendras for postal exports.
In EPI 2024 (4th edition, released by NITI Aayog in Jan 2026) Andhra Pradesh ranked 5th among large States, after Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat and Uttar Pradesh.

secs.t: SEZ Act 2005 — provisions, objectives and committees

x: SEZ exports were valued at Rs 14.64 lakh crore, approximately US$173 billion, and accounted for about
of India's exports.
An SEZ is a demarcated enclave under the 2005 Act, while an EOU is a single unit located anywhere under the FTP scheme.
The Baba Kalyani Committee proposed the term “3Es”, meaning
Employment and Economic Enclaves
, for SEZs.

secs.t: SEZs and units of AP → district and type — Number of SEZs

x: Andhra Pradesh had 32 notified SEZs as of July 2023 according to the APPSC figure.
Andhra Pradesh had 19 operational SEZs in the period referred to by the APPSC-GS 2018 key.

secs.t: SEZs and units of AP → district and type — SEZ / unit → district → type

x: Sri City is located in Tirupati district and combines a multi-product SEZ, DTZ, Free Trade Warehousing Zone and Electronics Manufacturing Cluster.
Kakinada SEZ is a port-based multi-product SEZ with the GMR Kakinada Gateway Port.
Jawaharlal Nehru Pharma City is located at Parawada in the Anakapalli, or Vizag, region.
Divi's Laboratories is a pharmaceutical unit in the Visakhapatnam region (with Parawada Pharma City).

secs.t: SEZs and units of AP → district and type — Administration and industrial parks

x: Authority:
AP's SEZs under
Visakhapatnam SEZ Development Authority.
Nodal agency (2024-25):
APIIC for industrial parks + SEZs.
parks = 264 APIIC + 283 UDL + 24 non-APIIC.
Exam angle: "SEZ unit → product/location" matching and "how many notified/operational SEZs".

secs.t: Export infrastructure → location

x: New dry ports are generally not allowed within 200 km of a seaport or within 100 km of an Inland Container Depot.
Andhra Pradesh is classified as a
Blue-zone State
and receives relaxation for trade hubs that lack logistics.
The Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor (VCIC) is India's first coastal industrial corridor and is part of the East Coast Economic Corridor (ECEC).

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Sri City dry port proposal is associated with
on-site customs clearance
After bifurcation, Andhra Pradesh lost Hyderabad's industrial clusters and responded by pursuing port-led development.
The 50% US tariff was reported to have affected Andhra Pradesh's shrimp sector and aqua exports.
The first English factory in coastal Andhra was at
Machilipatnam

rows.title: Services sector geography - tourism (India and AP circuits), IT, banking; salient features
sub: Group-II S2-44: Tourism in India - types, major circuits and heritage sites
Group-II S2-45: Tourism in Andhra Pradesh - religious, coastal, eco and heritage tourism sites

secs.t: Services, IT and banking — data and places

x: STPI units and Global Capability Centres
are spreading IT activity to Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities.

Google's AI data centre is planned at Visakhapatnam and Anakapalli with an investment of US$15 billion (about Rs 87,520 crore), is described as its largest AI hub outside the US, and had its groundbreaking in April 2026.

secs.t: Tourism data — India and AP arrivals, earnings, ranks

x: India was ranked the eighth-largest tourism economy, valued at approximately US$231.6 billion.
Foreign tourist arrivals rose from 1.70 lakh to
2.72 lakh
, representing approximately 49% growth.
Total tourist arrivals rose from 28.58 crore in 2023–24 to 36.42 crore in 2025–26.
Andhra Pradesh was the
third
most visited State for domestic tourism in the cited period.

secs.t: Tourism and heritage schemes, Acts and bodies → year and features — Scheme → year → key facts

x: Exam angle: PRASHAD = pilgrimage destinations; Swadesh Darshan = thematic circuits (the swap is a common trap, Jul 2026).
NIDHI stands for
National Integrated Database of Hospitality Industry
and is a technology-driven database of hospitality and accommodation units maintained by the Ministry of Tourism.
PRASHAD expands to
Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual, Heritage Augmentation Drive
The Andhra Pradesh destinations identified in connection with PRASHAD are
Tirupati, Srisailam, Simhachalam and Annavaram

secs.t: Tourism and heritage schemes, Acts and bodies → year and features — Campaigns and initiatives → year

x: The e-Visa facility with ETA began in 2014; eleven ports were added in August 2026, increasing checkpoints from 77 to 88.
Gajendra Singh Shekhawat
was the Union Minister for Tourism associated with the revamped Incredible India Digital Platform.
ASI conserves 3,688 centrally protected monuments, including 28 World Heritage properties, under the stated legal framework.

secs.t: AP Tourism Policy 2024-29 — hubs, circuits, bodies and funding

x: The policy plans more than 25 thematic circuits: Buddhist, temple, beach, river-cruise, eco-tourism, sea-cruise and seaplane circuits.
The policy grants industry status and offers up to 25% fixed capital subsidy, industrial power tariff and 100% net SGST reimbursement.
Rs 206.77 crore = Rs 127.40 crore under Swadesh Darshan 2.0 + Rs 79.37 crore under PRASHAD.

secs.t: Tourism formats → place

x: Gujarat's submarine tourism project, off Dwarka, is being developed with
Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited

Andhra Pradesh's draft MICE policy identifies Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada as hubs; its plans include two sea-cruise, four river-cruise and one seaplane circuit, while Travel for LiFE promotes eco-responsible travel.
MICE tourism is characterised as high-yield, low-volume tourism and includes meetings, incentives, conferences and exhibitions.

secs.t: UNESCO World Heritage Sites → state and year

x: Exam angle: count, latest site and its state, and cultural/natural/mixed split.
The correct sequence is 2021, 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026: Ramappa Temple and Dholavira; Santiniketan and the Hoysalas; Moidams; Maratha Military Landscapes; and Sarnath.
The Ministry of Culture coordinates nominations, the ASI is the nodal agency, ICOMOS is the relevant NGO, and India served on the World Heritage Committee during 2021–2025.

secs.t: Geo-heritage and fossil sites → state

x: Exam angle: match-the-following of site to state.
Geological heritage sites are declared and maintained by the
Geological Survey of India
, which functions under the Ministry of Mines and has its headquarters at Kolkata.
Erra Matti Dibbalu consists of red sand dunes at Bheemunipatnam near Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh.
GSI declared Belum Caves (Nandyal, AP) a geo-heritage site in 2025.

secs.t: Hill stations, beaches, pilgrimage centres and landmarks of India → state

x: Munnar is in Kerala, Mount Abu in Rajasthan, Bodh Gaya in Bihar, and Sarnath and Kushinagar in Uttar Pradesh.
The Statue of Unity at Kevadia (Ekta Nagar), Gujarat, is dedicated to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, is 182 m tall, stands between the Satpura and Vindhya ranges, and was sculpted by Ram V. Sutar.

secs.t: AP temples → deity, district, hill and river

x: Tirumala is in the Seshachalam hills; Srisailam is in the Nallamala hills on the Krishna; Kanaka Durga is on Indrakeeladri on the Krishna; and Annavaram is on Ratnagiri hill near the Pampa.
Simhachalam is dedicated to Varaha Lakshmi Narasimha, has 96 black-stone pillars, and its idol is uncovered from sandal paste during Chandanotsavam.

secs.t: AP beaches → nearest town; Blue Flag

x: Exam angle: beach → nearest town matching.
Vodarevu Beach is in Bapatla district, lies near Suryalanka and is linked to Piduguralla by NH-167A.
Kotha Koduru, Ramatheertham and Mypadu beaches are associated with
SPSR Nellore
district.
Shivrajpur in Gujarat
is cited as an Indian Blue Flag beach outside Andhra Pradesh.
The amended policy permits temporary, eco-friendly beach shacks in CRZ-III and CRZ-IV areas.

secs.t: AP caves, waterfalls, hills, forts and crafts → district — Natural sites → district

x: Borra Caves were found in 1807 by
William King George
, as recorded in the Geological Survey of India account.
Thimmamma Marrimanu in Sri Sathya Sai district is recognised for having the world's largest banyan canopy.
Polavaram district, with headquarters at Rampachodavaram, and Markapuram district were formed on 31 December 2025, taking the total to 28 districts.

secs.t: AP caves, waterfalls, hills, forts and crafts → district — Forts and monuments → district

x: Kondapalli toys are associated with NTR district and are made from soft Tella Poniki wood.
Gandikota fort stands on the Penna (Pennar) gorge in YSR Kadapa district and is one of the seven anchor hubs (heritage, adventure).
Lepakshi (Sri Sathya Sai district) has the hanging pillar, India's largest monolithic Nandi and Vijayanagara murals.

secs.t: AP caves, waterfalls, hills, forts and crafts → district — Projects and proposed circuits

x: Proposed circuit:
CM proposed
Gandikota-Horsley Hills-Talakona
in the Tirupati region plan (Jul 2026)
Araku-Lambasingi-Borra Caves project:
₹29.88 crore (approved 5 Mar 2024)
Lepakshi:
₹103.05 crore proposal.
Caravan parks proposed:
Araku, Chintapalli, Maredumilli.

secs.t: Tourism FIRSTs, largest, longest and only → place

r: Asia's largest maritime heritage museum (to be)
Only hill station in the Aravallis

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Andhra Pradesh has sought reclassification of Visakhapatnam Beach Road from
CRZ-3 to CRZ-2
so that tourism projects can proceed.
Andhra Pradesh has a 1,053 km coastline, five beach circuits are identified, and tourism has been accorded industry status in the State.
Polavaram and Markapuram
are identified as new districts whose creation affects older district-based answers.

rows.title: Energy resources - coal, petroleum, natural gas, hydel, nuclear and renewable; distribution in India and AP
sub: Group-II S2-31: Energy resources of India - coal, petroleum, natural gas, hydel, nuclear, renewable

secs.t: Energy sources — definitions and types

x: Exam angle: "which is not a fossil fuel / which is renewable" one-liners.
Solar and wind
are identified as energy-transition sources because they support the shift towards cleaner, non-fossil energy.
Natural gas
is a finite, non-renewable fossil fuel.
Fossil fuels account for approximately 75% of global greenhouse-gas emissions and about 90% of global carbon-dioxide emissions.

secs.t: Energy data — capacity, shares, potential and targets — Installed capacity and non-fossil share

x: India’s installed-capacity mix has crossed the 54% non-fossil level, while coal continues to dominate primary energy and electricity generation.
The non-fossil share crossed the earlier 50% target at
in December 2025, ahead of the 2030 schedule.
Pumped storage stores surplus daytime electricity, particularly solar power, and releases it during night-time peak demand.

secs.t: Energy data — capacity, shares, potential and targets — Potential

x: The Brahmaputra, Indus and Ganga basins possess most of India’s hydroelectric potential because Himalayan rivers have perennial snow-fed flow and steep gradients.
Off-stream closed-loop pumped storage projects no longer require concurrence from the Central Electricity Authority.
Arunachal Pradesh
, in the Brahmaputra basin with perennial snow-fed rivers and steep gradients, has the highest hydel potential.

secs.t: Coal — grades, types and coalfields → state — Grade → carbon → occurrence

x: Peat contains less than 40% carbon, lignite about 40–50%, bituminous coal 40–80%, and anthracite 80–95%.
Jharia is in Jharkhand, Talcher in Odisha, Makum in Assam and Singareni in Telangana.
NLC India
operates the Neyveli lignite mines in Tamil Nadu.
Tertiary coal is approximately
15–60 million years old
and is associated with lignite.

secs.t: Coal — grades, types and coalfields → state — Mining methods → meaning

x: Rat-hole mining involves very narrow pits, sometimes extending up to 400 feet, dug with primitive tools by small, often family-run groups.
Opencast, or surface, mining is the main method of coal extraction in India.
Andhra Pradesh does not possess a Gondwana coalfield of the scale of Singareni and would draw on Singareni coal supplies.

secs.t: Oilfields, refineries and reserves → state — Oil history

x: The Barmer basin in
Rajasthan
is an important onshore oil-producing region containing the Mangala, Bhagyam and Aishwariya fields.
Assam contains Digboi and Naharkatiya, Gujarat contains the Cambay Basin fields, and the KG Basin extends across offshore and onshore areas of Andhra Pradesh.
The first oil well was drilled at Makum near Digboi, Assam, in 1866-67; the commercial industry began at Digboi in 1889.

secs.t: Oilfields, refineries and reserves → state — Refineries → state → operator

x: Digboi refinery in Assam is operated by IOCL.
Guwahati is the first public-sector refinery, Numaligarh is operated by NRL, Jamnagar is the largest refining complex and Visakhapatnam is operated by HPCL.
The Reliance refinery complex at
Jamnagar
in Gujarat is the world’s largest single-site refinery.
The Barmer refinery at Pachpadra is owned by the HPCL–Rajasthan joint venture.

secs.t: Oilfields, refineries and reserves → state — Strategic reserves and gas grid → location

x: The three strategic petroleum reserve locations together have a capacity of 5.33 million metric tonnes.
Phase-II strategic petroleum reserve development is identified at
Chandikhol and Padur
The Pradhan Mantri Urja Ganga pipeline is identified by the
Jagdishpur–Haldia–Bokaro–Dhamra
route.
The Strategic Petroleum Reserves are located at
Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru and Padur
in Karnataka.

secs.t: Power stations → district and state

x: Vindhyachal
thermal power station, located in Singrauli district of Madhya Pradesh, is identified as India’s largest thermal station.
Srisailam hydel project is located on the Krishna River at the Andhra Pradesh–Telangana border, not on the Godavari.
Simhadri is a coal thermal station at Visakhapatnam (Anakapalli) using seawater.
Coal plants generally operate at a 60–85% plant load factor, can run continuously and consume substantial industrial water.

secs.t: Nuclear plants → district; three-stage programme and fuels — Reactor → district, state

x: Kudankulam is located in Tirunelveli district of Tamil Nadu and uses Russian VVER-1000 reactors.
Tarapur, located in Palghar district of Maharashtra, was commissioned in 1969 and was India’s first commercial nuclear power plant, using US BWRs.
The PFBR at Kalpakkam reached first criticality on
6 April 2026
Nuclear 85–90%, solar 20–25% and wind 25–35%.

secs.t: Nuclear plants → district; three-stage programme and fuels — Three-stage programme (Bhabha, 1954)

x: Stage I = PHWRs on natural uranium with heavy-water moderator; Stage II = fast breeders burning Stage-I plutonium and breeding more fuel than they consume.
India’s thorium reserves are the world’s third largest and are estimated at about 3.6 lakh tonnes.
Tummalapalle uranium is in YSR Kadapa district, AP.

secs.t: Renewable energy — parks and leading states

x: Bhadla Solar Park is located near Jodhpur in Rajasthan and has a capacity of 2,245 MW.
Green hydrogen is produced by electrolysis powered by renewable energy.
India's first hydrogen train began operation on the
Jind–Sonipat
route in July 2026.
Gujarat
leads in rooftop solar under the PM Surya Ghar programme.

secs.t: Acts, missions, schemes and PSUs → year and provision

x: The SHANTI Act, 2025 repeals the Atomic Energy Act, 1962 and the CLNDA, 2010, and permits the admission of private companies.
The Budget provided no basic customs duty on capital goods used for processing critical minerals and nil duty on monazite.
The National Green Hydrogen Mission has an outlay of ₹19,744 crore and targets production of 5 million metric tonnes per year.

secs.t: AP energy → projects, district and data

x: The 1,680 MW Pinnapuram Pumped Storage Project is located in
Kurnool
district.
NP Kunta (the Ananthapuramu Ultra Mega Solar Park) is in Sri Sathya Sai district.
The Polavaram hydel project is planned to have
960 MW
capacity through 12 units of 80 MW each.
Andhra Pradesh plans 7,370 MW of pumped storage capacity and 3,931 MW of battery storage capacity by 2035–36.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Raniganj was associated with the first coal mine in 1774, Digboi with the first oil discovery in 1889, Tarapur with the first nuclear plant in 1969, and Pinnapuram is the later integrated renewable-energy storage project.
About
150 GW
of solar capacity goes offline after sunset, contributing to night-time grid stress.
India imports
about 88%
of its crude oil; the Strait of Hormuz closure (Mar 2026) exposed this dependence despite renewable growth.

rows.title: Patterns and issues in transport and trade - regional imbalance, connectivity gaps, logistics

secs.t: Regional imbalance — rail and road density data

x: Rail density is highest in
Punjab, Haryana and the Ganga plains
; it is lowest in the north-east, Himalayan region and Rajasthan desert.
Andhra Pradesh has 17.64 km of National Highways per lakh population compared with India's 12.09 km, and 53.65 km per 1,000 sq km compared with India's 44.46 km.

secs.t: Schemes and programmes → year, targets and features

x: Exam angle: statement pairs on GatiShakti (year, number of ministries); matching each programme to its mode.
PMGSY, the last-mile rural roads programme, was launched in 2000; it now covers 99.6% of eligible habitations nationally (AP 99.09%).
Bharatmala, launched in 2017, covers
of National Highway corridors and aims to improve freight and passenger efficiency.

secs.t: Corridors and rail links → terminals and location

x: Exam angle: UPSC 2023: none correct (the East-West Corridor is not Dibrugarh-Surat; the Trilateral Highway does not end at Chiang Mai).
The full 2,843 km is operational; the Eastern DFC connects Ludhiana with Sonnagar and the Western DFC connects Dadri with JNPT.
The
Kottavalasa–Kirandul
railway carries Bailadila iron ore to Visakhapatnam port through tunnels in the Eastern Ghats.

secs.t: Ports and trade concentration — data and leaders

x: Sea routes carry approximately
of India's trade by volume.
About
of India's transhipment cargo passes through Colombo or Singapore.
Deendayal Port led with 160.11 MT, followed by Paradip and JNPA in FY 2026.
Krishnapatnam
handled the highest volume among the specified non-major ports, with 41.09 million metric tonnes during April–November 2025.

secs.t: Logistics cost, policy and indices → ranks

x: In LEADS 2025, Tamil Nadu was the top performer among coastal States, Uttar Pradesh among landlocked States, Mizoram among North-Eastern States and Delhi among Union Territories.
The National Logistics Policy complements GatiShakti and focuses on improving logistics processes, regulation, skills and technology.
The policy seeks a single-digit logistics cost and a top-25 position in the Logistics Performance Index by 2030.

secs.t: Transport and environment — factor → effect

x: Rail transport emits approximately 90% less CO2 than road transport and costs about half as much.
Rail currently carries about 27% of freight, while the National Rail Plan targets a
share by 2030.
Indian Railways aims to become net zero by 2030.
20 new National Waterways are proposed in 5 years.

secs.t: World railways — rank, density and transcontinental lines

x: Exam angle: APPSC G1 2024 asked for the Trans-Siberian's end points:
Moscow to Vladivostok
Canadian Pacific links Halifax and Vancouver, Union Pacific links New York and San Francisco, Orient Express links Paris and Istanbul, and Trans-Andean links Buenos Aires and Valparaiso.
The
Trans-Australian Railway
between Sydney and Perth crosses the Nullarbor Plain, which has the world's longest straight track of about 478 km.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The logistics-cost estimate of 7.97% is debated in comparison with the older 13–14% figure.
The
Sonnagar–Dankuni
PPP is identified as a failed project.
The four greenfield ports in Andhra Pradesh are expected to add 145 million tonnes per annum of capacity by 2030.
